### D-24300 — Mastermind Tactic onFight execution framework + Doc Ock "Octet of Valence Electrons" (Active — WP-497 / EC-532; landed 2026-08-05)

> **Status: Active. Landed 2026-08-05** (WP-497 / EC-532, commit `EC-532:`; game-engine 2337 pass / 0 fail; sentinel `finalStateHash` + `PRE_WP080_HASH` byte-identical — no re-pin, as predicted; `sim:runtime-observed:check` current; `pnpm -r build` 0). Reserved in `NUMBER-LEDGER.md`.

**Context.** Defeating a Mastermind tactic fires **none** of the tactic's printed **Fight:** ability. `defeatMastermindTacticCore` (`moves/fightMastermind.ts`) moves the tactic to the victory pile, rescues bystanders, and (on the final tactic) sets the endgame counter — but runs no tactic text. The `// tactic text effects are WP-024` comment there is **stale/misleading**: WP-024 implemented scheme + mastermind **strike** execution; tactic **Fight** effects were explicitly scoped **out** of WP-316, WP-386, and WP-388, and no shipped WP owns them. Surfaced live 2026-08-04 (co-op match `KdHnMXaOPin`: all four Doctor Octopus tactics — Octal Octyls, Octet of Valence Electrons, High Octane, Absolute Octarchy — defeated, zero effect).

**Decision.**
- **Per-tactic onFight dispatch (per-mastermind pattern, operator ruling 2026-08-04).** `defeatMastermindTacticCore` gains a final step: `dispatchTacticOnFight(G, ctx, defeatedTacticId)` in a new `rules/tacticHandlers.ts` (sibling to `rules/mastermindHandlers.ts`), branching on the defeated tactic ext_id (`${setAbbr}-mastermind-${slug}-${tacticSlug}`, e.g. `co2e-mastermind-doctor-octopus-octet-of-valence-electrons`). This mirrors the WP-386/388 per-mastermind strike-resolver dispatcher — **NOT** a data-driven marker vocabulary (extract a shared vocabulary later, once ≥3 tactics reveal common primitives — the repo's "abstract on the third copy" rule). Unknown/unimplemented tactic id → **silent no-op** (moves never throw); every non-Octet tactic stays exactly as inert as today, so the change is strictly additive. The dispatch fires on `ctx.currentPlayer`, after the tactic + bystanders are awarded and after the all-tactics-defeated block, on every tactic defeat (each tactic's Fight resolves when that tactic is defeated).
- **First resolver — "Octet of Valence Electrons" via an optional lazily-created hashed per-player hand-size override.** The tactic reads "When you draw a new hand this turn, draw 8 cards instead of 6." This engine has **no end-of-turn cleanup draw** — the hand fills once per turn at the play-phase `onBegin` (`game.ts`). So the tabletop "new hand this turn" ≡ the defeating player's **next `onBegin` fill**, and the override must be **per-player** (recorded on defeat during the player's `main` stage, surviving intervening opponents' turns until that player's next fill). New field `handSizeOverrides?: Record<string, number>` on `LegendaryGameState`. The Octet resolver sets `G.handSizeOverrides[currentPlayer] = OCTET_HAND_SIZE (8)`; the `onBegin` fill computes `target = G.handSizeOverrides?.[current] ?? HAND_SIZE` and **deletes** the consumed entry (no persistence beyond one fill).
- **Determinism — lazy-create avoids a re-pin.** The override is gameplay-affecting, so it **must** live in the hashed `G` (not excluded like `lastPlayEffectsFired`). But following that same hygiene pattern it is **not** seeded in `buildInitialGameState` — the key exists only after an Octet tactic is actually defeated. Consequence: the empty-registry `PRE_WP080` replay and the `core/dr-doom` recorded sentinel fixture never create the key (neither defeats a Doc Ock Octet), so both hash oracles are byte-unchanged and **no re-pin is expected**. Only a real Octet-defeat game gains the field — and that game's hash *should* differ. Verify both oracles at execution; STOP on any drift, never blind-re-pin (`reference_hashed_g_field_dual_repin`).
- **No Magneto composition concern.** `MAGNETO_HAND_SIZE_LIMIT` applies only when Magneto is the mastermind (a post-draw `onTurnStart` trim); Octet only when Doctor Octopus is. One mastermind per match → the two never co-occur. No RNG in the Octet path.

**Scope refinement (arc).** This is the foundational WP of the Mastermind-Tactic-Fight arc. Out of scope / follow-on WPs (each hard-dep on WP-497): the other three Doc Ock tactics — Octal Octyls (look at top 8 of your deck, draw 1, discard rest), High Octane (reveal top 8 of Hero Deck, gain one costing 8, shuffle rest — needs `ctx.random.*`), Absolute Octarchy (each other player reveals a cost-8 card or gains a Wound) — plus every other mastermind's tactics, a marker-vocabulary refactor, and richer narration.

**Consequences.** Additive contract change (one new optional hashed `G` field + a new `rules/tacticHandlers.ts` dispatcher). No new zone, `RuleEffect`, move, phase, or code category (same "rule handler" family as `mastermindHandlers.ts`). Reserved by WP-497; hard-deps WP-019 (tactics MVP) + WP-024 (strike-dispatch precedent) + WP-386/D-24188 + WP-388/D-24192 (per-mastermind resolver pattern) + WP-236 (`onBegin` `HAND_SIZE` draw).

### D-24302 — Join-by-reference (match ID or invite link) lobby contract (Active — WP-499 / EC-534; landed 2026-08-04)

> **Status: Active. Landed 2026-08-04** (WP-499 / EC-534; arena-client 1174/0, no re-pin).

**Context.** The lobby has two ways to join a match: click **Join** on a row in the auto-fetched public list (`GET /games/legendary-arena?isGameover=false`), or open a WP-369 copy-join-link (`?route=lobby&match=<id>`) that merely *highlights* a row already in that list. There is no way to type/paste a match ID or link to join directly, so an **unlisted** match — or one not in the fetched list — is unreachable without the exact deep link. Surfaced 2026-08-04 when an operator tried to play with a newly-registered friend: the by-`@handle` invite path errored (root cause: the handle-claim feature was never wired — `claimHandle` has zero non-test call sites), and the only working path was emailing the copy-link.

**Decision.**
- **Parse a reference to a match ID.** A pure `parseMatchReference(raw): string | null` (`apps/arena-client/src/lobby/matchReference.ts`, no I/O, no boardgame.io import) accepts either a raw boardgame.io match ID or a full invite-link URL: trim; empty → `null`; if it contains `?`, read the `match` query param (present, non-empty → the id; absent → `null`, a malformed link); else if it matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$`, the trimmed string is the id; else `null`.
- **Resolve via a read-only single-match fetch.** `lobbyApi.fetchMatch(matchID): Promise<LobbyMatchSummary | null>` does `GET /games/legendary-arena/:id` (public, like `listMatches`; no Authorization header) — **404 → `null`** (unknown match, rendered as inline copy, not an exception), other non-2xx → throw a full-sentence error, 200 → the existing `LobbyMatchSummary` mapping. Using the per-match GET (not the filtered list) is what makes **unlisted** matches joinable by ID.
- **Join reuses the existing path.** `joinByReference()` parses → fetches → selects the **first open seat** (existing `isOpenSeat`; a `gameover` or full match → inline error, no join) → delegates to the existing `joinExisting(matchID, seatId)`, which owns the playerName guard, the Bearer token, `POST /api/match/join`, and the navigation. No new endpoint, credential path, or navigation code.
- **Trust model unchanged.** A match is joinable by anyone holding its ID — exactly as it already is by anyone holding the WP-369 shareable link. This adds a manual-entry path to an existing capability; it introduces **no new exposure** and no identity/friendship requirement (it is deliberately identity-agnostic, sidestepping the broken by-`@handle` invite).

**Consequences.** App-layer only (`apps/arena-client`): one new pure parser + one read-only `lobbyApi` helper + a lobby input/handler. No server/engine/registry/data change, no new HTTP endpoint, no contract file. Zero determinism/persistence surface (no `G`/RNG/replay/hash). The handle-claim fix (auto-assigning handles so by-`@handle` invites work) is a separate Track-2 follow-up WP, not this one. Reserved by WP-499; hard-deps WP-307/D-24092 (authenticated match-gate join) + WP-369 (copy-join-link `?match=<id>` deep link).

### D-24301 — `return-on-discard` reactive hero ability + forced-discard chokepoint (Active 2026-08-05 — WP-498 / EC-533)

**Decision.** Cyclops "Unending Energy" (`core/cyclops/unending-energy`) — *"If a card effect makes you discard this card, you may return this card to your hand."* — is implemented as the engine's **first reactive (non-play-initiated) hero ability**, via a new `return-on-discard` `HeroKeyword` (bare marker `[keyword:return-on-discard]`, `HERO_KEYWORDS` 33→34) + the first reactive `HeroAbilityTiming` `onDiscard` (`HERO_ABILITY_TIMINGS` 5→6). The keyword is a REACTIVE marker, not an onPlay-family effect.

**The chokepoint.** All card-effect hand→discard sources route through a single new helper `discardFromHand(G, playerID, cardId): boolean` (`moves/discardFromHand.ts`), which moves the card hand→discard and then fires the G-only `checkReturnOnDiscard` reaction. **Execution amendment (2026-08-05):** the EC drafted the chokepoint into `zoneOps.ts`, but `zoneOps.ts`'s module contract is "pure array helpers that never mutate their inputs" — a G-mutating, reaction-parking chokepoint violates it — so it landed in a dedicated `moves/discardFromHand.ts` (the engine move layer, exactly as this D-entry's draft text specified). A cheat-proof drift-guard test (`discardFromHand.test.ts`) asserts no other hand→discard zoneOps idiom (`moveCardFromZone`/`moveAllCards` from `.hand` to `.discard`) exists outside the chokepoint, allowlisting only `discardFromHand.ts` and the end-of-turn CLEANUP discard in `coreMoves.impl.ts` (cleanup is turn structure, not "a card effect", so it must NOT trigger the return — WP §Out of Scope). The negative assertion injects each of the four routed idioms.

**The closed set is SIX sites, not five (execution amendment).** The draft enumerated five card-effect hand→discard sites (`resolveDiscardToPlay`, `discardChoice.resolve`, `mastermindHandlers.discardCardFromHand`, `schemeTwistResolvers.discardHand`, `dodgeCard`). Execution (and the drift-guard) surfaced a sixth the surface study missed: `rules/ruleRuntime.effects.ts` `applyDiscardHand` (the generic `discardHand` rule effect). All six now route through `discardFromHand`.

**The reaction.** `checkReturnOnDiscard` (G-only, no `ctx`) scans `getHooksForCard` for the `return-on-discard` keyword (the reaction keys on the KEYWORD; `onDiscard` is a declarative-only timing with no dispatch in the onPlay executor loop). If present, it parks an OPTIONAL `PendingReturnOnDiscard { playerID, cardId }` on lazy-init `G.pendingReturnOnDiscard` (FIFO). Resolution is `resolveReturnOnDiscard` (`client: false`, args `{ decline: true } | { cardId }`, the `resolveOptionalPutBottomHQ` decline template): accept moves the card discard→hand, decline pops (card stays in discard). Block-all guards on every action-move cluster + `game.ts advanceStage`; `ai.legalMoves` forced-resolve defaults to accept (strictly beneficial); chooser-only `UIPendingReturnOnDiscard` projection + `ReturnOnDiscardPrompt.vue`.

**Executor-visit enrollment (load-bearing, copilot-caught at draft).** `executeHeroEffects`/`getHooksForCard` is NOT timing-filtered, so the executor VISITS the `return-on-discard` hook whenever Unending Energy is *played*. Without enrolling the keyword in a `DISCARD_TIME_EXECUTED_KEYWORDS` set folded into `MVP_KEYWORDS` (`hero/heroEffects.execute.ts`), that visit would emit a spurious `no-handler` hollow breadcrumb every play and redden `ledger:heroes:check` — the same allowlist pattern `dodge`/`undercover`/`size-changing` use. `NO_MAGNITUDE_KEYWORDS` is NOT needed (the classifier keys only on `MVP_KEYWORDS`). Parser: `'return-on-discard': 'onDiscard'` in `KEYWORD_TIMING_DEFAULTS`.

**Broad reading LOCKED.** "A card effect makes you discard" is read broadly: the `discard-to-play` COST (the operator's cited Determination/Optic Blast example) and the voluntary Dodge discard both COUNT; normal end-of-turn cleanup does NOT (it never routes through the six sites).

**Determinism — no re-pin (confirmed empirically).** `G.pendingReturnOnDiscard` is hashed but lazy-init (never in `Game.setup`), so canonical JSON omits it from the empty-replay final state → `PRE_WP080_HASH` + `hashGameState` byte-unchanged. The `core/dr-doom` sentinel fixture `finalStateHash` is byte-unchanged (no fixture plays+returns Unending Energy) — all 163 hash/fixture/sentinel tests pass. Only `core/cyclops/unending-energy` is marked; the co2e twin stays unmarked (deferred, the WP-494 precedent). Move count 25→26 (`resolveReturnOnDiscard`, not a `CORE_MOVE_NAME`).

Reserved by WP-498; hard-deps WP-383/D-24184 (discard-to-play site + keyword substrate) + D-24139 (return-zero-cost-discard pending precedent) + WP-248/D-24019 (optional-decline pending template) + WP-476/D-24284 (mastermind reveal-or-discard site) + D-24266 (unmarked-ability breadcrumb).

### D-24303 — Auto-assigned changeable handles + WP-101 mutual-presence invariant amendment (Active — WP-500 / EC-535; landed 2026-08-05)

> **Status: Active. Landed 2026-08-05** (WP-500 / EC-535; server suite exit 0, `assignAutoHandle` DB-gated + backfill verified against local Postgres, no re-pin).

**Context.** WP-101 built the account handle (`handle_canonical` / `display_handle` / `handle_locked_at`, `HANDLE_REGEX = ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,23}$`, `RESERVED_HANDLES`) but the claim path was **never wired**: `claimHandle` — the sole writer — has zero non-test callers, no HTTP endpoint, and no profile field. So `handle_canonical` is **NULL for every account**, and every `@handle` affordance (friend-request WP-351; match-invite WP-358/366, both via `findAccountByHandle`) returns `handle_not_found` for every target. Surfaced when an operator tried to invite a newly-registered friend by username (2026-08-04); the diagnosis + the identity-agnostic workaround shipped under WP-499 / D-24302, and this decision is the root-cause fix.

**Decision.**
- **Auto-assign a changeable handle at first-sign-in provisioning.** New pure `deriveHandle(displayName): string` slugs the display name to a `HANDLE_REGEX`-valid handle (trim → lowercase → `[^a-z0-9]`-runs → `_` → collapse/trim `_` → ensure a leading letter + length 3..24 → empty/reserved/underivable ⇒ `player`). New `assignAutoHandle(accountId, displayName, db)` sets `handle_canonical` = `display_handle` = the derived slug **and leaves `handle_locked_at` NULL**, idempotently (`UPDATE … WHERE ext_id = $ AND handle_canonical IS NULL`). It is wired into `attemptProvisioning` (`accountResolver.logic.ts`) after `provisionPlayerAccount`, inside an **explicit call-site `try/catch`** that logs and continues — a handle-assign failure never breaks sign-in. (This is *unlike* the D-24079 marketing enqueue, which is fail-open via a dependency-injected fail-safe wrapper with no call-site guard; `assignAutoHandle` is a direct DB call that can reject.) `attemptProvisioning` is the resolver's **no-match branch only**, so this fires **only when provisioning a brand-new account** — existing NULL-handle accounts do NOT self-heal on login and are healed **solely by the one-time backfill** (a required post-deploy step, since the entire current user base is NULL-handle). `assignAutoHandle` does not `throw` (it `return`s `null` or `Promise.reject`s), preserving the `handle.logic.ts` no-`throw` property.
- **Collision strategy.** Candidates `base`, `base2`, `base3`, … (bounded); a partial-unique `23505` on `handle_canonical` (a concurrent account took the candidate) advances the suffix; the final fallback is `base`+short-`ext_id`-hex (guaranteed unique). **The base is truncated to `24 − suffix.length` before any suffix is appended, and each candidate is validated against `HANDLE_REGEX` before the UPDATE** — `handle_canonical` is bare `text` with no length CHECK, so an over-length (25-char) handle would otherwise persist invalid. Auto-assigned handles are intentionally allowed to be "uglier" (a numeric/hex suffix) because they are **changeable** (the follow-up WP adds the change UI).
- **Backfill via the TS functions, not SQL.** A one-time `scripts/backfill-handles.mjs` (run `node --env-file=.env scripts/backfill-handles.mjs`) assigns handles to all pre-existing `handle_canonical IS NULL` rows by calling the **same** `deriveHandle`/`assignAutoHandle` — single source of truth. It imports the server TS via the `scripts/process-stripe-events.mjs` / D-13405 precedent (`createRequire` → `tsx/esm/api` `register()` → `pathToFileURL` dynamic-import of the `.ts` source), because `apps/server` emits no dist. A SQL-migration backfill is rejected: re-deriving the slug rules in SQL would drift from the TS logic. No schema migration is needed (the columns + partial unique index exist since migration 008).
- **Amends the WP-101 mutual-presence invariant.** WP-101 stated the three handle columns are "NULL together or non-NULL together" and that `claimHandle` is their **sole** writer. As of this decision: `handle_canonical` + `display_handle` still move together, but **`handle_locked_at` is independent** — **NULL = auto-assigned (changeable)**, **`now()` = explicitly claimed (immutable)**. `assignAutoHandle` is a sanctioned **second, disjoint** writer that touches only `handle_canonical` + `display_handle` and **never** `handle_locked_at`; `claimHandle` remains the only writer of `handle_locked_at`. The invariant is **prose-enforced**: there is no automated sole-writer/mutual-presence grep-gate or test (migration 008's comment claiming it is "verified by application-layer tests" is stale, and migrations are immutable so it stays), so the amended invariant is documented in the `handle.logic.ts` module header — the executor updates that header in lockstep rather than tripping a gate.

**Consequences.** Server identity only (`apps/server`): two new functions + a fail-open wiring line + a backfill script; no engine/registry/client change, no schema migration, no new HTTP endpoint, zero determinism/persistence-of-`G` surface. Handles remain **presentation/routing aliases** — `AccountId` stays the identity/trust key (FR-2), so auto-assignment does not touch ranked eligibility or the friendship trust key. **Out of scope (paired follow-up WP):** the change-handle/claim **endpoint** + the profile **UI** field, and rewiring `claimHandle`'s `handle_canonical IS NULL` guard to `handle_locked_at IS NULL` so a claim can overwrite an unlocked auto-handle. Reserved by WP-500; hard-deps WP-101 (handle contract) + WP-174 (provisioning) + WP-499/D-24302 (join-by-ID + diagnosis).

Protect this file.

### D-24304 — Engineering Wiki: optional `canonical-source` front-matter for mirror pages — amends the D-13810 field surface (Active 2026-08-05 — INFRA, no WP)

> **Amends** the WP-139 / D-13810 wiki front-matter surface by adding **one
> optional** field. **Does not** touch the six-field metadata-panel render lock
> (D-13810 / EC-142): `canonical-source` is consumed **only** by the
> `editing-this-page.html` partial and is never rendered in the panel, so the
> `single.html` field-surface lock is unaffected.

**Context.** #1225 (INFRA) added an "Editing this page" affordance to every ewiki
page with two variants: **native** ("edit `wiki/<slug>.md`; the Sources list are
files it documents, not an edit target") and **changelog** (generated; "edit
`docs/09-CHANGELOG.md`"). A third archetype had no precise handling: a **mirror
page** — a wiki page whose prose is a synthesis of a single upstream doc that
owns the wording. `development-workflow` is the only clear one today (it restates
`docs/ai/REFERENCE/development-workflow.md`). Mirror pages fell to the native
variant, which wrongly implies the wiki page is the source of truth. Deriving the
owner from `source` is ambiguous — `development-workflow` cites **four** REFERENCE
docs with no marker for which owns the prose.

**Decision.** Introduce an optional, singular `canonical-source` front-matter
field: a repo-root-relative path to the one upstream doc that owns a mirror
page's canonical prose. Present **only** on mirror pages (native pages omit it);
when present, the same file must also be cited in `source`. When set, the
editing-this-page block renders a **mirror variant** directing the editor to edit
the upstream doc, then re-sync the wiki page and bump `last-reviewed`.

1. **Schema** (`wiki/SCHEMA.md`): add the `canonical-source` field-reference row +
   a "Mirror pages" subsection defining the native-vs-mirror test and the
   qualifying rubric (documenting code or citing a data spec does **not**
   qualify). Amended **before** any template reads the field, per the
   `single.html` "amendment first, never a template-side widening" rule.
2. **Template** (`layouts/partials/editing-this-page.html`): a new
   `{{ else if $canonical }}` branch between the `changelog` slug-check and the
   native default. Panel untouched.
3. **Validation** (`apps/wiki-viewer/scripts/check-links.mjs`): when a page has
   `canonical-source`, assert the target file exists **and** its resolved path
   also appears in `source` — a cheap drift guard keeping provenance complete.
4. **Assignment** (SPEC content edit): `development-workflow.md` gains
   `canonical-source: docs/ai/REFERENCE/development-workflow.md` and its now-
   redundant hand-authored "Editing this page" blockquote is removed (the auto
   mirror variant replaces it). No other page qualifies today.

**Consequences.** ewiki tooling only (`apps/wiki-viewer` + `wiki/`): one optional
schema field, one template branch, one validation check, one content edit. Native
pages render byte-identical output. No engine/registry/server/client surface, no
schema migration, no determinism or persistence-of-`G` surface. The mirror rubric
in SCHEMA.md lets future pages self-select; the check-links guard catches a
`canonical-source` that drifts out of `source`.

### D-24305 — Change-handle contract (freely-changeable-while-unlocked; third disjoint handle writer) (Active — WP-501 / EC-536; landed 2026-08-05)

> **Status: Active. Landed 2026-08-05** (WP-501 / EC-536; handle logic+route 28/28, arena-client 1188/0, no migration).

**Context.** WP-500 / D-24303 auto-assigns every account a `@handle` (changeable — `handle_locked_at` NULL) but there is **no way to change it**: `MyProfilePage.vue` only renders `@handle`, and a slug collision leaves a user with e.g. `jeff2` when they wanted `jeff` (the operator's own account, 2026-08-05). This decision locks the change mechanism.

**Decision.**
- **`changeHandle` — freely changeable while unlocked.** New `changeHandle(accountId, requestedHandle, database): Promise<Result<{ handleCanonical: string; displayHandle: string }>>` in `handle.logic.ts`, structured like `claimHandle`: `validateHandleFormat` (→ `invalid_handle` / `reserved_handle`), then `UPDATE legendary.players SET handle_canonical = <canonical>, display_handle = <display> WHERE ext_id = <accountId> AND handle_locked_at IS NULL RETURNING`. A partial-unique `23505` → `handle_taken`; an empty `RETURNING` disambiguates via `findPlayerByAccountId` to `unknown_account` (no row) or `handle_already_locked` (row exists but locked). It **never** `throw`s (returns `Result` / `Promise.reject`). This realizes the D-24303 "auto-assign but changeable" model: a handle can be changed any number of times while `handle_locked_at IS NULL` — which is every account today (no lock feature is wired). The previous handle is **released to the free pool** (no redirect/reservation — standard username-change behavior).
- **Third disjoint writer (extends D-24303).** `changeHandle` is the **third** sanctioned writer of `handle_canonical` + `display_handle` (after `claimHandle` and `assignAutoHandle`) and — like `assignAutoHandle` — **never writes `handle_locked_at`**. Unlike `assignAutoHandle` (which only fills a NULL handle), `changeHandle` *overwrites* an existing unlocked handle. The `handle.logic.ts` writer-invariant header (amended by WP-500) gains a one-line note.
- **No contract-union change.** `changeHandle` reuses the **existing** five `HandleErrorCode` values (including `handle_already_locked` for the defensive locked case), so `handle.types.ts` and its drift test are **not** touched. `changeHandle` returns a small `{ handleCanonical, displayHandle }` rather than `HandleClaim` (whose required-`string` `handleLockedAt` cannot represent an unlocked/NULL handle).
- **Endpoint + UI.** New `PATCH /api/me/handle` (`authenticated-session-required`, body `{ handle }`) in a new `handle.routes.ts` (`registerHandleRoutes`, mirroring `ownerProfile.routes.ts`; identity session-resolved, `Cache-Control: no-store`), registered in `server.mjs`. `ownerProfileApi.changeHandle` wraps it; `MyProfilePage.vue` gains a change-your-handle affordance (input + Change + inline error) near the `@handle` line. `api-endpoints.md` gains the endpoint + `changeHandle` Library-only rows (D-11804).

**Consequences.** Cross-layer (server identity + arena-client owner profile); no schema migration (columns exist since migration 008), no engine touch, zero determinism/persistence-of-`G` surface. Handles stay presentation/routing aliases — `AccountId` remains the identity/trust key (FR-2), so a handle change does not affect ranked eligibility or friendships (a friendship is keyed on `AccountId` and survives a handle change — FR-3). **Out of scope (deferred follow-ups):** the explicit **lock/claim** action (a "make permanent" that sets `handle_locked_at`, which would rewire `claimHandle`'s `handle_canonical IS NULL` guard to `handle_locked_at IS NULL`); a per-account change **rate-limit / cooldown** (anti-squat). Reserved by WP-501; hard-deps WP-101 (handle contract) + WP-500/D-24303 (auto-assign + changeable model) + WP-104 (owner-profile edit surface).

### D-24306 — Match end-of-life controls: player "End Game" (endgame counter) + non-scored `endedEarly` marker + "Play Again" (Active — WP-502 / EC-537; landed 2026-08-05)

**Context.** On match end the play surface rendered only the inline `EndgameSummary` (outcome + reason) with no next step — no way to replay, and no way to close out a match that could not finish (a co-op table that ran out of time). Two controls were requested: an arcade-style **Play Again** (relaunch the same loadout — "insert another quarter" to improve your score) and an **End Game** escape hatch that closes an in-progress match out **for everyone**.

**Decision.**
- **End Game is an endgame COUNTER, not `events.endGame`.** The client-visible `UIState.gameOver` is produced by `buildUIState` from `evaluateEndgame(G.counters)` — it deliberately does **not** read `ctx.gameover` (`uiState.build.ts`, "No ctx.gameover access needed"). A boardgame.io `events.endGame(...)` end would set `ctx.gameover` and terminate the match but **never surface the endgame panel** to any client (a hard-freeze). So End Game latches a new `ENDGAME_CONDITIONS.MATCH_ENDED_EARLY = 'matchEndedEarly'` counter, which `evaluateEndgame` checks **first** (highest priority, above every natural win/loss/tie) and turns into `{ outcome: 'tie', reason: 'The players ended the match early.', endedEarly: true }`. The existing top-level `endIf` then sets `ctx.gameover` for **every** seat, and `buildUIState` projects the endgame panel to all clients. The counter is set by a new server-only `endMatchEarly` move (`{ move, client: false }` per D-10008; never throws; a no-op when the match is already over; NOT a `CORE_MOVE_NAME`).
- **`endedEarly` is an ADDITIVE optional marker; the outcome stays `'tie'`.** `endedEarly?: boolean` rides `EndgameResult` and `UIGameOverState` only. It is deliberately kept OFF the `EndgameOutcome` union so that adding it does not ripple through the union's exhaustive consumers (`CompetitiveOutcome`, migration `026_add_outcome_to_competitive_scores`, the dashboard/coop/campaign/simulation switches). The audience filter passes `gameOver` through by spread (`{ ...uiState.gameOver }`), so no per-field whitelist edit is needed.
- **An early-ended match is NEVER scored.** The server (`submitCompetitiveScoreImpl`) rejects an `endedEarly` reduced gameover with a new `ended_early` `SubmissionRejectionReason` (added to the union AND the `SUBMISSION_REJECTION_REASONS` canonical array in lockstep) **before** any score is computed or written — the authoritative enforcement of the operator's "never score an early end" decision. The arena-client submit-on-gameover hook also skips the POST entirely and sets status `'ineligible'` (permanent, non-error, non-retriable — mirrors the `par_not_published` disposition), so no doomed request is sent.
- **Play Again relaunches SOLO with the same loadout.** On match end the play surface offers Play Again (and Back to Lobby), mounted once at the D-16501 viewport root. Play Again reads the client-stashed `MatchSetupConfig` (`readMatchSetup`), reuses the original seat count (`snapshot.players.length` — the composition is player-count-specific, WP-370), and calls `launchMatchFromComposition` to create+join+navigate into a fresh match at seat 0. Gated on an authenticated account (create requires auth, D-24092) and the stashed loadout; a guest or a non-creator sees only Back to Lobby.

**Consequences.** Cross-layer (Game Engine + Server + Arena Client). **No new top-level `G` field** — the counter is written only at runtime when `endMatchEarly` fires, so initial `G` is unchanged and there is **no `finalStateHash`/`PRE_WP080` re-pin**. Replay-safe and deterministic (a pure counter read + a counter write; no RNG, no I/O, no `G` persistence). End Game is fired only by the active player (boardgame.io gates top-level moves to the current player) — an accepted limitation, since the gameover broadcast still closes the match for everyone. §22 (determinism): No conflict. §20 Funding: N/A. §21 API: no new HTTP endpoint (`ended_early` extends an existing reason union). Reserved by WP-502; landed at WP-502 execution.

### D-24307 — Doctor Octopus (villain) Fight: `override-next-hand-size` primitive writing the WP-497 `handSizeOverrides` field (Active — WP-503 / EC-538; landed 2026-08-05)

**Context.** The core spider-foes **Doctor Octopus** villain (`core/spider-foes/doctor-octopus`, 2 copies) prints *"Fight: When you draw a new hand of cards at the end of this turn, draw eight cards instead of six."* It was unimplemented — a live `no-handler` hollow (2026-08-05, Magneto match `zdcAitTRmIY`, log 17.2.17). This is the **villain-side sibling** of the co2e *mastermind*-tactic Doc Ock "Octet of Valence Electrons" (WP-497 / D-24300): the same "draw 8 next hand" effect and the same shared `G.handSizeOverrides` field, but fired through a **different subsystem** (the villain-effect vocabulary, not the mastermind-tactic dispatcher).

**Decision.**
- **New keyword-less auto-resolve primitive `override-next-hand-size`.** Appended to the `VillainEffectPrimitive` union + `VILLAIN_EFFECT_PRIMITIVES` array at position 14 (append-only per D-24034; the drift test moves 13 → 14). Marker grammar `[effect:override-next-hand-size:<N>]` where `<N>` (Doc Ock: `8`) is the **absolute** next-hand target, carried on the descriptor's existing `magnitude` field. A dedicated parse arm in `setup/villainAbility.setup.ts` (the generic chain has no shared magnitude arm) mirrors `draw-cards-current`'s strict positive-integer grammar; the apply-effect-markers.mjs local primitive validator + grammar are synced in lockstep (the no-import producer/consumer discipline).
- **Handler WRITES the WP-497-owned field.** `villainEffectOverrideNextHandSize` sets `G.handSizeOverrides[currentPlayer] = magnitude` (lazy-init with WP-497's exact idiom — never seeded in `buildInitialGameState`) and self-narrates via `pushLog` (keyword-less → no legacy reverse-map → the generic "Fight effect:" line never fires). It **reuses WP-497's field declaration AND its play-phase `onBegin` consumption verbatim** — this decision adds **no new `G` field** and **no second consumption/clear site**. After WP-503 there is exactly one `handSizeOverrides` declaration (`types.ts`) and one consumption (`game.ts` `onBegin`), with two disjoint writers (the WP-497 tactic resolver + this villain handler).
- **Magneto composition — ORTHOGONAL lifecycles, not a precedence.** Unlike the one-per-match mastermind Doc Ock, the villain Doc Ock can co-occur with any mastermind, including Magneto (it did, in the surfacing match). But the two effects have **no shared merge point**: Doc Ock's override governs only the play-phase `onBegin` fill (consumed + cleared there); Magneto's `MAGNETO_HAND_SIZE_LIMIT` (=4) is a **Master-Strike-time** discard-to-4 reaction that parks a `discard-to-limit` pending choice. WP-497's `onBegin` is Magneto-unaware (`target = handSizeOverrides[player] ?? HAND_SIZE`) — there is no precedence rule to encode. The execution added an independence test (the override survives a real discard-to-limit resolve; the override write never touches the parked choice).
- **Determinism.** No `ctx.random` (Doc Ock reveals/shuffles nothing). Two hashed surfaces *could* move — (a) the marker changes Doc Ock's setup-built `villainAbilityHooks` (a fixture whose villain config **includes** spider-foes shifts its initial-`G` hash even if Doc Ock is never fought); (b) the `handSizeOverrides` **write** shifts state only when a fixture **fights** him. **No committed fixture does either** (sentinel = `core/brotherhood`; `PRE_WP080_HASH` = synthetic group), so both oracles are byte-identical — **no re-pin**, confirmed by the green suite.

**Consequences.** Additive contract change (one new primitive + handler + parser arm + marker; one card flips unmarked → executable in the villain ledger + effect-index with `{ WP-503, D-24307 }` provenance). Single layer (Game Engine + card-data markers); no client change (auto-resolve, no pending choice, no UIState field). No new zone / move / phase / code category. Reserved by WP-503; landed at WP-503 execution. §17 (§1/§2/§10; No conflict; determinism line). §20 N/A. §21 N/A. `User-Visible Surface = play.legendary-arena.com` — **D-24026 live-verify operator-pending** (fight Doc Ock, end the turn, next hand is 8). The co2e / other-set Doc Ock villain twins stay unmarked (deferred, the WP-494 twin precedent).

### D-24308 — Friend request by `@handle` OR `accountId`: `account_not_found`, input-only, FR-2 is output-only (Active — WP-504 / EC-539; landed 2026-08-06)

**Context.** The add-friend endpoint `POST /api/me/friends/requests` resolved a target only by `@handle` (`findAccountByHandle`). The operator asked whether players could be matched "by their handle or their UUID" (ewiki Profile Login, PR #1245). A player's `AccountId`/`ext_id` (a v4 UUID) is a stable, unambiguous identity key already shown to its owner on their own profile — but FR-2 keeps it off every friend/invite/profile **response**, so it is never enumerable. That raised the question of whether accepting it as request **input** breaches FR-2.

**Decision.** The friend-request endpoint accepts **exactly one** of `{ handle }` (unchanged) or `{ accountId }`. The `accountId` path: a pure shape guard `isWellFormedAccountId` (UUID `8-4-4-4-12`, case-insensitive) rejects malformed input as `invalid_request` **without a DB round-trip**; `findPlayerByAccountId` then resolves it, and a well-formed-but-unknown id returns a new `account_not_found` (404) — distinct from `handle_not_found` (handle path) and `invalid_request` (malformed). Supplying both fields or neither → `invalid_request`. The resolved target — by either path — funnels into the **unchanged** WP-355 block/cooldown/rate-limit chain + `sendFriendRequest` (`self_friendship` etc. stay in the logic layer; no new self guard). `account_not_found` is added in lockstep to **five** drift sites: the server `FriendApiErrorCode` union, `FRIEND_API_ERROR_CODES` array, and the route-test's hardcoded `expected` set; and the client mirror + its `expectedServerUnion` copy. The client add-friend input accepts an `@handle` or a pasted Account ID, discriminated by a pure `parsePlayerIdentifier`.

**FR-2 scope clarification (the load-bearing decision).** FR-2 is an **output-redaction** invariant — no friend/invite/block/profile **response** ever emits `accountId`/`ext_id`/`player_id`. Accepting a **self-held** AccountId as request **input** emits no identifier and reveals nothing (the only way to hold another player's AccountId is if they shared their own, out-of-band), so it does **not** breach FR-2. This is the same copy-paste-capability trust model as WP-499/D-24302's join-by-match-ID: reachable only by someone the id was deliberately given to, never by enumeration. FR-2's response redaction is unchanged and asserted by the existing no-`accountId`-on-the-wire test.

**Consequences.** Cross-layer (server friendships + a shared identity guard; arena-client friends API/composable/component); no schema migration, no engine/registry/data touch, zero determinism/persistence-of-`G` surface, no `finalStateHash`/`PRE_WP080` re-pin. `docs/ai/REFERENCE/api-endpoints.md` friend-request row replaced whole (D-11804): request schema gains `accountId`, responses gain `account_not_found`; Status stays `Wired`, Auth stays `authenticated-session-required`. **Out of scope (dropped, not deferred):** match-invite-by-`accountId` (the paired WP-505 was drafted then dropped — invites are friend-gated via `createMatchInvite → not_friends`, so a valid invite target is always already a friend addressable by `@handle`; its reserved numbers were retracted). ### D-24310 — Engineering Wiki: cross-repo `canonical-source` via `canonical-source-repo` — extends D-24304 (Active 2026-08-05 — INFRA, no WP)

> **Extends** D-24304 (optional `canonical-source` for mirror pages) with an
> optional companion field for mirror pages whose canonical doc lives in a
> **different repo**. Does not change same-repo behaviour, and — like D-24304 —
> is consumed only by the `editing-this-page.html` partial, never rendered in
> the metadata panel, so the six-field D-13810 / EC-142 panel surface lock is
> untouched.

**Context.** D-24304 added `canonical-source` for mirror pages, but resolved the
path against **this** repo only (`github.com/barefootbetters/legendary-arena`).
The three homepage pages (`homepage-spec`, `homepage-appendix`,
`homepage-review-template`) mirror docs in the separate marketing repo
(`legendary-arena/legendary-arena-website`), which the same-repo field could not
link — so they kept a hand-authored provenance blockquote as an interim (the
#1250 slim).

**Decision.** Add an optional `canonical-source-repo` front-matter field: a
GitHub `owner/repo` slug. When present, `canonical-source` is a path within
**that** repo, and the footer's mirror variant links
`github.com/<owner/repo>/blob/main/<path>` (and the edit link to `/edit/main/`),
noting the repo inline. When absent, same-repo behaviour is unchanged.

1. **Schema** (`wiki/SCHEMA.md`): add the `canonical-source-repo` field row + a
   "Cross-repo mirrors" paragraph in the Mirror pages subsection.
2. **Template** (`editing-this-page.html`): the mirror variant computes its blob
   and edit bases from `canonical-source-repo` when set; the canonical-doc edit
   step reads "following that repo's commit convention" cross-repo (the marketing
   repo owns its own convention) instead of the same-repo `SPEC:`.
3. **Validation** (`check-links.mjs`): cross-repo, the doc is not checked out
   here, so the existence + source-membership checks cannot apply — the guard
   instead validates only that the slug matches `owner/repo` and the path is
   non-empty. Same-repo checks are unchanged.
4. **Adoption** (content): the three homepage pages set both fields
   (`canonical-source-repo: legendary-arena/legendary-arena-website`) and drop
   their interim provenance blockquote — the footer's mirror variant now links
   the marketing-repo source, the same clean state `development-workflow` is in.

**Consequences.** ewiki tooling only (`apps/wiki-viewer` + `wiki/`): one optional
schema field, one template conditional, one validation branch, three content
migrations. Same-repo mirrors and native pages render unchanged. No
engine/registry/server/client surface, no schema migration, no determinism or
persistence-of-`G` surface. Branch pinning is fixed to `main` (a non-`main`
canonical branch is a future extension if ever needed).

### D-24311 — Captured cards under city villains and the mastermind: `UICityCard.attachedHeroDisplay` + count-only `attachedBystanderCount` (reverses the D-12806 city-villain safe-skip) (Active — WP-505 / EC-540; landed 2026-08-06)

**Context.** Three capture stores are tracked in `G` at runtime but were not displayed on the play board. Villains capture Heroes from the HQ (`G.villainAttachedHeroes`, **face up** — public identity) — projected as `UICityCard.attachedHeroes` (WP-214) but never rendered, and the arena-client has no ext_id→image resolver, so the ext_id array alone cannot draw art. Villains/henchmen capture Bystanders (`G.attachedBystanders`, **face down** — hidden identity) — projected **nowhere**, deliberately excluded by the D-12805 Interpretation-B / D-12806 safe-skip ("do NOT flatten `G.attachedBystanders`"). Masterminds capture Bystanders via Master Strike (`G.mastermind.attachedBystanders`, **face down**, wired by WP-154 / D-15401) — projected, but rendered as a text `<li>` list. WP-214 explicitly deferred "arena-client UI rendering of attached heroes" to a UI WP that was never drafted; this is that work plus the bystander display.

**Decision.**
- **Two additive, public `UICityCard` fields**, both added through the 5-step Board-Visible Field contract (declare on the type → populate in `buildUIState` → pass through `filterUIStateForAudience` `deepCopyCitySpaces` → non-vacuous audience-filter test → Play Diagnostics `uiStateSnapshot`):
  - `attachedHeroDisplay: UICardDisplay[]` — **index-aligned** with `attachedHeroes` (same length/order), each entry `resolveDisplay(heroExtId, gameState)`. Face-up captured heroes are public identity; the client renders them as card art (mirrors the HQ `slots`/`slotDisplay` parallel-array pattern).
  - `attachedBystanderCount: number` = `G.attachedBystanders[space]?.length ?? 0` — **count only**. This **reverses the D-12806 safe-skip for the count only**: captured bystanders are face down, so the projection carries the count (rendered as an "N captured" badge) and **never** the ext_ids or display — a face-down identity must not leak.
- **The D-12805 Interpretation-B prohibition is preserved:** city-villain bystanders (`G.attachedBystanders`) are still **never** flattened onto the mastermind tile. They render on the **city** card (`attachedBystanderCount`); the mastermind's own captures (`G.mastermind.attachedBystanders`) render separately. The two capture stores stay distinct.
- **Both fields are `required` (not optional).** A city tile always has a (possibly-empty) capture state, so the field is always present. arena-client `vue-tsc` is the only compile-time enforcer of the required-field backfill (game-engine `.test.ts` are `tsc`-excluded and `tsx`-type-stripped); the game-engine guard is the runtime `Object.keys` assertion in `uiState.types.drift.test.ts`, updated to the full 8-key set (which also repaired a stale WP-214 omission).
- **Client render:** `CityRow.vue` renders `attachedHeroDisplay` as face-up `CardTile` art plus a count-only "N captured" badge, outside the fight button; `MastermindTile.vue` swaps its `<li>` list for the same badge (no engine change on the mastermind side — the projection already existed).

**Consequences.** Additive UIState contract change (two new public `UICityCard` fields); no new zone / move / phase / persisted state. Determinism untouched — the projection is observability-only, excluded from the state hash (no re-pin). Cross-layer (game-engine projection + arena-client render), boundary respected: the engine adds read-only projections, the client consumes them. §17 (product legibility; No conflict; NG-1..7 not crossed). §20 N/A. §21 N/A. `User-Visible Surface = play.legendary-arena.com` — **D-24026 live-verify operator-pending** (a captured hero shows as art, captured bystanders show as a count badge under the holding villain/mastermind). Reserved by WP-505; landed at WP-505 execution.

### D-24312 — Core Magneto "Crushing Shockwave" tactic Fight: `resolveCrushingShockwave` no-choice per-player reveal-or-two-Wounds (Active — WP-506 / EC-541; landed 2026-08-07)

**Context.** Defeating core Magneto's **"Crushing Shockwave"** tactic fired **none** of its printed *"Fight: Each other player reveals an [team:x-men] Hero or gains two Wounds."* The tactic-onFight dispatch framework (WP-497 / D-24300) is in place and fires on every tactic defeat, but ships a single resolver — co2e Doctor Octopus's "Octet of Valence Electrons" — so every other tactic ext_id, including all four core Magneto tactics, falls through `dispatchTacticOnFight` to the silent no-op. Surfaced live 2026-08-06 in a core Magneto co-op match (tactics defeated at zero effect). This is the **second** resolver in the mastermind-tactic-Fight arc.

**Decision.**
- **New `resolveCrushingShockwave(G, currentPlayer)` in `rules/tacticHandlers.ts`** + a `dispatchTacticOnFight` branch keyed by the tactic ext_id `core-mastermind-magneto-crushing-shockwave` (grammar `${setAbbr}-mastermind-${slug}-${tacticSlug}`, card slug `crushing-shockwave` in `data/cards/core.json`). For each player id in `Object.keys(G.playerZones).sort()` **except `currentPlayer`**: a player holding a card with `G.cardTraits?.[extId]?.team === 'x-men'` **reveals** it (a no-op mutation, only a log line); every other player **gains up to two Wounds** from the supply.
- **No-choice deterministic auto-resolve, no pending-choice.** For "reveal X or penalty" the player-optimal choice is invariant — a free reveal beats two Wounds — so auto-revealing when able is fully faithful and avoids a blocking multi-player pending-choice, per the **D-24192 / D-24284** mastermind-strike precedent. Three deltas from the sibling `resolveCo2eMagnetoStrike` ("each player discards an X-Men Hero or gains a Wound"): **reveal not discard** (an X-Men holder loses nothing), **two Wounds not one**, and **each OTHER player** (skip the defeating `ctx.currentPlayer` — a tactic Fight is the defeating player's reward against the others, unlike a Master Strike, which hits every player).
- **Inlined, not exported.** The X-Men-in-hand scan (`handHasXMenHero`) is a local explicit hand scan against `G.cardTraits`; the wound gain calls `board/wounds.logic.ts` `gainWound` directly. Per the "duplicate first, abstract only when a third copy appears" rule, `mastermindHandlers.ts`'s `playerHasXMenHeroInHand` / `gainWoundToDiscard` are **not** exported and `mastermindHandlers.ts` is untouched — the change stays inside `tacticHandlers.ts` + its test. The two `gainWound` calls **thread** (assign both returned arrays back between calls) because `gainWound` is non-mutating; a supply shortfall gains the available count and is a logged no-op (moves never throw). Team read is **team-only** with a **map-level `?.`** (`G.cardTraits?.[extId]?.team`) — legacy/unit states predate WP-179, and only Heroes carry a team (Wounds, Bystanders, and the three basic S.H.I.E.L.D. cards are teamless), so a team match cannot false-positive on a non-Hero; no `heroClass` guard is added.
- **Determinism.** No `ctx.random` (nothing revealed or shuffled). The resolver mutates `G.piles.wounds` + player discard zones (correctly hashed), but fires **only** when a `core-mastermind-magneto-crushing-shockwave` tactic is defeated, and **no committed replay/sentinel fixture does so** — so sentinel `finalStateHash` + `PRE_WP080_HASH` stay **byte-identical** (no re-pin, confirmed by the green suite). No new `G` field.

**Consequences.** Additive engine change (one resolver + three consts + one dispatch branch + one local scan helper) in a single layer (Game Engine); no new zone / move / phase / `G` field / persisted state; no `boardgame.io`/registry import; no `.reduce()`. Engine suite 2349 → 2356 (+7), 0 fail; `sim:runtime-observed:check` current with no regeneration. The other three core Magneto tactics (Bitter Captor, Electromagnetic Bubble, Xavier's Nemesis) stay inert (each needs a pending-choice / deferred hand injection — separate follow-on WPs), and the /debug/effects tactic-coverage feed is WP-507. §17 (§3 faithful rules; No conflict; NG-1..7 not crossed; determinism §8/§22). §20 N/A. §21 N/A. `User-Visible Surface = play.legendary-arena.com` — **D-24026 live-verify operator-pending** (defeat Magneto's Crushing Shockwave; each other X-Men-less player gains two Wounds + the Fight log lines show). Reserved by WP-506; landed at WP-506 execution.

### D-24313 — Mastermind tactics in the effect-implementation index: a closed-enum `mastermind` scope + a card-data tactic feed with a curated provenance overlay (Active — WP-507 / EC-542; landed 2026-08-07)

**Context.** Mastermind **tactic** cards appeared **nowhere** in the effect-implementation index (`data/metadata/effect-implementation-index.json`), so `/debug/effects` could not show whether a tactic's printed **Fight:** ability is implemented. The index was a verbatim join of the **hero + villain** mechanic ledgers only, and tactics live in neither — so a defeated-but-inert tactic (the whole WP-497 arc) was invisible until someone played it (as reported 2026-08-06 for core Magneto). This closes the observability gap the arc exposed.

**Decision.**
- **New closed-enum `mastermind` scope (a registry contract change).** `"mastermind"` is appended to `EFFECT_INDEX_ENTRY_SCOPES`; `EffectImplementationSummarySchema.byScope` gains a required `mastermind` count; and the `superRefine` `scopeTally` accumulator (a hardcoded literal the comparison loop reads) gains `mastermind: 0` — the drift-lockstep the enum widening demands (the loop iterates the array, but the accumulator is a literal, so a missing seed is `NaN`). Chosen over folding tactics under the `villain` scope (which would conflate two different card kinds) and over a separate tactic index (which the dashboard would have to merge).
- **A generator tactic feed, engine-free.** `scripts/build-effect-implementation-index.mjs` gains `readMastermindTactics`, which enumerates every mastermind tactic from the card data (`data/cards/*.json`, sorted `readdir`; `masterminds[].cards[]` with `tactic: true`) into `mastermind`-scoped entries — ext_id `${setAbbr}-mastermind-${mastermindSlug}-${tacticSlug}` (the `mastermind.setup.ts` grammar), `name` = the tactic card name, `set` = the file-level `abbr`, `mechanic` = the tactic **slug** (each tactic is its own `card × mechanic` row). The generator stays engine-free — card data + committed JSON only, no `packages/game-engine` import.
- **Curated provenance overlay + verbatim honesty.** A new committed `scripts/coverage/tactic-provenance.json` (the WP-493 generated-identity / curated-provenance split) supplies `status`/`handler`/`wp`/`decision` for the **implemented** tactics only (WP-497 Octet, WP-506 Crushing Shockwave). A tactic absent from the overlay defaults to `status: "unmarked"` with blank `handler`/`wp`/`decision` — the honest "no handler ran" signal, never a fabricated attribution (AC-4/AC-5). The regenerated index is CI-gated by `effect-index:check`; the generator's own honesty invariants are now CI-gated too, via a new `effect-index:test` `.test.ts` (imported after guarding the CLI behind `isRunDirectly`) wired into `ci.yml` beside `roadmap:counts:test`.
- **Dashboard scope wiring.** `useEffectIndex.ts` gains the `scopeLabel` mastermind case and `EMPTY_INDEX.byScope.mastermind`; `EffectsPage.vue` gains a **Mastermind** filter chip (from `SCOPE_FILTERS`), the `byScope` mastermind count, and a `.fx-scope-mastermind` badge. The bundled index JSON stays gitignored, regenerated by `prebuild:effect-index`.

**Consequences.** Cross-layer (registry schema contract + shared-tooling generator + dashboard reader), each layer's boundary respected: the registry owns the widened contract, the generator reads data only, the dashboard reads the index verbatim. Regenerated index 1367 → 1823 entries (+456 mastermind rows; 2 executable, 454 unmarked). **No engine / `G` / runtime / determinism surface** — no `finalStateHash` / `PRE_WP080` re-pin, no card-data change. Registry 221 → 222 / 0; `effect-index:test` 7 / 0; dashboard 435 → 436 / 0 + `vue-tsc` 0; `pnpm -r build` 0. No Vue component-render test was added — the dashboard has no component-render infrastructure; coverage is the composable tests (`scopeLabel` + the mastermind scope filter) plus the `vue-tsc` typecheck of `EffectsPage.vue`. §17 (§22 product legibility; No conflict; determinism untouched; NG-1..7 not crossed). §20 N/A. §21 N/A. `User-Visible Surface = dashboard.legendary-arena.com/debug/effects` — **D-24026 live-verify operator-pending** (filter to Mastermind → core Magneto's four tactics show, Crushing Shockwave + Octet `executable`, the rest `unmarked`). Reserved by WP-507; landed at WP-507 execution.

### D-24314 — Escaping villains carry their captured Bystanders into the Escaped Villains pile (`G.escapedPile`), not back to the supply (Active — WP-508 / EC-543; landed 2026-08-07)

**Context.** On a villain escape the engine returned the villain's attached Bystanders to the shared supply (`resolveEscapedBystanders`, "prevent memory leaks"). That is the opposite of the tabletop rule ("carried away") and left the Bystanders uncountable — so Midtown Bank Robbery's printed Evil-Wins ("8 Bystanders carried away by escaping Villains") could not be modeled and rode the twist-count doom-clock proxy (D-24178). Surfaced live 2026-08-07: a core Magneto / Midtown co-op ended `scheme-wins` at twist 8 with an empty escaped pile.

**Fences.** `G.escapedPile` is hashed, so this re-pins any fixture that escapes a villain **with attached Bystanders**. No committed fixture does — sentinel `finalStateHash` + `PRE_WP080_HASH` verified byte-identical at execution. No new `G` field. Reserved by WP-508; landed at WP-508 execution.

### D-24315 — Scheme resource-loss conditions: data-only `SchemeTwistConfig.resourceLossCondition` (escaped-pile card-type count) that sets `SCHEME_LOSS` from the escape path and suppresses the twist-count proxy (Active — WP-508 / EC-543; landed 2026-08-07)

**Context.** D-24178 records six core schemes whose real Evil-Wins is a resource condition, not a twist count — for them the twist-count `SCHEME_LOSS` write is a doom-clock proxy. WP-508 begins modeling the real conditions, starting with the escaped-pile-count subclass (Midtown; later Negative Zone / Secret Invasion / Killbots).

**Decision.** `SchemeTwistConfig` gains an optional data-only `resourceLossCondition` = `{ kind: 'escaped-pile-count'; cardType: RevealedCardType; threshold: number }`. A new pure module `rules/schemeResourceLoss.ts` (`countEscapedPileByType` + `applyEscapedPileResourceLoss`) sets `G.counters[SCHEME_LOSS] = 1` when `G.escapedPile` holds ≥ `threshold` entries of `cardType`, checked at the **end of the escape branch** (the only place the pile grows). `evaluateEndgame` stays counter-only. When a scheme declares a `resourceLossCondition`, the twist-count proxy is **suppressed** for it: `schemeTwistHandler` (which holds `config`) passes `suppressTwistLoss` into `buildGenericTwistEffects`; the twist count still increments. Wired for Midtown Bank Robbery (`cardType: 'bystander'`, `threshold: 8`). Twist-loss schemes (Portals, Cosmic Cube) declare none and keep the twist-threshold loss.

**Classification refinement (surfaced at execution).** Escaped-pile entries are classified via `G.villainDeckCardTypes`, which covers villain-deck cards but **not** supply Bystanders (`BYSTANDER_EXT_ID = 'pile-bystander'`, which Midtown's twist captures from the supply). `countEscapedPileByType` therefore also maps `BYSTANDER_EXT_ID` → `'bystander'`; without this Midtown would undercount its supply-captured Bystanders. This refines the WP's "via `villainDeckCardTypes`" wording.

**Fences.** Data-only config (JSON-serializable); no new `G` field; `SCHEME_LOSS` set to 1 (idempotent; `evaluateEndgame` checks ≥ 1). Determinism preserved (no re-pin; see D-24314). Reserved by WP-508; landed at WP-508 execution.

**Context.** Negative Zone Prison Breakout's printed Evil-Wins is *"If 12 Villains escape"* (`data/cards/core.json`). ### D-24317 — Retire the generic `escapedVillains >= ESCAPE_LIMIT` game-loss from `evaluateEndgame`; villain-escape losses are per-scheme (Active — WP-509 / EC-544; landed 2026-08-07)

**Context.** `evaluateEndgame` carried a generic `escapedVillains >= ESCAPE_LIMIT (8)` → `scheme-wins` branch — an MVP cap (its own comment: *"becomes part of MatchSetupConfig in a later packet when scheme-specific limits are implemented"*). It fired for **every** scheme at 8 escaped adversaries: it preempted Negative Zone's real 12 and was simply wrong for any scheme whose Evil-Wins is not villain-escape-count. With D-24316 modeling the real per-scheme condition, the generic branch had to go — Negative Zone could never reach 12 while the generic 8 stood.

**Decision.** The `escapedVillainCount >= ESCAPE_LIMIT` branch (plus its now-unused local and the `ESCAPE_LIMIT` import) is removed from `evaluateEndgame`; villain-escape losses now arrive via `SCHEME_LOSS` from the escape path (D-24316 / D-24315 framework). `evaluateEndgame` stays counter-only. The `ESCAPED_VILLAINS` counter keeps incrementing per escaped adversary (stats + heuristic); the `ESCAPE_LIMIT` constant is **retained** — it remains the `coopOutcome.ts` loss-cause heuristic threshold and a `sweep.analyze.ts` diagnostic. `classifyCoopOutcome` keeps its `'loss-villains-escaped'` category and its `escapedVillains >= ESCAPE_LIMIT` branch, now documented as a **loss-cause heuristic** (a Negative Zone loss carries escapedVillains ≥ 12 ≥ 8, so the label stays correct); `COOP_OUTCOME_CATEGORIES` / `CoopGameRecord` unchanged (no dead category, no closed-set churn).

**Fences.** `evaluateEndgame` is a pure `G.counters` read **outside** the hashed state, so removing the branch does not move `finalStateHash` / `PRE_WP080_HASH` — verified byte-identical at execution. It CAN change a match *outcome* (a match that lost at 8 escapes now continues); no committed replay/sentinel/simulation fixture depended on the 8-escape loss (`sim:runtime-observed:check` current; whole-workspace suite green). ### D-24318 — Stack-depletion resource-loss: the `'pile-depleted'` kind + a central `turn.onMove` chokepoint (Active — WP-510 / EC-545; landed 2026-08-07)

**Context.** D-24178 records six core schemes losing on a twist-count doom-clock proxy. WP-508 (D-24315) modeled the escaped-pile-count subclass; WP-510 adds the **stack-depletion** subclass — schemes whose printed Evil-Wins is "a named pile runs out." Super Hero Civil War is the first: *"Evil Wins: If the Hero Deck runs out."*

**Decision.** `SchemeResourceLossCondition` is widened from a single interface to a **discriminated union on `kind`**: the existing `{ kind: 'escaped-pile-count'; cardType; threshold }` member is unchanged, and a new `{ kind: 'pile-depleted'; pile: 'heroDeck' }` member is added (WP-511 extends `pile` to `'wounds'` for Legacy Virus). A new pure helper `applyPileDepletionResourceLoss(G)` (`rules/schemeResourceLoss.ts`) sets `G.counters[SCHEME_LOSS] = 1` (idempotent) when the active scheme declares a `'pile-depleted'` condition and the named pile is empty (`remainingPileCount` resolves `'heroDeck'` → `G.heroDeck.length`). It is wired into the **play-phase `turn.onMove`** hook (`game.ts`), immediately after `latchFinalTurnIfDeckExhausted(G)` — a **central per-move chokepoint**, distinct from WP-508's escape-branch chokepoint, chosen because the hero deck drains from multiple paths: ordinary recruiting AND the Civil War twist's `ko-from-hq` (`koCount: 2`) resolver, which forces HQ refills outside any recruit move. A `recruitHero`-only check would miss twist-driven depletion. Twist-proxy suppression is inherited (the `schemeHandlers.ts` `suppressTwistLoss = config?.resourceLossCondition != null` gate is kind-agnostic).

**Reachability (honest scope).** The loss models `heroDeck.length === 0` faithfully; *reaching* zero depends on player count (the twist drains only 2 cards/twist, so most drain is ordinary recruiting). At 3-5 players the deck empties reliably; at **2 players with a full-size deck** it may not — which is why the card prints *"use only 4 Heroes at 2 players."* That per-player hero-deck **sizing** is a setup-time override. WP-510 ships the depletion **mechanic** (a strict improvement over the twist proxy at every count); the 2p Civil War hero-deck sizing that completes 2p reachability shipped as **WP-515 / D-24328** (`resolveEffectiveHeroDeckIds`, 4 groups at 2p; landed 2026-08-10) — RS-1 correction: this note originally deferred it to WP-511, but WP-511 / D-24321 shipped **only** the Legacy Virus 6-wounds/player sizing, not Civil War hero sizing. Legacy Virus is deferred entirely because its flat-30 wound stack would be unlosable at every count with the proxy suppressed — a hard regression, unlike Civil War's degree-only 2p weakness.

**Fences.** Contract change to a `.types.ts` file, gated here (mirrors D-24315's authorization of the original additive change); backward-compatible — the only consumers narrow on `.kind` before reading member fields, so `applyEscapedPileResourceLoss` is untouched. `applyPileDepletionResourceLoss` mutates only `G.counters` + log; no new `G` field, no new counter, `evaluateEndgame` stays counter-only. Determinism: a read of `G.heroDeck.length` + the existing `SCHEME_LOSS` write; `finalStateHash` + `PRE_WP080_HASH` **byte-identical** (no committed Civil War fixture depletes the hero deck). ### D-24319 — Civil War hero-deck-empty pre-empts the deck-exhaustion tie via counter precedence, not new tie logic (Active — WP-510 / EC-545; landed 2026-08-07)

**Context.** The deck-exhaustion final-turn logic (WP-367 / D-24159) latches the final turn when the villain **or hero** deck empties (`latchFinalTurnIfDeckExhausted`, `turn.onMove`) and resolves a **tie** at `turn.onEnd` if no win/loss fired. Civil War's hero-deck-empty must be an Evil-Wins (`SCHEME_LOSS`), NOT that tie — so the two conditions co-occur (an empty hero deck both latches the final turn and triggers the scheme loss on the same move).

**Decision.** No change to `finalTurn.logic.ts` or `evaluateEndgame`. The override is a consequence of two existing mechanisms: (1) `evaluateEndgame` checks `SCHEME_LOSS` (→ `scheme-wins`) **before** `FINAL_TURN_TIE` (→ `tie`); (2) `resolveFinalTurnTieIfUnresolved` sets the tie only when `evaluateEndgame(G) === null`. Because `applyPileDepletionResourceLoss` sets `SCHEME_LOSS` on the same `turn.onMove` that empties the deck, the top-level `Game.endIf` (WP-411 / D-24223) resolves `scheme-wins` before `turn.onEnd` even runs; and even if the turn continued, the tie-resolution guard would see `SCHEME_LOSS >= 1` and early-return. The tie can never precede the loss — the tie is only ever set at `onEnd`, strictly after the `onMove` that empties the deck.

**Fences.** Verified by the `finalTurn.logic.test.ts` D-24319 integration test (drives the full chain: empty hero deck → latch + depletion helper → tie no-op → `evaluateEndgame` returns `scheme-wins`) and the `game.test.ts` AC-6 wiring test (the real `turn.onMove` closure). No `finalTurn.logic.ts` / `evaluateEndgame` change; no new counter. Reserved by WP-510; landed at WP-510 execution.

### D-24321 — Scheme-specific setup sizing: Legacy Virus builds 6×players Wounds (Active — WP-511 / EC-546; landed 2026-08-07)

**Context.** Legacy Virus prints *"Wound stack holds 6 Wounds per player,"* but setup built a flat `config.woundsCount` (default 30). In-match `UIState` and snapshots read the built pile (12), so gameplay is correct. Reconciling the loadout display is deferred.

### D-24322 — Sim turn loops honor pile-depletion losses; coverage/win-rate backdrop switched off Legacy Virus (Active — WP-511 / EC-546; landed 2026-08-08)

**Context.** Surfaced during WP-511 execution. Pile-depletion scheme losses (Civil War hero deck, D-24318; Legacy Virus wounds, D-24320) are set in the bgio play-phase `turn.onMove` hook. The simulation harnesses (`simulation.runner.ts` `runPerTurnLoop` — used by the hollows coverage sweep, coop-winrate, and the sweep runner — and `par.aggregator.ts`) **reimplement the turn loop and bypass bgio**, dispatching moves + checking `evaluateEndgame` but never calling `turn.onMove`. Escaped-pile losses (WP-508/509) fire in the `revealVillainCard` *move*, so they were already sim-visible; pile-depletion losses were **not**. This was latent under WP-510 (no harness runs Civil War) but WP-511 exposed it: the hollows harness + coop-winrate use **Legacy Virus** as their fixed backdrop, and its now-deck-dependent wound loss stopped terminating the solo sweep — games ran to `MAX_TURNS` and the `sim:runtime-observed:check` CI gate timed out (>10 min vs seconds).

**Decision.** Two parts. (1) **Sim-visibility:** both reimplemented turn loops now call `applyPileDepletionResourceLoss(gameState)` after each dispatched move, mirroring `turn.onMove`; the next iteration's `evaluateEndgame` reads the `SCHEME_LOSS` it sets. Idempotent + pile-agnostic; a no-op for schemes without a `pile-depleted` condition. This makes pile-depletion losses (Civil War, Legacy Virus) terminate in-sim, consistent with real bgio play. (2) **Backdrop switch:** the hollows coverage harness (`scripts/runtime-observed-hollows.mjs`) and coop-winrate yardstick (`scripts/coop-winrate.mjs`) switch their fixed backdrop scheme from `core/legacy-virus-the` to `core/unleash-the-power-of-the-cosmic-cube` — a true twist-loss scheme (`lossThreshold: 8`, explicit) whose loss is set in the twist-count path the sim already honors, giving deterministic ~twist-8 termination regardless of the hero deck under test (the property a coverage backdrop needs; Legacy Virus's real loss is now deck-dependent and unsuitable).

**Cost + follow-up.** Cosmic Cube's "wound all players" twist plays fewer hero abilities, so the runtime-observed artifact drops ~16→10 distinct mechanics; the dashboard in-play-coverage metric moves `totalObs` 178→163, `percentResolved` 33.1→36.2 (resolvedObs unchanged at 59). Portals-to-the-Dark-Dimension yields 12 mechanics (better) but loses via the unconfigured MVP fallback (fragile), so Cosmic Cube was chosen for robustness. A follow-up may optimize the coverage backdrop (e.g., give Portals an explicit `lossThreshold`, or a coverage-tuned backdrop) to recover the lost coverage.

**Fences.** The sim call reads pile lengths + sets the existing `SCHEME_LOSS` counter — no new `G` field, no engine-behavior change in real bgio play (`turn.onMove` unchanged). The runtime-observed artifact (`docs/ai/coverage/runtime-observed-hollows.json`) was regenerated; the dashboard's gitignored build-time copy (`build-coverage-ledger.mjs`) and the `useInPlayCoverage` test's pinned values were updated in lockstep. `sim:runtime-observed:check` is green (4 s). Whole-workspace suite green. Reserved by WP-511; landed at WP-511 execution.

**Post-merge re-gate addenda (2026-08-08, INFRA follow-up — disclosures the fold's single-pass verification missed).** (1) **coop-winrate comparability:** `sim:coop-winrate` is the bot-ally STRENGTH yardstick; switching its backdrop to Cosmic Cube (plus WP-511 suppressing Legacy Virus's proxy loss) changes *what it measures* — pre/post-WP-511 win-rate numbers are NOT comparable (Cosmic Cube's wound-all twist lowers the absolute rate for scheme-difficulty reasons unrelated to bot strength). Treat it as a go-forward baseline from WP-511; noted in the `coop-winrate.mjs` header. (2) **Third off-bgio dispatch path:** the "both sim turn loops" wording above is precise for the *live* sim harnesses, but a **third** move-dispatch path — `replay/replay.execute.ts` (`replayGame`/`applyReplayStep`, the reducer-determinism harness, D-0205) — also does not run `turn.onMove` effects (it already omits the final-turn latch), so a recorded pile-depletion game replayed there will not set `SCHEME_LOSS`. This is by-design and consistent (faithful reconstruction, D-24119, uses boardgame.io's own reducer, which DOES run `turn.onMove`; setup sizing is honored regardless); a clarifying comment was added to `replay.execute.ts`. Both are comment/doc-only fixes; no behavior change.
