Marker `[effect:ko-wounds-current-hand-and-discard]` on Ymir's Fight line (`inputs/villain-effect-markers.json` → `data/cards/core.json`). A no-param primitive needs **no new parser arm** — it parses via `parseUngatedEffect`'s terminal `parts.length === 1` branch (and the marker script's mirror `return parts.length === 1`), once the token is appended to both `VILLAIN_EFFECT_PRIMITIVES` arrays.

**Two narrowings (locked).** (1) *"Choose a player"* → the **current player**, and *"any number"* → **all**, in the shipped solo / co-op modes: a rational chooser KOs every one of their own Wounds since it is pure upside, so there is no player-selection UI and no partial-KO pending choice. (2) The scan is **hand + discard only** (the printed zones) — deliberately NOT in-play (distinct from `ko-heroes-current-by-trait`, which scans in-play because a Hero played this turn sits there): Wounds enter a deck via `gainWound` (→ discard) or a draw (→ hand) and are never played into in-play. KO'd Wounds go to the general KO pile (`G.ko`), not back to the `G.piles.wounds` supply.

**Fences.** No `ctx.random` (Ymir's Fight reveals/shuffles nothing). The marker adds a Fight descriptor to Ymir's setup-built, hashed `villainAbilityHooks`, so a fixture whose villain config includes Enemies-of-Asgard would shift its initial-`G` hash — but **no committed fixture references Enemies-of-Asgard or Ymir** (sentinel = `core/brotherhood`, `PRE_WP080_HASH` = synthetic group; the runtime-observed sweep is brotherhood-only), so `finalStateHash` / `PRE_WP080_HASH` are **unchanged** (verified — full engine suite green, `sim:runtime-observed:check` no diff). Reserved by WP-516; landed at WP-516 execution.

### D-24332 — Melter Fight `ko-cullable-each-deck-top`: KO each player's cullable deck-top card (Superseded by D-24413 2026-08-24 — WP-519 / EC-554; the auto-resolve landed 2026-08-10, replaced by the WP-603 interactive KO/keep choice)

**Context.** The core Masters-of-Evil villain **Melter** (`core/masters-of-evil/melter`, copies 2) has one printed ability — a Fight, *"Each player reveals the top card of their deck. For each card, you choose to KO it or put it back."* — that was **unmarked**, so `onFight` reached no executable handler. A 2p co-op Secret Invasion vs Dr. Doom live-verify (2026-08-10, match `25b12dd6`) logged the D-24266 `unmarked-ability` `no-handler` breadcrumb on both Melter copies (turns 10 and 29; game-log lines `9.2.11` and `28.2.15`). Baron Zemo / Ultron / Whirlwind (same group) were already marked/executable, so this is a single-villain, single-ability WP, not a cluster. (Separately: all four **co2e** 2nd-edition Masters-of-Evil villains are unmarked — a distinct whole-set gap, out of scope here.)

**Decision.** Add a sixteenth `VillainEffectPrimitive`, `'ko-cullable-each-deck-top'` (append-only, D-24034; count 15 → 16) — a **keyword-less, no-param, auto-resolve** primitive. Its handler `villainEffectKoCullableEachDeckTop` iterates every player in `Object.keys(G.playerZones).sort()` (D-18902 determinism), reveals each player's deck top — reshuffling their discard into the deck first when the deck is empty (`reshuffleDiscardIntoDeck`, the standard reveal-reshuffle rule, the `scry-ko-own-deck` precedent D-24285) — and KOs the revealed card to `G.ko` (via `moveCardFromZone` + `koCard`) **only when it is cullable**, otherwise leaving it on top. It self-narrates via `pushLog` (keyword-less → `descriptorToLegacyKeyword` returns `undefined`, no `VillainEffectResult`). Marker `[effect:ko-cullable-each-deck-top]` on Melter's Fight line (`inputs/villain-effect-markers.json` → `data/cards/core.json`). A no-param primitive needs **no new parser arm** — it parses via `parseUngatedEffect`'s terminal `parts.length === 1` branch (and the marker script's mirror), once the token is appended to both `VILLAIN_EFFECT_PRIMITIVES` arrays.

**The choice-collapse (locked).** The printed *"you choose to KO it or put it back"* gives the fighting player a per-card KO/keep decision over every player's revealed deck top. In the shipped solo / co-op modes all players are allies, and a rational cooperative chooser thins **weak** cards while keeping real ones — so the choice collapses deterministically to: KO the revealed card iff it is **cullable**, defined as a Wound (`WOUND_EXT_ID`) or a basic starting S.H.I.E.L.D. card (`SHIELD_AGENT_EXT_ID` / `SHIELD_TROOPER_EXT_ID`). This is the `selectScryKoTarget` tiers-1–2 "worst-worthy" set (D-24267); the tier-3 lexical fallback is **excluded** (it exists only because `scry-ko-own-deck` must KO one of two cards — Melter can keep), and the recruited `SHIELD_OFFICER_EXT_ID` and every real Hero are **kept**. Because a real Hero is **never** force-KO'd, the auto-resolve carries no agency loss: the failure mode that made `scry-ko-own-deck` an *interactive* pending choice (WP-470 / D-24282 — its must-KO-one rule destroyed a real Hero when both revealed cards were Heroes) cannot arise here. So there is **no pending choice, no player-selection UI, no UIState field, no client change** (operator-selected fidelity, drafting session 2026-08-10).

**Fences.** Randomness only via the seeded reshuffle (`reshuffleDiscardIntoDeck` → `shuffleContext.random.Shuffle`); no `Math.random()`. The marker adds a Fight descriptor to Melter's setup-built, hashed `villainAbilityHooks`, so a fixture whose villain config includes Masters-of-Evil would shift its initial-`G` hash, and the reveal/reshuffle/KO writes shift state when a fixture fights Melter. **Unlike Ymir, `masters-of-evil` is referenced by scoring fixtures** (`parScoring.keys.ts`, `parScoring.logic.test.ts`, `par.storage.test.ts`) — but those are PAR-key/scoring string-key fixtures, not hashed replay oracles. The hashed oracles use non-MoE configs (sentinel `sentinel-core-doom-2p.replay.json` = `core/brotherhood`; `PRE_WP080_HASH` = synthetic `test/test-villain-group-001`), so `finalStateHash` / `PRE_WP080_HASH` are **unchanged** (verified — full engine suite green including the replay/sentinel tests, `sim:runtime-observed:check` no diff). Reserved by WP-519; landed at WP-519 execution.

### D-24333 — co2e Masters of Evil curation subset + deferred-epic enumeration (Active — WP-520 / EC-555; landed 2026-08-10)

**Context.** The co2e (Legendary 2nd-edition) Masters-of-Evil villain group ships four villains whose timing lines are all unmarked (the whole-set gap flagged while executing WP-519). Faithfully closing the group is **not** uniform: three timing lines reduce to primitives the engine already ships, while three others each need a brand-new primitive, and two lines are variable-attack passives (a different mechanic class). Marking everything at once would cross from card-data into the engine layer and bundle multiple new primitives into one WP.

**Decision.** WP-520 is the **curatable-subset** increment (the WP-185 conservatism-over-coverage discipline): mark **only** the three timing lines whose whole effect reduces to an existing `VillainEffectPrimitive`, card-data only, no engine change:
- **Melter Fight** — verbatim the core Melter Fight text → `[effect:ko-cullable-each-deck-top]` (WP-519 / D-24332; hard-dep on WP-519 being on `main`).
- **Ultron Escape** *"Each player reveals a [hc:tech] Hero or gains a Wound."* → `[effect:reveal-or-wound:hc:tech]` (WP-469 / D-24281 — the exact marker core Ultron Escape already uses).
- **Whirlwind Fight** *"If you fight Whirlwind on the Rooftops or Bridge, KO one of your Heroes."* → `[effect:ko-hero:current@rooftops+bridge]`. "KO **one**" is the bare `ko-hero:current` (implicit magnitude 1, the WP-242 interactive KO) under the universal `@`-location gate (WP-489 / D-24295). **`ko-hero:current:1` is deliberately NOT used** — the parser rejects a magnitude token < 2 (D-24298), so magnitude 1 is expressed by omitting the token. `parseParameterizedEffect` splits the `@` gate first, then parses the bare left side, so `ko-hero:current@rooftops+bridge` yields `{ primitive: 'ko-hero', target: 'current', requireCitySpaces: ['rooftops','bridge'] }`. Distinct from core Whirlwind's `ko-hero:current:2@rooftops+bridge` (KO two). No `mechanic-provenance.json` row is added — each marked line inherits its owning primitive's WP/decision (no net-new primitive).

**Deferred epic (each needs a NEW `VillainEffectPrimitive` — one WP apiece, not part of WP-520):**
- **Baron Zemo Ambush** — *"captures a Bystander. Then he captures another Bystander for each [team:avengers] Hero in the HQ."* A **dynamic HQ-team-count capture**: no existing primitive counts HQ heroes by team for a capture count (`capture-bystander:<N>` is a *fixed* count; `rescue-bystanders-current-by-trait-count` counts *your* heroes and *rescues*, not HQ heroes captured).
- **Ultron Fight** — *"Choose a [hc:tech] Hero from the HQ. Either KO that Hero or choose a player to gain it."* An **interactive HQ-hero KO-or-gift**: `capture-hq-hero` captures by a fixed selector and offers no KO-or-give-to-player branch.
- **Whirlwind Ambush** — *"Two Villains in the city swap spaces."* A **city board-position manipulation**: no existing primitive moves/swaps villains between City spaces.

**Passives (a separate, non-hollow mechanic class, tracked outside this curation):** Baron Zemo *"+1[icon:attack] for each Bystander he has"* and Ultron *"+1[icon:attack] for each [hc:tech] Hero in the HQ"* are **not** Fight/Ambush/Escape timing lines, so they never trip the D-24266 `unmarked-ability` detector — they are variable-villain-attack (`resolveFightCost`) work, distinct from this hollow-line curation.

**Fences.** Card data only — no `packages/**` change, no new primitive, no test change. The only determinism surface is the hashed `villainAbilityHooks` of a fixture whose villain config includes `co2e/masters-of-evil`; the known hashed oracles use `core/brotherhood` + a synthetic group (WP-519 pre-flight), so `finalStateHash` / `PRE_WP080_HASH` are expected **unchanged** (verify at execution; re-record via the canonical tool if any shifts). Reserved by WP-520; **Active at WP-520 execution — landed 2026-08-10**: all three markers applied (`co2e.json — 3 new marker(s)`, idempotent), the three lines flipped unmarked → executable in the villain ledger + effect-index (attributed to their owning primitives, no net-new provenance row), `PRE_WP080_HASH` / `finalStateHash` **byte-identical** (no committed fixture references `co2e/masters-of-evil`), engine test 2447 pass / 0 fail with no test change. Card-data only; the co2e `masters-of-evil` marker block already existed (created by WP-521 for Baron Zemo Ambush), so this appended the melter/ultron/whirlwind rows.

### D-24334 — co2e Baron Zemo Ambush `capture-bystanders-plus-per-hq-hero-by-trait` + first HQ-by-trait count (Active — WP-521 / EC-556; landed 2026-08-10)

**Context.** Epic 1/3 of the co2e Masters-of-Evil deferred-primitive set (D-24333). co2e Baron Zemo's Ambush — *"Baron Zemo captures a Bystander. Then he captures another Bystander for each [team:avengers] Hero in the HQ."* — is unmarked (D-24266). Its capture count scales with **HQ** heroes matching a team trait, which no existing primitive expresses (`capture-bystander:<N>` is a fixed count; `rescue-bystanders-current-by-trait-count` counts the current player's hand+in-play heroes and *rescues*).

**Decision.** Add an auto-resolve `VillainEffectPrimitive` `'capture-bystanders-plus-per-hq-hero-by-trait'` (append-only, D-24034; count 16 → 17) carrying a `{ requireKind, requireValue }` trait predicate (`parseTraitPredicateTokens`, marker `[effect:capture-bystanders-plus-per-hq-hero-by-trait:team:avengers]`, a new parse arm mirroring `reveal-or-wound`). Its handler `villainEffectCaptureBystandersPlusPerHqHeroByTrait` attaches `1 + countHqHeroesByTrait(G.hq, G.cardTraits, requireKind, requireValue)` Bystanders to the triggering villain via `attachBystanderToVillain`, supply-bounded on `G.piles.bystanders`, **attach-only at Ambush** (the award is deferred to defeat, the existing `capture-bystander` Ambush semantics, D-18506), self-narrating via `pushLog`. Introduces the engine's **first HQ-by-trait count** — a local `countHqHeroesByTrait` that runs `cardTraitMatches` over the five `G.hq` slots (the shared player-zone scanners are left unchanged). The printed base is fixed at 1; only the additional captures scale.

**Fences.** No `ctx.random`. `buildCardTraits` omits synthetic component cards (Wounds, basic S.H.I.E.L.D. — D-24296), but those never sit in the HQ and an `[team:avengers]` predicate never matches them, so no widening is needed. The marker adds an Ambush descriptor to Baron Zemo's hashed `villainAbilityHooks`; no hashed oracle includes co2e MoE (sentinel `core/brotherhood`, `PRE_WP080_HASH` synthetic — WP-519 pre-flight), so hashes are **unchanged** (verified — full engine suite green including the replay/sentinel tests; no committed fixture references co2e Masters of Evil). Reserved by WP-521; landed at WP-521 execution.

### D-24335 — co2e Ultron Fight HQ tech-Hero KO-or-gift: fidelity fork (Active — WP-522 / EC-557; landed 2026-08-10, Fork A)

**Context.** Epic 2/3 of the co2e MoE deferred-primitive set (D-24333). co2e Ultron's Fight — *"Choose a [hc:tech] Hero from the HQ. Either KO that Hero or choose a player to gain it."* — is unmarked (D-24266). It carries two nested choices (which HQ tech Hero; KO vs gift; and if gift, which player), so it needs a new primitive and a **fidelity fork**.

**Decision (fork, operator to confirm at review; drafted for Fork A).** **Fork A — auto-resolve (recommended):** in the shipped solo/co-op modes, gifting an HQ Hero into a player's **discard** dominates KO'ing it in the common case (the player gains a free Hero card *and* the HQ still refills, whereas KO only refills), so a rational cooperative chooser essentially always gifts. Two honest caveats the operator should weigh: the collapse fixes the recipient to the **current player** (the card allows any player — occasionally another benefits more), and adding a Hero to a deck is not *universally* upside (a thinning-focused player might marginally prefer the KO). Neither overturns the common-case gift; both are why Fork B exists. The choice therefore collapses to a new primitive `give-hq-hero-by-trait-to-current` (marker `[effect:give-hq-hero-by-trait-to-current:hc:tech]`): remove the **highest-cost** `[hc:tech]` HQ Hero (cost from `G.cardStats`, ties → rightmost index, matching `captureHeroFromHq`), `refillHqSlot`, and push it onto the **current (fighting) player's discard** (the WP-514/D-24327 gain-routing — "gain" is discard, never victory); no `[hc:tech]` HQ Hero → reachable no-op. Deterministic, no pending choice, no client change — consistent with the WP-516 Ymir / WP-519 Melter "choose a player → current player" collapses. The KO branch is intentionally not implemented under Fork A (dominated). **Fork B — interactive pending-choice (alternative):** preserve the full choice as a parked `pendingUltronHqChoice` (the scry-ko WP-470/D-24282 shape), which requires the 7-touchpoint pending pattern (resolve move, block-all guards across ~12 move/turn-transition sites, `buildUIState` projection + `filterUIStateForAudience` whitelist arm, a client prompt component + wiring, and the bot `ai.legalMoves` entry) shipped atomically. **Recommendation: Fork A** — the KO option has one rational answer in co-op, so auto-resolving preserves the only outcome a rational player picks at a fraction of the cost.

**Fences.** No `ctx.random` (Fork A selection is deterministic; the HQ refill is the already-hashed `G.heroDeck` FIFO shift). The marker adds a Fight descriptor to Ultron's hashed `villainAbilityHooks`; no hashed oracle includes co2e MoE, so hashes are expected **unchanged** (verify; re-record if any shifts). Reserved by WP-522; **Active at WP-522 execution — landed 2026-08-10, Fork A confirmed by the operator**: the new primitive `give-hq-hero-by-trait-to-current` (union + array position 18, drift test 17→18) removes the highest-cost `[hc:tech]` HQ Hero (ties → rightmost, matching `captureHeroFromHq`), refills the vacated slot from `G.heroDeck`, and gives the Hero to the current player's discard; the KO branch is not implemented (dominated). Engine test 2452 pass / 0 fail (+5); `PRE_WP080_HASH` / `finalStateHash` byte-identical (no committed fixture references `co2e/masters-of-evil`); co2e Ultron Fight flipped unmarked → executable with `{ WP-522, D-24335 }`. No client change (Fork A).

### D-24336 — co2e Whirlwind Ambush `swap-two-city-villains`: first City board-position manipulation + swap-rule fork (Active — WP-523 / EC-558; landed 2026-08-10, Rule B + Whirlwind eligible)

**Context.** Epic 3/3 of the co2e MoE deferred-primitive set (D-24333). co2e Whirlwind's Ambush — *"Two Villains in the city swap spaces."* — is unmarked (D-24266), and is the **first** effect that repositions cards within the City. The `G.city` writes today are only `pushVillainIntoCity` (entry+advance) and the defeat null-out; no swap/reposition primitive exists. The card names **neither a chooser nor which two Villains**, so the swap-selection rule is a genuine design fork the engine must lock deterministically (the City RNG surface is `Shuffle`-only, and the wider swap family selects by fixed position).

**Decision (fork, operator to confirm at review; drafted for Rule B).** Add a no-param `VillainEffectPrimitive` `'swap-two-city-villains'` (append-only, D-24034; marker `[effect:swap-two-city-villains]`, parsed by the generic no-param terminal branch — no parser arm). Its handler `villainEffectSwapTwoCityVillains` collects the `G.city` indices whose occupant is `'villain'`-classified (`G.villainDeckCardTypes` — **henchmen excluded**, per "Villains"); with fewer than two it is a reachable no-op; otherwise it swaps the **lowest-index and highest-index** such spaces — **Rule B (frontmost ↔ rearmost)**, the largest positional displacement and the strongest "disrupt the board" reading — with **Whirlwind itself eligible** (it is pushed into the City at the entrance before its Ambush fires). Candidate rules considered and rejected as the default: Rule A (frontmost two — minimal displacement when adjacent) and Rule C (fixed Sewers↔Bridge — frequent no-op on a sparse board). Fires at the Ambush site (`cityIndex` undefined; the swap is space-relative, reading `G.city` directly — not the WP-489 location gate). The City stores `CardExtId | null` only, so the swap exchanges two ext_id strings between indices. **Locked disposition (operator-confirmable): Rule = B; Whirlwind = eligible; henchmen = excluded; `< 2` villains = no-op** — flipping any is a one-line handler + EC change.

**Family forward-compat.** "Swap two City Villains" is the first of an unimplemented City-swap/reposition family (Ravenous, Weaponized Galactus, Ravagers, Infinity Stones, Vulture, Storm, a co2e Green Goblin Twist — none implemented); the primitive/helper is designed as a general City-position swap so the family can reuse it, but WP-523 is scoped to Whirlwind's Ambush only.

**Fences.** No `ctx.random` (Rule B is positional). The marker adds an Ambush descriptor to Whirlwind's hashed `villainAbilityHooks`, and a swap **write** shifts City state when a fixture reveals co2e Whirlwind with ≥ 2 City Villains; no hashed oracle includes co2e MoE, so hashes are expected **unchanged** (verify; re-record if any shifts). Distinct from `core/masters-of-evil/whirlwind` (WP-492, a different card). Reserved by WP-523; **Active at WP-523 execution — landed 2026-08-10, Rule B + Whirlwind-eligible confirmed by the operator**: the new no-param primitive `swap-two-city-villains` (union + array position 19, drift test 18→19) collects the villain-occupied City indices (`G.villainDeckCardTypes[id] === 'villain'`, henchmen excluded) and, with ≥ 2, swaps `G.city[lowest]` ↔ `G.city[highest]` (`collectCityVillainIndices` + direct index assignment mirroring the defeat null-out); fewer than two is a reachable no-op. Engine test 2458 pass / 0 fail (+6); `PRE_WP080_HASH` / `finalStateHash` byte-identical (no committed fixture references `co2e/masters-of-evil`); co2e Whirlwind Ambush flipped unmarked → executable with `{ WP-523, D-24336 }`. First City board-position manipulation; the helper is general enough for the future City-swap family but only Whirlwind's Ambush is wired. No client change.

### D-24330 — DR-readiness dashboard feed derives from the `dr-drill-reminder` GitHub issues (Active — WP-517 / EC-552; landed 2026-08-10)

**Context.** The DR arc (backups → GFS → 3-2-1 → runbook → reminder) is complete; the remaining risk is a drill cadence that silently lapses. The `dr-drill-reminder` workflow (#1298) already opens dated `DR drill due — <Month> <Year>` issues (em-dash U+2014, UTC month) on cadence — that issue lifecycle is the operator's existing system of record for drills. WP-517 surfaces DR-drill readiness as a tile on the dashboard's System-Health (ops) page.

**Decision.** The `GET /api/dash/dr-readiness` feed derives readiness from those drill issues rather than from a parallel committed status ledger or a parse of `DISASTER_RECOVERY.md` §7: an OPEN drill issue whose title month is earlier than the (injected) reference month = **overdue**; the newest **closed** drill issue = **last drill**; `nextDue` = the 1st of the next month (UTC). The issue body carries no PASS/FAIL field today, so WP-517 amends `dr-drill-reminder.yml` to add a single `- [ ] Drill passed` checkbox; the operator checks it before closing a drill issue, and the feed reads that checkbox on the newest closed drill issue → `result: pass | fail | unknown` (checked / present-unchecked / absent). The endpoint mirrors the existing `/api/dash/*` idiom exactly (`requireAdminSession`, `Cache-Control: no-store`, `{ data }` envelope) and is **mock-first** — absent/invalid `DASH_GITHUB_TOKEN` returns `200` with `source:"mock"`, never a 500. Read-only end to end: neither the endpoint nor the tile ever creates/edits/closes issues; the workflow edit only adds the checkbox to newly-opened issues.

**Fences.** No `packages/**` change; no engine/registry/determinism/persistence/RNG surface (an ops-only, read-only projection). The derivation `deriveDrReadiness(issues, referenceDate)` is pure — the reference date is injected, never read from a clock inside the logic — so the derivation is unit-tested against fixture issues with a fixed date. Field names follow the `/api/dash/*` projection convention (WP-373/374/439), not a new 00.2 lock. Reserved by WP-517; landed **Active** at WP-517 execution (2026-08-10) — `deriveDrReadiness(issues, referenceDate)` shipped pure in `apps/server/src/dashboard/dashboardDrReadiness.logic.ts`, fed by the mock-first `GET /api/dash/dr-readiness` route and surfaced by the `DrReadinessWidget` ops tile; `dr-drill-reminder.yml` carries the `- [ ] Drill passed` checkbox. (Renumbered from D-24329 after Ymir shipped under WP-516/EC-551/D-24329, #1300/#1301.)

### D-24331 — Secret Invasion Skrull gain announced in the fight overlay narrative (Active — WP-518 / EC-553; landed 2026-08-10)

**Context.** Surfaced 2026-08-10 from a 2p core Magneto + Secret Invasion of the Skrull Shapeshifters co-op match (`TYSkhUJwNsZ`): the operator believed the scheme's *"If you defeat that Hero, you gain it"* rule was not firing. It was — the diagnostics, durable log, and post-match zone state all confirm the WP-514 / D-24327 defeat-to-gain path routing the defeated Skrull to the defeating player's discard, six times across both players. The gap was **feedback, not mechanic**: the `fightResolved` notable-event narrative (the sentence the center-screen `NotableEventOverlay` shows on a defeat) read `Fought "X".` for a Skrull — byte-identical to an ordinary villain kill — and because a gained Hero routes to the discard (no VP-bearing card lands in the victory pile), nothing on screen distinguished the two. The player read the correct engine outcome as "the gain isn't happening."

**Decision.** `composeFightNarrative` (`events/notableEvents.compose.ts`) gains a fourth parameter `skrullGained: boolean = false`. When true it appends `" and gained the Hero into the active player's discard pile"` after the bystander clause and before the `"; Fight effect: …"` clause. `defeatCityVillainCore` (`moves/fightVillain.ts`) captures `skrullGained = true` from `G.convertedVillainOrigins[cardId] === 'skrull'` **before** it deletes the origin overlay, and threads it into the emission. Third-person voice (`"the active player's"`) matches the effect clauses because the overlay narrative is a shared, all-audience projection, not owner-scoped. The engine mechanic (routing, deletion, durable log line) is unchanged — this is a presentation-only enrichment.

**Fences.** Game-engine only; no card data, no marker pipeline, no registry, no client change (the arena-client already renders `event.narrative` verbatim). No new G field, no new event type, no `appliedEffects` change, no `ctx.random`. **Determinism:** `notableEvents.narrative` IS hashed (no observation-channel exclusion, unlike `messages`/`logMeta`/`diagnostics`), but the default `false` keeps every non-Skrull narrative byte-identical and the clause fires only on a Skrull defeat — and no committed fixture defeats a Skrull (grep-verified: no fixture/`*.replay.json` references `skrull`/`secret-invasion`; the sentinel replay fires no fight event; `PRE_WP080_HASH` uses a synthetic group), so `finalStateHash` / `PRE_WP080_HASH` are unchanged (confirmed by the full engine suite green). Hard-deps WP-514 / D-24327 (defeat-to-gain) + WP-319 / D-24105 (the `composeFightNarrative` overlay contract).

### D-24337 — Secret Invasion requires a scheme-aware effective hero-group count (its "6 Heroes" setup clause) (Active — WP-524 / EC-559; landed 2026-08-11)

**Context.** Secret Invasion of the Skrull Shapeshifters prints *"Setup: 8 Twists. 6 Heroes. Skrull Villain Group required. Shuffle 12 random Heroes from the Hero Deck into the Villain Deck."* WP-514 / D-24326 shipped the 12-hero → Skrull conversion + combat + loss, but its scoped "printed rules" quote **dropped the "6 Heroes" clause** — so the setup pipeline sized the match by the standard `PLAYER_COUNT_SETUP.heroCount` (5 at 2–4 players) and live matches ran with 5 hero groups (confirmed from a 2p Dr. Doom + Secret Invasion co-op match, `heroDeckIds.length === 5`).

**Decision.** A new pure `resolveEffectiveHeroCount(schemeId, numPlayers, baseHeroCount)` in `packages/registry/src/playerCountSetup.ts` returns `Math.max(baseHeroCount, 6)` for `core/secret-invasion-of-the-skrull-shapeshifters` (FLAT 6 — 2/3/4p 5→6; 5p already 6; solo-1p 3→6, the literal clause), else the base count. Unlike the two `schemeSetupSizing` DOWNSIZE overrides (D-24321 Legacy Virus wounds, D-24328 Civil War hero deck), which post-validation size a BUILT pile below the validated config, this is a requirement **INCREASE**: the operator must actually supply 6 hero groups, so the override lives on the requirement side and is reached by every hero-count enforcement site — `checkPlayerCountComposition` (registry; via a new optional `schemeId` on `PlayerCountCompositionInput`), and — exposed as a **required** member of the `CardRegistry` interface (both `impl/localRegistry.ts` + `impl/httpRegistry.ts`) — the game engine's `validatePlayerCountComposition`, which forwards `input.schemeId` and applies `registry.resolveEffectiveHeroCount?.(schemeId, numPlayers, row.heroCount) ?? row.heroCount` through the structural `CardRegistryReader` (the `?.`/`??` fallback is for hand-rolled test mocks only; production impls compile-error if they omit it). The registry-viewer loadout builder (`useLoadoutDraft`) threads the draft `schemeId` and displays the effective count (a spread row, never mutating the immutable table row). The base `PLAYER_COUNT_SETUP` table is not mutated; the 9-field `MatchSetupConfig` composition lock is preserved (`heroDeckIds` unchanged field).

**Scope / split.** WP-524 is the enforcement core (registry + engine + registry-viewer). The scheme-blind arena-client **play lobby** + the server `/api/match/setup-requirements` projection are **WP-525 / D-24338**, which ships as a set: WP-524's live engine change without WP-525 would make Secret Invasion un-creatable via the play lobby (it disables Create on a mismatch). The co-located *"Skrull Villain Group required"* villain-group membership constraint is a separate follow-up (already satisfied in the reported match).

**Fences.** No `.reduce()` in the resolver; no new `ctx.random`; no `boardgame.io` import in the registry helper; no registry import in the engine (structural reader). **Determinism:** scheme-gated → every other scheme/count is byte-identical; no committed fixture materializes Secret Invasion (D-24327 grep — no fixture/`*.replay.json` references `skrull`/`secret-invasion`; the sentinel replay is Legacy Virus; `PRE_WP080_HASH` uses a synthetic scheme), so `finalStateHash` + `PRE_WP080_HASH` are unchanged (confirmed by the full engine suite green + whole-workspace `pnpm -r --no-bail test` exit 0). Control-revert non-vacuous at all three layers. Hard-deps WP-514 / D-24326 + WP-370 / D-24165.

### D-24338 — Secret Invasion play-lobby requirement projection is scheme-aware (`/api/match/setup-requirements?schemeId=`) (Active — WP-525 / EC-560; landed 2026-08-11)

**Context.** WP-524 / D-24337 made the engine + registry-viewer builder require 6 hero groups for Secret Invasion, but the arena-client **play lobby** (`play.legendary-arena.com`) is scheme-blind: it compares the loadout against a flat `GET /api/match/setup-requirements` projection (`PLAYER_COUNT_SETUP` verbatim, no scheme input) and **disables Create** on any mismatch (`canSubmitCreate` / `canSubmitFromJson`). So WP-524 alone would make Secret Invasion **un-creatable via the play lobby** — a correct 6-hero loadout is blocked by the lobby while a 5-hero one is rejected by the engine.

**Decision.** `GET /api/match/setup-requirements` gains an **optional `schemeId` query**. When present, a pure server-side `projectSetupRequirements(schemeId)` (`apps/server/src/match/matchGate.routes.ts`) projects each row's `heroCount` through the WP-524 registry `resolveEffectiveHeroCount` (imported from the browser-safe `@legendary-arena/registry/playerCountSetup` subpath — the barrel does not re-export it — so **no registry-package change**); when absent it returns the base `PLAYER_COUNT_SETUP` unchanged, **byte-identical to the pre-WP-525 response**, so every existing caller is unaffected. The `schemeId` is part of the URL cache key (kept `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`), so per-scheme responses cache independently. The arena-client lobby — barred from importing the registry at runtime — threads the **selected scheme** (the manual form's `schemeId` ref and the pasted loadout's `composition.schemeId`, each its own path) into `fetchSetupRequirements(schemeId?)` (URL-encoded) and **re-fetches on scheme change** (a captured-scheme guard discards a stale in-flight response) into per-path requirement refs; the pure comparator `playerCountRequirements.ts` is **unchanged** — the scheme-awareness lives entirely in the row values. The `matchGate.routes.ts` module-header JSDoc that claimed no registry import (already false since WP-371) was corrected.

**Scope / fences.** Server + arena-client wiring only — **no engine / registry / determinism surface touched**. Autoplay is **Out of Scope** (its default-loadout pool is a fixed non-Secret-Invasion scheme, so Secret Invasion never reaches it; the bot-ally path `POST /api/match/create-with-bot` has no scheme-blind client gate — it relies on the engine 400). `api-endpoints.md` whole-row replaced for `/api/match/setup-requirements` (D-11804 §21; `Auth` stays `guest`, `Status` `Wired`). **Ship as a set with WP-524 / D-24337** — WP-524's live engine change without this play-lobby change is the un-creatable-scheme regression this split avoids. Server 12-test matchGate suite + full server suite green; arena-client 1229 pass / 0 fail (two new scheme-aware Create-gate tests); whole-workspace green; control-revert non-vacuous (neuter the server projection → the SI route test fails; neuter the client `schemeId` pass-through → the SI Create-gate test fails; base + other-scheme stay green). Hard-dep WP-524 / D-24337.

### D-24339 — `bystanderLost` penalty is derived at end-of-match from `G.escapedPile`, not a new counter (Active 2026-08-11 — WP-528 / EC-563)

**Decision.** The `bystanderLost` `PenaltyEventType` is produced by deriving its count at end-of-match from `G.escapedPile` — counting entries whose `villainDeckCardTypes[extId] === 'bystander'` — rather than from a new `G.counters.BYSTANDERS_LOST` counter or a structured event log (the two options the stale `deriveScoringInputs` safe-skip comment named).

**Why the derivation, not a counter.** `G.escapedPile` already durably records carried-away Bystanders: `carryEscapedBystandersToPile` (D-24314) routes a captured Bystander into it when its Villain escapes — from both the villain-deck reveal escape branch and the scheme-twist city-displacement escape branch. A pure derivation therefore reads state that already exists and adds **no** `G` field — keeping `finalStateHash` and `PRE_WP080_HASH` byte-identical and avoiding the dual hash re-pin a new counter would force. It also mirrors the existing `bystandersRescued` derivation exactly (same `'bystander'` discriminator, opposite zone: victory pile for rescued, escaped pile for lost).

**Symmetric across both derivation copies.** The same derivation is applied in `deriveScoringInputs` (real-match / leaderboard) and `deriveScoringInputsFromFinalState` (`par.aggregator.ts`, PAR-calibration). Counting `bystanderLost` on only the real-match path would make calibrated PAR baselines systematically too easy on any bystander-losing scenario, breaking the `finalScore = rawScore − parScore` premise.

**No double-count.** Villains in `escapedPile` remain the `villainEscaped` / `ENDGAME_CONDITIONS.ESCAPED_VILLAINS` count; only `bystander`-typed entries feed `bystanderLost`.

**Scoring-version posture.** Wiring a penalty producer shifts the score distribution for a given `ScenarioScoringConfig`. Because this lands **before** any production `ScenarioScoringConfig` or `legendary.competitive_scores` row depends on `bystanderLost`, no retroactive `scoringConfigVersion` bump or re-score is owed. Any producer wired **after** production configs / competitive entries exist MUST bump `scoringConfigVersion` (the general rule this entry also records).

**Scope.** This entry covers only `bystanderLost`. The remaining safe-skips (`schemeTwistNegative`, `mastermindTacticUntaken`, `scenarioSpecificPenalty`) and any re-anchoring of per-config penalty weights to the community/rulebook 4:3:1 ratio are separate future work.

_Active — landed at WP-528 execution (EC-563). Hard-dep: WP-048 ✅ + D-24314 ✅._

### D-24340 — `schemeTwistNegative` counts every scheme twist (from `G.counters.schemeTwistCount`), not a polarity subset (Active 2026-08-11 — WP-529 / EC-564)

**Decision.** The `schemeTwistNegative` `PenaltyEventType` is produced by deriving its count at end-of-match as `G.counters.schemeTwistCount ?? 0` — the total number of scheme twists flipped during the match — rather than by classifying each twist's outcome as "negative" or not.

**Why every twist counts (not a polarity subset).** In Legendary a Scheme Twist *is* the villain's clock: every twist advances the scheme against the players, and there is no beneficial scheme twist. The community/rulebook Total Score confirms it — it subtracts `3 × (Number of Scheme Twists)` unconditionally. So a per-twist polarity/outcome classification (which the Scoring wiki previously anticipated as "a discriminated scheme-twist outcome projection") is neither needed nor faithful; the faithful producer is simply the count of twists flipped.

**Why the counter, not new state.** Every revealed scheme twist already increments the durable `G.counters.schemeTwistCount` via `buildGenericTwistEffects` (`rules/schemeHandlers.ts`) — including the Mystique escape→twist path and schemes whose twist-count loss is suppressed by a `resourceLossCondition` (the increment still runs; only the loss latch is suppressed). Reading it adds **no** `G` field, keeping `finalStateHash` and `PRE_WP080_HASH` byte-identical (no re-pin). It mirrors the existing `escapes = counters[ESCAPED_VILLAINS] ?? 0` counter read.

**Symmetric across both derivation copies.** Applied in `deriveScoringInputs` (real-match) and `deriveScoringInputsFromFinalState` (`par.aggregator.ts`, PAR-calibration). Counting on only the real-match path would make calibrated PAR baselines systematically too easy on twist-heavy scenarios.

**Scoring-version posture.** Wiring a penalty producer shifts the score distribution for a given `ScenarioScoringConfig`. Because this lands **before** any production `ScenarioScoringConfig` or `legendary.competitive_scores` row depends on `schemeTwistNegative`, no retroactive `scoringConfigVersion` bump or re-score is owed. Any producer wired **after** production configs exist MUST bump `scoringConfigVersion`.

**Scope.** This entry covers only `schemeTwistNegative`. The remaining safe-skips (`mastermindTacticUntaken`, `scenarioSpecificPenalty`) and any re-anchoring of per-config penalty weights to the community/rulebook 4:3:1 ratio are separate future work. (`bystanderLost` is WP-528 / D-24339.)

_Active — landed at WP-529 execution (EC-564). Hard-dep: WP-048 ✅ + D-24178 ✅._

### D-24341 — AI Second Brain knowledge platform: architecture + governance-vehicle lock (Active 2026-08-11 — architecture record, no WP)

**Decision.** Adopt a self-hosted **AI second brain** — an operator-owned knowledge platform whose durable store is the system of record and whose AI models and agent frameworks are *replaceable* clients (*knowledge is permanent; agents are replaceable*). It is governed as a **standalone DECISIONS architecture record plus the ewiki design page** ([`ai-second-brain`](https://ewiki.legendary-arena.com/ai-second-brain/)), **not** as an engine Work Packet.

**Governance vehicle (why a D-record, not a WP).** The platform is operator/personal cross-project infrastructure that crosses **none** of the engine layers (Registry / Game Engine / Server) the Work Packet spine governs. Forcing it through the `01.0a` WP+EC workflow would be a category mismatch. Instead it follows the **Ubuntu Lab Provisioning precedent**: a `DECISIONS.md` architectural lock in this engine repo, a descriptive ewiki companion, and the executable runbook deferred to when it is built (a future Work Packet or a separate program repo). This entry is the authoritative source the ewiki page cites; the page stays `status: draft` until the platform is actually built.

**Ownership & model independence.** Knowledge lives on operator-controlled hardware in open, portable formats (PostgreSQL, Markdown, Git, MCP). Models reach it only through MCP + a routing gateway, so swapping a model (Claude → open-weights → whatever is next) is a configuration change, never a data migration. **No single-vendor lock-in format may be persisted into the store** (e.g. proprietary embeddings only one provider can read), or the swap-freely property silently breaks.

**Retrieval architecture (mostly-Markdown, minority-vector).** Roughly **90% navigable structured Markdown / 10% semantic vector**, not a vector-first system. Governed, structured, context-sensitive records — `DECISIONS.md`, Work Packets, Execution Contracts, runbooks, the Architecture Inventory, the wikis — are reached by **exact reference / grep / per-domain index navigation**, and are **never chunk-embedded** (chunking strips the surrounding context those records exist to preserve). The vector layer (`pgvector` + HNSW, `nomic-embed-text` 768-dim as the CPU-friendly default) is reserved for **high-volume unstructured reference** (transcripts, research archives, email) where exact lookup does not scale.

**Hosting.** A **dedicated host is the preferred end-state**, separate from production `api.legendary-arena.com`, because a chat surface, model gateway, and vector DB next to the live game server is a resource-contention and attack-surface concern. **Co-location is acceptable during the bootstrap phase** — while infrastructure is small and operator-managed — provided the brain stays *logically* separate: process isolation, its own credentials, independent backups, and clear service boundaries. Physical separation is a scaling/risk-management decision, not a prerequisite for initial deployment. _(Revised 2026-08-11 from the initial "never co-located" wording to match the actual bootstrap-then-separate plan; the isolation guarantees, not the host boundary, are the load-bearing part.)_

**Operating discipline & boundaries.** Work runs in a **Plan → Build → Verify → Improve** loop with the operator as product manager (defines intent, boundaries, acceptance criteria) and the AI as researcher/executor within them. **Permissions beat prompts** is a hard rule: enforce boundaries with scoped credentials, blocked commands, hooks, and read-only access, not with instructions a model can ignore or a swap can drop. AI capability is layered simplest-first (skills → verification checks → conservative safety/logging hooks → subagents-for-research → orchestration last). Deliberately **out of scope until a real pain point justifies it**: always-on autonomous ingestion (fights the deterministic/auditable/grepable posture) and a general knowledge graph (only the Work Packet → EC → Decision → Change → Release governance chain is a possible future).

**Scope / deferred.** This entry locks the *architecture and governance vehicle* only. The buildable artifacts — the ingestion script, Postgres schema, `docker-compose`, and provision/deploy runbook — are execution instruction and are **deferred** to a future Work Packet or separate program repo; they are deliberately kept off both this record and the descriptive ewiki page.

_Active — architecture record, no WP. ewiki companion: `ai-second-brain` (stays `status: draft` until built). Precedent: Ubuntu Lab Provisioning governance pattern. No engine-layer, determinism, or persistence impact._

### D-24342 — Penalty weights anchored to the rulebook 4:3:1 ratio (Active 2026-08-15 — WP-531 / EC-566)

**Decision.** The three **rulebook** penalty weights are anchored to the community/rulebook **4:3:1** ratio — `bystanderLost : schemeTwistNegative : villainEscaped = 4 : 3 : 1` — expressed in this engine's centesimal weights as **`bystanderLost 400` : `schemeTwistNegative 300` : `villainEscaped 100`** (`villainEscaped = 100` is the rulebook's "1.00" unit). This is the Legendary Leagues / rulebook Total Score relationship (`Total Score = VP − 4·bystanders − 3·twists − 1·escapes`), validated by the cross-system review that also motivated the producer WPs (WP-528 / WP-529).

**Scale.** The ratio is fixed; the absolute scale is the minimal centesimal mapping `400 / 300 / 100`. The alternative `800 / 600 / 200` (retaining the reference's prior `villainEscaped = 200`) is rejected as non-minimal — the rulebook's lightest penalty maps to `1.00`, not `2.00`.

**Where it applies.** The frozen scoring surface `docs/12-SCORING-REFERENCE.md` (all **four** weight-bearing statements: the default-weights table, the "Default Values Satisfy All Invariants" worked block, the "Full Formula (Expanded)" line, and the **Worked Example**, whose two players were recomputed — Player A raw `-1900` / final `-700` ["7.00 under PAR"], Player B raw `-700` / final `+500` ["5.00 over PAR"], the gap widening `11.00 -> 12.00`; reward weights and PAR are unchanged, so only the penalty coefficients moved) and the test `ScenarioScoringConfig` (`data/scoring-configs/test-…json`, previously `villainEscaped 100 / schemeTwistNegative 50 / bystanderLost 300`), the latter with a `scoringConfigVersion` bump `1 → 2`. This establishes the authoring standard for production configs when they are created; none exist yet.

**Unchanged.** `mastermindTacticUntaken` (+100) and `scenarioSpecificPenalty` (scenario-defined) are Legendary-Arena-specific penalties **not** part of the rulebook triple, and the reward weights (`W_BP` bystanderReward, `W_VP`, `W_R`) are untouched.

**Deliberate parity.** Lowering `villainEscaped` to the rulebook 1-unit (`100`) makes it equal to `mastermindTacticUntaken` (`100`) and `roundCost` (`W_R = 100`) in the reference defaults. This is intended, not a collision: neither equality is an enforced structural invariant, and semantically a villain escape, a missed tactic, and one round of elapsed time are all reasonably "one unit" of cost. The reference prose framing `mastermindTacticUntaken` as a "minor / tiebreaker-level" penalty (calibrated when escape was `200`) is now parity, not sub-escape; kept as-is (a scenario may still weight tactics lower via its own config).

**Invariants preserved.** All three `12-SCORING-REFERENCE` structural invariants (enforced by `validateScoringConfig`) hold under the new weights: `W_BP > villainEscaped` (reference `300 > 100`; test config `200 > 100`); `bystanderLost > villainEscaped` (`400 > 100`); `bystanderLost > W_BP` (reference `400 > 300`; test config `400 > 200`).

**No logic / no re-score.** Weights are data consumed by the existing `computeRawScore`; no engine logic changes and no `G` state is touched, so `finalStateHash` is unaffected. No production `ScenarioScoringConfig` or `legendary.competitive_scores` row exists under the old weights, so no historical re-score is owed; the `scoringConfigVersion` bump is the forward comparability boundary (VISION §22). SAFE-KNOBS §"Explicitly Non-Configurable" lists scoring formulas as a governed surface, so this change is a WP + this record, not a customer knob.

**Scaffold result (recorded, not reasoned).** Applying the weights produced **zero** failing assertions — engine 2613/0 and `pnpm -r --no-bail test` exit 0, before and after. The three test files WP-531 listed conditionally therefore stayed out of the diff. The reason is worth keeping: `scoringConfigLoader.test.ts` writes its own configs into a `mkdtemp` temp dir and `par.aggregator.test.ts` uses hand-built inline weights, so neither reads the real `data/scoring-configs` file. That is deliberate test isolation, not a coverage gap.

**Guard is non-vacuous under the new numbers.** Verified directly against the built `validateScoringConfig`: the updated test config returns `{valid: true}`, while a control dropping `bystanderLost` to `100` is still rejected, naming both violated invariants.

_Active 2026-08-15 — landed at WP-531 execution (EC-566). Data + docs only; no engine-logic file changed. `wiki/scoring.md` — the ewiki page this ratio was sourced from — moves from "Phase-1 seed" to adopted reference default while preserving the calibration-supremacy caveat. Hard-dep: WP-048 ✅ + WP-528 ✅ + WP-529 ✅. `User-Visible Surface = play.legendary-arena.com` (Final Score) — D-24026 live-verify operator-pending, and player-observable only once a production `ScenarioScoringConfig` ships with these weights; the reference + test-config re-anchor is correct regardless._
### D-24343 — Paibok the Power Skrull Fight is an interactive per-player HQ-hero gain (`give-hq-hero-each-player`) (Active 2026-08-12 — WP-532 / EC-567)

**Decision.** The core Skrulls villain Paibok the Power Skrull's printed Fight — *"Choose a Hero in the HQ for each player. Each player gains that Hero."* — is implemented as the twentieth `VillainEffectPrimitive` `give-hq-hero-each-player` (append-only per D-24034; union + array lockstep, count 19 → 20) — another villain-effect primitive that introduces its own pending-choice type, after `ko-hero` (WP-242, reused by WP-492) and `scry-ko-own-deck` (WP-470). On Paibok `onFight`, **every player gains one Hero from the HQ into that player's `discard`** (the D-24327 "gain" routing — never victory), and each vacated HQ slot **refills** from `G.heroDeck` (`refillHqSlot`; leaves `null` on an empty reservoir). The mutation reuses the WP-522 / D-24335 `give-hq-hero-by-trait-to-current` shape **minus the trait filter** (any HQ Hero) and **broadened to each player**.

**Fidelity fork resolution (operator, 2026-08-11).** "Choose a Hero in the HQ" is a genuine per-player choice. The operator locked it as **interactive for the human, highest-cost for the bot** — each player's Hero is chosen by that player when human-controlled, or auto-picked (highest-cost) when bot/auto-driven. In the shipped co-op case (human fighting, bot allies) this maps cleanly onto the **current-player-parks / others-auto-resolve** split established by D-24284 (`PendingDiscardChoice`). **This is an operator design choice, not an engine limitation:** a more literal rendering — the fighting player making N sequential picks (one Hero per player) via the same FIFO queue — was available but deliberately not taken, because the operator assigns the bot allies' Heroes to the auto-highest-cost rule rather than to the human's choice. A future WP could add current-player-multi-pick as an extension seam:

- **The current (fighting) player** — the human, in the reported co-op case — parks a new `pendingGiveHqHeroChoice` when ≥ 2 HQ Heroes remain (auto-gains when exactly 1, no-ops when 0). The client renders a "choose a Hero to gain" prompt over the public HQ; if the current player is bot/auto-driven, `ai.legalMoves` pre-fills the resolve move with the **highest-cost** HQ Hero, so the bot never blocks.
- **Every other player** auto-gains the **highest-cost** HQ Hero synchronously (no park; ties → rightmost index, matching `captureHeroFromHq`) — the D-24284 "others auto-resolve" arm, satisfying the operator's "for the bot, just choose the highest cost."

**Ordering (determinism).** Non-current players resolve FIRST, in `Object.keys(G.playerZones).sort()` order (each gains highest-cost from the live HQ + refill), THEN the current player is handled — so the human picks from the HQ that remains after the others resolve, a single deterministic sequence. No `ctx.random`.

**Atomic ship (`project_pending_choice_no_ux_freeze`).** The block-all guard (`hasPendingGiveHqHeroChoice` added to the full pending cascade), the `buildUIState` + `filterUIStateForAudience` projection (`UIPendingGiveHqHeroChoice`, `eligible` recomputed from the public `G.hq`), and the arena-client `PendingGiveHqHeroChoicePrompt.vue` land in the SAME WP — an engine `pending*` block shipped without a client prompt is a hard-freeze.

**Surface.** New pending type `PendingGiveHqHeroChoice` + `G.pendingGiveHqHeroChoices` FIFO; new move `resolveGiveHqHeroChoice` (`client: false`, not in `CORE_MOVE_NAMES`; move count 27 → 28); `PENDING_CHOICE_MOVE_NAMES` (`botLoopProgress.mjs`) + `PENDING_CHOICE_FLAGS` (`botAllyDriver.mjs`) extended. Net-new primitive → `{ "wp": "WP-532", "decision": "D-24343" }` provenance row. Marks **core** `core/skrulls/paibok-the-power-skrull` Fight only; the co2e Paibok twin (also `(unmarked)`) is a fast follow-up. Determinism: the new hashed pending queue + Fight hook re-pin oracles only if a committed fixture fights Paibok (`core/skrulls`) — verified at execution, never hand-edited.

_Active 2026-08-12 — landed at WP-532 execution. The 20th `VillainEffectPrimitive` (union+array lockstep, drift 19→20); move count 27→28 (`resolveGiveHqHeroChoice`, not a CORE_MOVE_NAME). Block-all guard follows the D-24301 `returnOnDiscard` 9-site convention (NOT the 12-file ko-hero set). No new hashed-oracle re-pin (the new `pendingGiveHqHeroChoices` field is lazily created / undefined by default → `finalStateHash`/`PRE_WP080_HASH` byte-identical; no committed fixture fights Paibok). co2e twin left `(unmarked)` — fast follow-up. Hard-deps: WP-242/D-24007 + WP-243/D-24010 + WP-476/D-24284 + WP-522/D-24335._

### D-24344 — Preferences foundation uses the "Option A" path (all under `registry-viewer/src/prefs/`, no new workspace package) (Active 2026-08-12 — WP-534 / EC-569)

**Decision.** The registry-viewer preferences foundation (WP-534) is delivered via the **Option A** path: every preferences module — the Zod preferences schema, the section registry, the Pinia store factory, its persistence layer, and the `usePreferences` composable — lives under `apps/registry-viewer/src/prefs/`. **No new workspace package** (`packages/ui-preferences/`) is created; `apps/registry-viewer` stays an independent Vue 3 SPA that gains `pinia` as a dependency.

**Why Option A.** The viewer is self-contained and the preferences system is viewer-specific; a shared workspace package would add a build edge and cross-package coupling for no current consumer. Keeping everything in-app is the lower-friction delivery for the foundation and for every follow-up section WP (Display / Filters / DataSource / Advanced), which register into the in-app section registry.

**Supersedes the never-merged D-1414.** The original WP-068 locked this same Option-A choice as D-1414, but WP-068 and D-1414 never merged to `main` — they survived only on retired commit `8ec6ceda`. D-24344 re-locks the decision on `main` under the WP-534 resurrection; the code was brought forward verbatim (scaffold-verified: 0 typecheck errors + 17/17 prefs tests on current `main`).

**Scope.** Foundation only — **no user-visible UI**. The settings drawer, the gear icon, and the app-specific sections are later WPs that build on this foundation.

_Active — landed at WP-534 execution (EC-569). Hard-dep: none._

### D-24345 — Rogue "Copy Powers" is an interactive re-fire of a copied Hero's ability plus a runtime dual-class grant (`copy-powers`) (Active 2026-08-12 — WP-535 / EC-570)

**Decision.** Rogue's printed `core/rogue/copy-powers` — *"Play this card as a copy of another Hero you played this turn. This card is both [hc:covert] and the color you copy."* (cost 5, no printed attack/recruit) — is implemented as a new `copy-powers` **HeroKeyword** (append-only to the union + `HERO_KEYWORDS` array, 34 → 35; in `HANDLED_KEYWORDS` + `NO_MAGNITUDE_KEYWORDS`; `[keyword:copy-powers]` marker via `inputs/hero-ability-markers.json` — closed markupToken set extended, D-21601 — + regen `core.json`). The `heroEffectCopyPowers` handler builds the eligible-Hero set and resolves by cardinality (the WP-486 defeat-with-bystander 0/1/≥2 shape): **0 eligible → a self-narrated no-op** (logged `blocked`, never a hollow record — the keyword is in `MVP_KEYWORDS`); **exactly 1 → auto-copy** (no prompt); **≥2 → park a `PendingCopyPowersChoice`** so the current player picks which Hero to copy.

**Fork resolution (operator, 2026-08-12 — all four locked to the recommendation).** (1) **INTERACTIVE** pending-choice, not an auto-collapse — the human picks; a bot-driven chooser auto-defaults via `ai.legalMoves`. (2) "Copy" = **RE-FIRE the chosen Hero's on-play ability** via the reentrant `executeHeroEffects(G, ctx, playerID, chosenHeroId)`, NOT its printed stats (Copy Powers has no printed attack). (3) **Full dual-class** — Copy Powers counts as covert (already baked, `core.json` `hc:covert`) AND the copied Hero's class. (4) **0 eligible → clean no-op; 1 eligible → auto**.

**Eligible set.** `playerZones.inPlay`, minus the `copy-powers` ext_id (**ALL copies**, not just the one played instance — this neutralizes copy-of-copy recursion when two Copy Powers are played the same turn), real Heroes only (a non-null printed `heroClass` — S.H.I.E.L.D. starters / Sidekicks / Wounds carry `heroClass: null` and are excluded), deduplicated. Recomputed fresh at the UIState projection + the resolve validation (the round-trip rule) — no eligible snapshot is stored on the pending entry.

**Re-fire threads the FULL MoveContext (a first for a resolve move).** Both re-fire paths — the ≥2 `resolveCopyPowersChoice` move AND the 1-eligible in-handler auto path — pass the random-bearing move-context wrapper (`{ ctx, random, events, ... }`) into `executeHeroEffects`, because the copied ability may draw / reshuffle via `ctx.random`. `resolveCopyPowersChoice` mirrors `applyCardPlay`'s `{ G, playerID, ...context }` split. The re-fire calls `executeHeroEffects` **DIRECTLY** — it does NOT re-invoke `applyCardPlay`, re-append `inPlay`, or re-add the copied Hero's base attack/recruit economy (Fork 2 — ability only; base economy belongs to `applyCardPlay`, off the copy path). **[SUPERSEDED IN PART by D-24391, 2026-08-22 — WP-582.]** Fork 2's "ability only, NOT printed stats" clause is superseded: the operator confirmed from the physical card that Copy Powers is a FULL duplicate, so `applyCopyPowers` now ALSO adds the copied Hero's printed attack + recruit (via `addResources`, an intended double-count of an already-played Hero) and its team (a new lazy `cardCopiedTeams` map). The re-fire still calls `executeHeroEffects` directly and still does not re-invoke `applyCardPlay`; only the "no base economy on the copy path" clause changed. Every other D-24345 clause remains Active. `queue.shift()` front-pops the copy-powers entry BEFORE the re-fire, so a copied ability that parks its OWN nested pending lands behind it in FIFO (chained pending choices supported).

**Dual-class REUSES the existing `cardSizeChangingClasses` map (no new hashed field).** The copied class is written into the EXISTING runtime `G.cardSizeChangingClasses` (`Record<CardExtId, string[]>`, D-24074) — already read + unioned by `getGrantedClasses` at every `[hc:X]` gate — so **no new `G` field and no `sizeChanging.logic.ts` change** (copilot Finding 2). `cardTraits` is never mutated; the class is granted before the re-fire so Copy Powers already counts as the copied class if the copied ability reads classes. The one new `G` field (the `pendingCopyPowersChoices` FIFO queue) is **lazy-materialized** (undefined by default, created at the park site, never in `Game.setup`), so non-Copy-Powers games keep byte-identical `finalStateHash` + `PRE_WP080_HASH` (verified at execution — no oracle re-pin).

**Atomic ship (`project_pending_choice_no_ux_freeze`).** The block-all guard (`hasPendingCopyPowersChoice` across the full pending cascade — the 9-site D-24301 convention: `coreMoves.impl.ts` ×3 + `game.ts` + `fightVillain` + `fightMastermind` + `recruitHero` + `healWounds` + `dodgeCard` + `playFromUndercover`), the `buildUIState` + `filterUIStateForAudience` chooser-only projection (`UIPendingCopyPowersChoice`, eligible recomputed via `getEligibleCopyPowersCards`), and the arena-client `PendingCopyPowersChoicePrompt.vue` land in the SAME WP — an engine `pending*` block shipped without a client prompt is a hard-freeze.

**Surface.** New pending type `PendingCopyPowersChoice` + `G.pendingCopyPowersChoices` FIFO; new move `resolveCopyPowersChoice` (`client: false`, not in `CORE_MOVE_NAMES`; move count 28 → 29); `HERO_EFFECT_HANDLERS` 20 → 21; `HERO_KEYWORDS` 34 → 35. **Steal Abilities** (Rogue's other copy card) is a related follow-up, OUT of scope. `User-Visible Surface = play.legendary-arena.com` — **D-24026 live-verify operator-pending**.

**Fix-forward (2026-08-12, post-merge, EC-570).** Copy Powers' card text carries a
mid-sentence descriptive `[hc:covert]` ("This card is both `[hc:covert]` and the color you
copy"). The ability parser's generic Step-1a `[hc:X]` extraction (`heroAbility.setup.ts`)
turned it into a `heroClassMatch: covert` play **condition**, so the shipped hook gated the
copy behind "another covert card played this turn" — Copy Powers fired only with covert
synergy (surfaced from Jeff's live Secret Invasion game: `[blocked] a play condition … was
not met` on the Copy Powers plays). Fix: a copy-powers line's `[hc:X]` is now **suppressed**
at Step 1a (a new `lineHasCopyPowers` guard mirroring the D-24074 `lineHasSizeChanging`
exclusion) — the token is the descriptive class the card *becomes*, not a gate; covert is
already the printed `heroClass` (cardTraits) and the copied class is granted at runtime.
Copy Powers now always offers the copy. Regression guard: a real-card-data
`buildHeroAbilityHooks` test asserting the copy-powers hook carries **no** `heroClassMatch`
condition (the hand-built-hook unit tests missed it because they set no conditions). The
parser change reclassifies the copy-powers hook from condition-gated → executable, so the
hero-mechanic-ledger / effect-index / card-mechanics / runtime-observed feeds regenerate.

**Fix-forward #2 (2026-08-13, post-deploy, EC-570).** The copy-of-copy exclusion in
`buildCopyPowersTargets` compared each in-play card against the **bare** ext_id
`core/rogue/copy-powers`, but zones store **instance** ids (`<base>#<copyIndex>`, e.g.
`core/rogue/copy-powers#0`). The bare id never matched a real instance, so the exclusion never
fired: with only Copy Powers in play it counted **itself** as the single eligible target → the
1-eligible auto path re-fired `executeHeroEffects` on Copy Powers → unbounded recursion → stack
overflow → **server crash** (observed live as a ~30s "connection lost — reconnecting" whenever
Copy Powers was the only Hero in play). Fix: strip the `#N` suffix to a base id for the
exclusion AND the dedup (two instances of one Hero now collapse to one choice); the trait
lookup keeps the full instance id (cardTraits is instance-keyed). Root of the miss: the unit
tests used **bare** ext_ids, which the exclusion happened to match — so they never exercised
the production instance-id format. Added instance-suffixed regression tests (`…#0`, `…#1`).
Pure-logic change: no card-data / derived-feed drift.

_Active 2026-08-12 — landed at WP-535 execution (EC-570). Move count 28→29 (`resolveCopyPowersChoice`, not a CORE_MOVE_NAME); `HERO_EFFECT_HANDLERS` 20→21; `HERO_KEYWORDS` 34→35. No new hashed-oracle re-pin (the new `pendingCopyPowersChoices` field is lazily created / undefined by default → `finalStateHash`/`PRE_WP080_HASH` byte-identical; the dual-class reuses the existing lazy `cardSizeChangingClasses` map). Hard-deps: WP-532/D-24343 (give-HQ-Hero pending-choice precedent) + WP-251/D-24022 (`HERO_EFFECT_HANDLERS`) + WP-290/D-24074 (size-changing dual-class map). Post-merge fix-forwards: (2026-08-12) the descriptive-`[hc:X]` parser exclusion; (2026-08-13) the instance-id copy-of-self exclusion (recursion crash)._

### D-24346 — Core Loki's Master Strike is an auto reveal-`[hc:strength]`-Hero-or-Wound (Active 2026-08-13 — WP-537 / EC-572)

**Decision.** Core Loki's printed Master Strike — "Each player reveals a `[hc:strength]` Hero or gains a Wound" — is resolved **automatically**, keyed by the mastermind selection `core/loki` (not a card-data marker). Per player (sorted id order): a player holding a Strength Hero **reveals and keeps it** (the printed escape — no penalty); a player holding none gains a Wound via `gainWoundToDiscard` (an empty Wound supply degrades to a logged no-op, never a throw). Revealing is not a meaningful choice, so no pending-choice is parked — mirroring `resolveRedSkullStrike` (auto) and `resolveCo2eMagnetoStrike` (reveal/discard-or-Wound), NOT the interactive Magneto discard path.

**Surface.** New `MASTERMIND_CORE_LOKI = 'core/loki'` constant + dispatch branch + `resolveCoreLokiStrike` in `packages/game-engine/src/rules/mastermindHandlers.ts`. Deliberately **distinct from** the existing co2e `resolveLokiStrike` (`co2e/loki` prints a different penalty — discard a Strength Hero / stack a Hypno-Thrall), so the two resolvers never fold. No new `G` field, no `ctx.random`, no card-data / marker / mechanic-ledger / effect-index change (Master Strikes are keyed by mastermind selection, not markers, and are not in the effect index). Determinism: reads `G` + deterministic Wound mutation → replay-identical; no committed fixture reveals a strike under `core/loki`, so `finalStateHash` / `PRE_WP080_HASH` are byte-identical (verified at execution).

_Active 2026-08-13 — landed at WP-537 execution (EC-572). Closes 1 of the 2 hollow Core Master Strikes found in the 2026-08-13 mastermind-coverage audit (the other, Dr. Doom, is WP-538, interactive). D-24026 live-verify operator-pending._

### D-24347 — Core Dr. Doom's Master Strike is a 6-card-gated reveal-`[hc:tech]`-Hero-or-interactive-put-2-on-top (Active 2026-08-13 — WP-538 / EC-573)

**Decision.** Core Dr. Doom's printed Master Strike — "Each player with exactly 6 cards in hand reveals a `[hc:tech]` Hero or puts 2 cards from their hand on top of their deck" — is resolved per player (sorted id order): a player not holding **exactly 6** cards is unaffected; a gated player holding a Tech Hero **reveals and keeps it** (the printed escape, no penalty); otherwise the player **puts 2 cards from hand on top of their deck** (selection order = deck-top order, `cardIds[0]` drawn first). The put-2-on-top penalty is **interactive for the current player** — who parks a new `PendingPutCardsOnDeckChoice` and picks which 2 cards and in what order — and **auto (deterministic cheapest-2)** for non-current / bot players, the single-current-player-scoped split established by WP-476's Magneto discard-to-4 (D-24284).

**Surface.** New `MASTERMIND_CORE_DR_DOOM = 'core/dr-doom'` + `resolveCoreDoomStrike` in `mastermindHandlers.ts` (distinct from the co2e `resolveDoctorDoomStrike`). New `PendingPutCardsOnDeckChoice` type + optional lazy-init `G.pendingPutCardsOnDeckChoices` FIFO; new server-only move `resolvePutCardsOnDeckChoice` (`putCardsOnDeckChoice.resolve.ts`; not a `CORE_MOVE_NAME`; move count 29 → 30); block-all guards on every action move; `ai.legalMoves` short-circuit + both simulation MOVE_MAPs; UIState build / types / **audience-filter pass-through** (chooser-only, D-24011); `PendingPutCardsOnDeckChoicePrompt.vue` mounted in `PlayDesktop`/`PlayMobile` + `useTurnActions`/`TurnActionBar` gating. Cross-layer (game-engine + arena-client); ships pending + projection + prompt together (no-UX-freeze). No `data/cards` / marker / mechanic-ledger / effect-index change (Master Strikes are keyed by mastermind selection, not markers, and are not in the effect index). Determinism: no `ctx.random`; the new `G` field is optional + lazy-init. The `sentinel-core-doom-2p` complete-game fixture legitimately parks now, so `runFixture` gained a `resolvePutCardsOnDeckChoice` dispatch entry + the fixture script gained a scripted resolve move, and the fixture was re-recorded (`finalStateHash` reflects the new park→resolve trajectory; `G.messages` is hash-excluded).

_Active 2026-08-13 — landed at WP-538 execution (EC-573). Closes the second of the 2 hollow Core Master Strikes (paired with WP-537 Loki); all 4 Core Master Strikes now fire (Magneto, Red Skull, Loki, Dr. Doom). D-24026 live-verify operator-pending._

### D-24348 — Core Portals is a true twist-loss with Dark-Portal attack buffs (Active 2026-08-13 — WP-539 / EC-574)

**Decision.** Core "Portals to the Dark Dimension" is faithful: a TRUE twist-loss (`lossThreshold: 7`, no `resourceLossCondition`) so Evil Wins at exactly twist 7 by design (previously it lost at 7 only by the MVP-fallback coincidence), plus the printed Dark-Portal attack buffs. A new `DARK_PORTAL_COUNT` counter (mirroring `KILLBOT_TWISTS_NEXT_TO_SCHEME`) is bumped once per Portals twist by a new `portals` resolver. Twist 1 places the Dark Portal above the Mastermind (+1 attack); twists 2-6 fill the **leftmost portal-less city space** (leftmost = Bridge = engine index 4 first, per `DESIGN-BOARD-LAYOUT.md §City row` + WP-489/D-24295, so city space K is portal'd once `DARK_PORTAL_COUNT >= 6 - K`), giving Villains in that space +1 attack; twist 7 is Evil Wins.

**Surface.** `SCHEME_TWIST_CONFIGS` gains the Portals entry; `schemeTwistResolvers.ts` gains the `portals` resolver + the `SchemeTwistResolverId` / `SchemeTwistResolverKey` union + registry + `RESOLVER_KEY_PHRASES` + `SCHEME_TWIST_RESOLVER_KEYS` additions; `DARK_PORTAL_COUNT` is a `G.counters` key in `types.ts`. The **villain** buff is applied in `resolveFightCost` (the single villain-attack source — `darkPortalVillainBonus` reads the villain's `G.city` index + the counter, stacking on static/dynamic/killbot/skrull costs). The **mastermind** buff is applied via a new centralized `resolveMastermindFightCost(G)` (base `fightCost` + `1` once `DARK_PORTAL_COUNT >= 1` under Portals), which replaces the inline `G.cardStats[baseCardId].fightCost` reads at `fightMastermind` and `ai.legalMoves` — the only two mastermind-requirement sites (uiState.build projects no mastermind requirement, so 2 sites, not the 3 the WP anticipated). Deterministic, counter-only (no new persistent shape), no `ctx.random`; no `data/cards`/marker/ledger/effect-index change; no fixture/hash re-pin (no committed fixture reaches a Portals twist).

_Active 2026-08-13 — landed at WP-539 execution (EC-574). Portals was the last truly-hollow Core scheme; all 8 Core schemes are now configured (5 faithful, 2 partial — Civil War / Cosmic Cube, and Portals now faithful). D-24026 live-verify operator-pending._

### D-24349 — Core Civil War KOs all HQ Heroes; Core Cosmic Cube deals the printed escalation (Active 2026-08-13 — WP-540 / EC-575)

**Decision.** The two **partial** Core scheme twists (fire but diverge from print, 2026-08-13 scheme-coverage audit) are now faithful, both param-driven on the existing resolvers — no new resolverId, counter, or persistent shape. **(A) Super Hero Civil War** — printed *"KO all the Heroes in the HQ."* The `koFromHq` resolver gains an additive `koAll?: boolean` param; when `koAll === true` it KOs **every** eligible HQ Hero (KO count = `eligible.length`, still cheapest-first / slot-index tiebroken, each vacated slot refilled), and the config `params` becomes `{ koAll: true }` (was `{ koCount: 2 }`). **(B) Unleash the Cosmic Cube** — printed escalation: nothing on twists 1-4, each player gains 1 Wound on twists 5-6, 3 Wounds on twist 7 (twist 8 = Evil Wins). The `woundAll` resolver gains an additive `escalation?: { atOrAfterTwist, woundCount }[]` param; when present it reads `currentTwist = (counters.schemeTwistCount ?? 0) + 1` and deals the **MAX** matching step's `woundCount` (0 when none match = a logged no-op), and the config `params` becomes `{ escalation: [{ atOrAfterTwist: 5, woundCount: 1 }, { atOrAfterTwist: 7, woundCount: 3 }] }` (was `{ woundCount: 1 }`).

**Load-bearing invariant.** `currentTwist = schemeTwistCount + 1` because the resolver runs BEFORE `schemeHandlers.ts:schemeTwistHandler` returns the `modifyCounter schemeTwistCount +1` effect for `applyRuleEffects` — so at resolver time the counter still holds the count from **prior** twists. Twist 7 matches both escalation steps (`atOrAfterTwist: 5` and `7`), so the resolver takes the MAX (3), not the first/last; the selection uses a `for...of` max-tracking loop (no `.reduce()`).

**Surface.** `schemeTwistResolvers.ts` (`koFromHq` `koAll`; `woundAll` `escalation`) + `schemeTwistConfigs.ts` (the two configs' `params` + `// why:` updates), engine-only. Additive params: every other scheme's flat `koCount` / `woundCount` path is the default when the new param is absent. Both **loss** configs are unchanged (Civil War hero-deck-empty via WP-510/515; Cosmic Cube `lossThreshold: 8` via D-24178). Deterministic (reads `G` / `G.counters`, no `ctx.random`, no new persistent shape); no `data/cards`/marker/ledger/effect-index/client change; no fixture/hash re-pin (no committed fixture reaches a Civil-War or Cosmic-Cube twist). One `schemeTwistResolved` emission per resolver preserved.

_Active 2026-08-13 — landed at WP-540 execution (EC-575). All 8 Core schemes are now faithful (the two partial twists closed). D-24026 live-verify operator-pending._

### D-24350 — Core villain/henchman Fight-reward primitives (`gain-recruit-current` + `gain-officer-current`); the beneficial "may gain an Officer" auto-takes (Active 2026-08-13 — WP-541 / EC-576)

**Decision.** Three hollow Core villain/henchman **Fight** abilities that *reward the defeating player* (2026-08-13 villain-effect audit) are now faithful. Two new **append-only** auto-resolve `VILLAIN_EFFECT_PRIMITIVES` (D-24034; union + array, 20 → 22, moved with the drift test): **`gain-recruit-current`** — the current (defeating) player gains `magnitude` recruit points (`G.turnEconomy.recruit += N`, `N` from the `:N` token, default 1; Hand Ninjas: `gain-recruit-current:1`); **`gain-officer-current`** — the current player gains one S.H.I.E.L.D. Officer"* **auto-takes** — a pure benefit with no downside, so it resolves synchronously with no interactive choice, consistent with the keyword-less auto-resolve discipline. `gain-recruit-current` reuses the existing descriptor `magnitude` field; both primitives are keyword-less (no `LEGACY_VILLAIN_KEYWORD_TO_DESCRIPTOR` entry), reverse-map to `undefined`, and self-narrate via `pushLog`.

**Surface.** `villainAbility.types.ts` (union + `VILLAIN_EFFECT_PRIMITIVES` array + descriptor JSDoc), `villainEffects.execute.ts` (two handlers + registry), `villainAbility.setup.ts` (the `gain-recruit-current[:<N>]` parser arm; `gain-officer-current` parses via the terminal no-param branch), `apply-effect-markers.mjs` (hand-synced primitives + validation branch), `villain-effect-markers.json` (3 markers: `henchmen.core['hand-ninjas'].fight` `gain-recruit-current:1`, `villains.core.hydra['hydra-kidnappers'].fight` `gain-officer-current`, `henchmen.core['savage-land-mutates'].fight` `override-next-hand-size:7`), `mechanic-provenance.json` (`gain-recruit-current` + `gain-officer-current` → `WP-541`/`D-24350`), and the regenerated `data/cards/core.json` + `villain-mechanic-ledger.{json,csv}` + `effect-implementation-index.json`. `gain-officer-current` is `G.piles.officers`' first consumer (previously only counted/scanned). No pending-choice / UIState / client change; no new `G` field. Deterministic (reads/mutates `G` recruit-econ / officers pile / `handSizeOverrides`, no `ctx.random`); no committed fixture fights these three, so `finalStateHash` / `PRE_WP080_HASH` are byte-identical (no re-pin).
