### D-24387 — The Competitive Score Is Server-Derived and Surfaced Client-Side (Endgame Panel)

A real match review surfaced "where is my score": the competitive score is computed
server-side on replay ingest (`parScoring.logic.ts`) and stored in
`legendary.competitive_scores`, but never shown — `buildParBreakdown` hard-returns
`undefined` under D-6701, so `UIGameOverState.par` is always omitted and `EndgameSummary`
rendered only the outcome + in-game VP total.

Locked:

1. **D-6701's premise stands — the fix is client-side.** The engine has no `ReplayResult`
   at gameover, so `buildParBreakdown` STAYS returning `undefined` and `UIGameOverState.par`
   is NOT populated. The score reaches the player from the SERVER: `submitCompetitiveScore`
   (the one-shot gameover submit, `useCompetitiveSubmitOnGameover`) already returns
   `record: MyCompetitiveScore` (carrying `rawScore` + `finalScore`) on HTTP 200 — the
   composable surfaces that record and `EndgameSummary` renders it. No new fetch.
2. **Read-only display.** The endgame score is a presentation of what the server already
   computed and stored; the client renders `finalScore` (the ranked, PAR-relative,
   lower-is-better headline) + `rawScore` VERBATIM and never recomputes them.
3. **Graceful absence.** `submittedScore` (and the `EndgameSummary` prop) is `null` for
   guests (no submit), network failures, non-200s, `par_not_published` (a non-ranked
   loadout), and early-ended matches; the panel then renders the existing outcome + VP
   summary with no score and no error. A casual/unranked match that still submits still
   shows its score (`is_ranked_eligible` is orthogonal to display).
4. **App-only.** No engine, persistence, or hash surface change; the additive
   `EndgameSummary` prop is optional and prop-drilled `PlayViewport` → `PlayDesktop` /
   `PlayMobile` (the live-route path; the dev `fixture`-route `ArenaHud` is untouched).

**Active 2026-08-21 (WP-578 / EC-613).** Shipped across the composable + `EndgameSummary.vue`
+ the `PlayViewport`/`PlayDesktop`/`PlayMobile` wiring + tests. arena-client 1359→1364/0 (+5);
`vue-tsc` clean; no `packages/game-engine` change (`buildParBreakdown` still returns
`undefined`); `pnpm -r build` + `--no-bail test` green across all packages. **D-24026
live-verify: operator-pending** (`User-Visible Surface = play.legendary-arena.com`; finish a
ranked match signed in and read the competitive score on the endgame panel).

### D-24388 — Legends Leaderboard Shows the Claimed Handle as a Profile Link (Snapshot-Only)

The legends leaderboard rendered each row's player as plain-text `legendary.players.display_name`
(no link) — which falls back to the email local-part, so a public board could print an email
prefix. A public profile page already exists at `play.legendary-arena.com/?profile=<handle>`
keyed on the claimed handle (`display_handle` / `handle_canonical`, migration 008).

Locked (executed on the recommended defaults):

1. **Path A — snapshot-only.** The claimed handle is carried to the legends snapshot via a
   snapshot-internal fetch (`fetchClaimedHandlesByReplayHash`), NEVER through
   `PublicLeaderboardEntry` (the D-5201 9-field lock) or any of the four `Wired` HTTP
   leaderboard endpoints — which stay **byte-identical**, so §21 is N/A and D-5201 is intact.
   (The alternative Path B — widening `PublicLeaderboardEntry` + a D-5201 amendment + a §21
   four-row update — was rejected in favour of the minimal snapshot-only change.)
2. **Co-op ambiguity is resolved safely.** The board query returns one row per
   competitive_scores row, so a co-op replay both teammates submitted appears as two rows
   sharing a `replay_hash`. The handle fetch includes only UNAMBIGUOUS single-claimed replay
   hashes — a hash claimed by more than one player is dropped, so a row NEVER links to the
   wrong teammate's profile (that row falls back to the neutral label instead).
3. **Unclaimed-handle fallback (recommended default).** A ranked player with no claimed handle
   is never dropped; the row shows the neutral, non-PII label `Anonymous` as plain text (no
   link), and the email-local-part `display_name` is **never emitted** to these boards — closing
   the PII leak. (A claimed handle links to `?profile=<handle_canonical>`, percent-encoded.)
4. **Additive snapshot, no version bump.** The snapshot entry types gain an optional
   `handleCanonical?` (omit-when-absent, appended last), and the `legends-board` client mirror
   (`snapshotClient.ts`) gains the same field in lockstep; `schemaVersion` stays the literal `1`.
   The board's `handle` field now holds the claimed handle or `Anonymous`, not `display_name`.
5. **Scope held.** The Gauntlet board (a team roster, different source), the latent
   NowPlaying / RecentAchievements panels, and the separate MatchResult pipeline are untouched.
   Score computation, ranking, eligibility, and the 5-minute publish cadence are unchanged; no
   `competitive_scores` migration.

**Active 2026-08-21 (WP-579 / EC-614).** Shipped across the server leaderboard/legends layer + the
three legends-board single-player panels + a shared `profileHref` helper. Server legends+leaderboard
tests green (DB-backed skip without `TEST_DATABASE_URL`), legends-board 129→131/0; `pnpm -r --no-bail
test` green across all packages. Allowlist additions surfaced at execution: `leaderboard.types.ts`
(the `ClaimedHandle` type), `legends.publisher.ts` (the Path A wiring), `profileLink.ts`/`.test.ts`
(the 3rd-copy shared helper); `api-endpoints.md` unchanged (Path A). **D-24026 live-verify:
operator-pending** (`User-Visible Surface = legends.legendary-arena.com`; a claimed-handle row links
to `/?profile=<handle>` and an unclaimed row shows `Anonymous`).

### D-24391 — Rogue "Copy Powers" Is a Full Duplicate: Adds the Copied Hero's Printed Attack, Recruit, and Team (Active 2026-08-22 — WP-582 / EC-617)

**Decision.** Rogue's `core/rogue/copy-powers` — *"Play this card as a copy of another Hero you played this turn."* — is a **full duplicate** of the copied Hero, matching the physical Marvel Legendary card (operator confirmation 2026-08-22, reading the card). In addition to the ability re-fire and dual-class grant already shipped under D-24345, `applyCopyPowers` now ALSO grants the copied Hero's **printed attack + recruit** and its **team**.

**Supersedes D-24345 Fork 2.** D-24345 Fork 2 locked *"'Copy' = RE-FIRE the chosen Hero's on-play ability … NOT its printed stats … does NOT re-add the copied Hero's base attack/recruit economy (Fork 2 — ability only)."* That was wrong — the real card is a full duplicate. Every other D-24345 clause stays **Active**: the interactive pending-choice, the dual-class grant, the descriptive-`[hc:X]` parser exclusion, and the instance-id copy-of-self recursion fix are all unchanged. Only Fork 2's "ability only, not stats" clause is superseded.

**Attack + Recruit (the reported defect).** `applyCopyPowers` reads `G.cardStats[chosenHeroId]` (the copied instance's printed stats, keyed by the same copy-suffixed ext_id) and adds them via `addResources(G.turnEconomy, attack, recruit)` — the same call `applyCardPlay` uses for a normal play — on BOTH resolution paths (the 1-eligible auto path and the ≥2 `resolveCopyPowersChoice` path funnel through `applyCopyPowers`). **The double-count is intended:** Copy Powers copies "a Hero you played this turn," so the copied Hero already contributed its own stat when it was played; the copy adds a genuine second instance, so a duplicate legitimately doubles the stat. A null-stat copied Hero (absent `cardStats` entry) adds 0/0 and never throws. Found live: a 2p match where Copy Powers cloned Cyclops' *Unending Energy* and added no attack.

**Team (a new runtime mechanism).** Team was read statically from `G.cardTraits[id].team` at every read site; no runtime team-grant map existed. This introduces a new lazy `G.cardCopiedTeams: Record<CardExtId, string[]>` (undefined by default, created at the grant site in `applyCopyPowers`, never in `Game.setup`, omit-when-empty — mirroring `cardSizeChangingClasses`, D-24074) plus a new pure helper `hero/effectiveTeams.logic.ts` (`getGrantedTeams` / `cardHasTeamWhenPlayed`, the exact mirror of `sizeChanging.logic.ts`). `applyCopyPowers` writes the copied Hero's `cardTraits[chosenHeroId].team` into `cardCopiedTeams[sourceCardId]` (init-if-absent → push-if-not-present; a teamless copy grants nothing — `team` is `string | null`). The hero team-synergy read `requiresTeam` (`heroConditions.evaluate.ts`) is routed through `cardHasTeamWhenPlayed`, preserving its self-exclusion loop, so a Copy Powers card counts as the copied team for a hero team-synergy ability.

**Team-copy reaches only the hero-synergy read (parity with class).** The existing D-24345 class grant reaches only the hero-class read; the six non-hero class reads (villain / mastermind / scheme-twist / tactic / villain-defeat-requirement / UIState) read `cardTraits.heroClass` directly and do NOT consult `cardSizeChangingClasses`. Team-copy mirrors that exactly — wiring only the `requiresTeam` hero-synergy read — so team and class stay **symmetric**. **Non-goal:** full team/class parity across all read sites (for both team and class) is a deferred consistency follow-up, not this fidelity fix.

**Surface.** `applyCopyPowers` (`hero/heroEffects.execute.ts`) gains the economy add + team grant; `types.ts` gains the lazy `cardCopiedTeams` field (and the stale `cardSizeChangingClasses` "read-only at runtime" comment is corrected — D-24345 already writes it at runtime); new `hero/effectiveTeams.logic.ts` + `.test.ts`; `heroConditions.evaluate.ts` routes `requiresTeam` through the helper. **No new move; no new keyword** (the `copy-powers` handler was already registered — `HERO_EFFECT_HANDLERS` / `HERO_KEYWORDS` / `CORE_MOVE_NAMES` counts unchanged); no `data/cards` / marker / hero-mechanic-ledger / effect-index change.

**Determinism.** `G.turnEconomy` is a hashed field — the economy add is a real gameplay change (the intended fix), not a violation. The new `cardCopiedTeams` map is lazy / omit-when-empty. No committed fixture plays Copy Powers (the sole complete-game fixture is `core/dr-doom`), so `finalStateHash` / `PRE_WP080_HASH` are byte-identical — verified at execution (2837/0 including the replay/sentinel suites; no re-pin). Not a snapshot field.

_Active 2026-08-22 — landed at WP-582 execution (EC-617). Supersedes D-24345 Fork 2 (D-24345 otherwise Active). No move/keyword count change; no hashed-oracle re-pin (turnEconomy delta unexercised by any committed fixture; `cardCopiedTeams` lazy/omit-when-empty). Mutation-verified: reverting the economy add + `requiresTeam` routing fails the new economy / team / requiresTeam tests. **D-24026 live-verify: VERIFIED 2026-08-22** — a real 2p Red Skull / Midtown Bank Robbery match on the deployed build (diagnostics `gitSha 4f81132` = PR #1560 merge) played Copy Powers copying God of Thunder: the log shows `gained +0 attack and +5 recruit from copying God of Thunder` (the printed +5 recruit duplicated) plus the ability re-fire (`can spend Recruit as Attack this turn`) — full duplicate confirmed._

### D-24392 — Endgame Score Breakdown + Grade Badge (Active 2026-08-22 — WP-583 / EC-618)

**Decision.** The endgame screen surfaces (a) the full competitive-score **component breakdown** (rounds, bystanders rescued, VP, per-event penalties, PAR) and (b) a **grade badge** (Legendary / A / B / C / D / F) banded from the PAR-relative `finalScore`. This is a follow-up to WP-578 (which showed only the two totals) and closes the legibility gap surfaced by a real match: the player couldn't see WHERE the score came from or HOW good it is.

**Breakdown is client-only — the data was already on the wire.** The server already calls `buildScoreBreakdown`, persists `score_breakdown` (jsonb, migration 007), and returns the full `ScoreBreakdown` inside `record.scoreBreakdown` from BOTH `POST /api/competition/scores` and `GET /api/me/scores`. The client `MyCompetitiveScore` type (`apps/arena-client/src/lib/api/competitionApi.ts`, declared locally by structural compatibility — no engine/server import) merely omitted the field. So this WP **extends the client type** (a local `CompetitiveScoreBreakdown` shape) and renders it **verbatim** in `EndgameSummary.vue` — never recomputed client-side (WP-578 / D-24387 preserved). **No server / persistence / migration change.**

**Grade is a shared engine enum; the word is client copy.** A new pure helper `gradeForFinalScore(finalScore): ScoreGrade` + `ScoreGrade` union + `SCORE_GRADES` drift-pinned canonical array in `packages/game-engine/src/scoring/parScoring.grade.ts`, barrel-exported — mirroring `menaceTierFor` / `MENACE_TIERS` (D-24366). Per the D-24367 / D-24371 boundary, the engine ships the **enum** (`'legendary' | 'a' | 'b' | 'c' | 'd' | 'f'`) and the client owns the player-facing **word** ("Legendary" replaces the conventional "S" elite rank — operator decision) in `apps/arena-client/src/vfx/gradeDisplay.ts`, beside `menaceDisplay.ts`. Placing the grade in the engine (not client-only) keeps a future leaderboard/legends grade badge on ONE threshold table with no drift.

**Grade bands** on `finalScore` (centesimal integer, lower = better, 0 = PAR), inclusive-upper ceilings: `<= -1000 legendary`, `<= -300 a`, `<= 300 b`, `<= 800 c`, `<= 1800 d`, else `f` (the live example `1220 → d`). Operator-approved at draft, **tunable** via the helper's threshold constants — a display-legibility choice, not a scoring-formula change.

**Surface.** game-engine: `scoring/parScoring.grade.ts` (new) + barrel export + `parScoring.grade.test.ts` (runtime drift pin + 14 band-boundary cases). arena-client: `competitionApi.ts` (+ local `scoreBreakdown` shape), `EndgameSummary.vue` (breakdown `<dl>` + grade badge; a separate value import of `gradeForFinalScore` since the existing engine import was `import type`), `vfx/gradeDisplay.ts` (new; the display copy) + tests. **Endgame screen only** — a leaderboard/legends grade badge is a deferred follow-up (the shared engine helper makes it a trivial later reuse). Accessible: the badge conveys meaning by text + `aria-label`, not colour alone (Vision §17).

**Determinism.** `gradeForFinalScore` is a pure function of one number — not stored in `G`, no hashed field, no fixture. The client change is display-only over already-served data. `finalStateHash` / `PRE_WP080_HASH` byte-identical (verified: engine 2837 → 2852 all pass, replay/sentinel green). No snapshot / DB / migration change; barrel export is additive.

_Active 2026-08-22 — landed at WP-583 execution (EC-618). Client-only display + one pure additive engine helper; no server/persistence/hash change. Engine 2837 → 2852 / 0 (+15 grade tests incl. runtime drift pin); arena-client 1372 / 0; `vue-tsc` clean; `pnpm -r --no-bail test` green. Hard-deps WP-578 / D-24387 (endgame score) + WP-557 / D-24366 (`menaceTierFor` band/copy-boundary pattern). D-24026 live-verify operator-pending (`User-Visible Surface = play.legendary-arena.com`; finish a ranked match and read the breakdown + grade)._

### D-24393 — Endgame Score Rendered as a Worked Calculation (Formula-First) (Active 2026-08-22 — WP-584 / EC-619)

**Decision.** The endgame competitive score, which WP-583 showed as a flat component list, is rendered as a **worked solution** — a symbolic formula, the same formula with the match's values substituted, the weighted products summed, and the result; then `Final = Raw − PAR → Grade`. This closes the legibility gap the operator raised on the WP-583 output: the components were listed but the arithmetic was not shown ("show the work, like grading a student's work").

**Operator design choices (confirmed at draft via an inline mockup).** (1) **Formula-first** — lead with the symbolic formula line `Raw = (Rounds × 50) + Penalties − (Bystanders × 200) − (VP × 10)`, then the substituted line, then products, then the result. (2) **Whole numbers** — the centesimal integers already shown elsewhere on the panel (Raw 20, Final 320); no ÷100.

**Weights are DERIVED, never hardcoded.** The engine's scoring weights are not exposed to the client. To show `× 50` etc. honestly, the helper (`apps/arena-client/src/vfx/scoreCalcDisplay.ts`) derives each per-term weight as `product ÷ count` from the breakdown itself (guarded `count > 0`); a zero-count term shows its `0` product with no invented weight. So the shown formula can never drift from the engine's real weights — the same no-duplication discipline as the D-24367 grade/menace copy boundary. Values are rendered **verbatim** from `record.scoreBreakdown` (never recomputed — WP-578 / D-24387 preserved).

**Surface.** arena-client ONLY: a new pure `vfx/scoreCalcDisplay.ts` (`buildWorkedScoreCalc`) + `EndgameSummary.vue` replacing WP-583's flat `.score-breakdown` `<dl>` with the worked-calc block (givens + Raw formula/substituted/products/result + Final = Raw − PAR → grade) + tests. `competitionApi.ts` UNCHANGED (WP-583's `scoreBreakdown` shape already carries every field). **No engine / server / persistence / migration / hash change** — a pure client display reformat. Accessible: each worked line carries an `aria-label`; meaning is in the text, not colour. Extends D-24392's endgame surface; leaderboard/legends grade badge remains the deferred follow-up.

_Active 2026-08-22 — landed at WP-584 execution (EC-619). Arena-client only; no engine/server/persistence/hash change (both oracles untouched). New helper `vfx/scoreCalcDisplay.ts` + `EndgameSummary.vue` reformat; arena-client 1372 → 1378 / 0 (+6 net: worked-calc + helper tests replace the WP-583 flat-list test); `vue-tsc` clean; `pnpm -r --no-bail test` green. Hard-deps WP-583 / D-24392 (the breakdown reformatted) + WP-578 / D-24387 (the server record). D-24026 live-verify operator-pending (`User-Visible Surface = play.legendary-arena.com`; finish a ranked match and read the worked calculation)._

### D-24394 — Rulebook-Faithful Scoring: Remove the Per-Round Cost (Active 2026-08-22 — WP-585 / EC-620)

**Decision.** The competitive RawScore no longer includes a per-round cost. The Marvel Legendary v23 rulebook's "Scoring" section (verified against `docs/Marvel Legendary Universal Rules v23.txt`) subtracts only **−4 per Bystander lost, −3 per Scheme/Plot Twist, −1 per Villain escaped** (the 4:3:1 anchor) and has **no round/turn penalty** — Scheme Twists are its length proxy. LA had layered a `roundCost` (50/round) on top, double-counting length. That term is **removed**:

```
RawScore = Penalties − (BP × bystanderReward) − (VP × vpReward)
```

Operator decision ("option 1, rulebook-purist," 2026-08-22) after inspecting the printed rulebook, prompted by questioning whether the Scheme-Twist penalty was luck; the rulebook check found the reverse — twists are the canonical length signal and the LA round cost was the redundant addition.

**Full removal.** `ScoringWeights.roundCost`, `ParBaseline.roundsPar`, and `ScoreBreakdown.weightedRoundCost` are deleted (chosen over zero-weighting, which would leave dead config + a weakened validation invariant + a misleading `(Rounds × 0)` display). `ScoringInputs.rounds` is **kept as informational** (shown as an endgame given, never scored; `computeParScore` sets `rounds: 0`). The bystander/VP rewards and all penalty weights are **unchanged** — the deliberate LA moral-hierarchy (Vision 20-26) stays; only the redundant round cost goes.

**Versions bumped (both).** `scoringConfigVersion 2→3` (any weight/config change bumps it, docs/12 calibration invariant) and `rawScoreSemanticsVersion 1→2` (removing a whole term is a formula-SHAPE change). Existing `legendary.competitive_scores` rows pin their own `par_version` / `scoring_config_version` / `score_breakdown` and are never re-scored (idempotency fast-path) — **no retroactive invalidation**; the `rawScoreSemanticsVersion` bump is the designed filter distinguishing old (v1-semantics) from new (v2-semantics) entries.

**Seed PAR artifacts regenerated.** `data/par/seed/v1/**` (128 + index) and `data/scoring-configs/**` (128) regenerated: every `parValue` drops by its old `roundsPar × 50`, every `artifactHash` recomputes. Regenerated **v1 in place** (write-once guard required `rm` first) — an acceptable exception to the `12.1` immutability doctrine because this is a pre-release, **uncalibrated** seed that Phase-2 simulation will replace; the version pins record the change. The server's defense-in-depth `computeParScore(config) === parValue` check holds because both sides recompute from the regenerated artifact (a stale artifact would fail-close every live submission — regeneration is mandatory).

**Surface.** `scoring/parScoring.types.ts` + `parScoring.logic.ts` + `simulation/par.storage.ts` (semantics const + validator/type-guard); `scripts/generate-seed-par.mjs` (weights/baseline/versions); regenerated artifacts; arena-client `competitionApi.ts` + `vfx/scoreCalcDisplay.ts` (drop the round term, keep "Rounds" as a given); `docs/12-SCORING-REFERENCE.md`; engine/arena-client/server test fixtures. **No `apps/server` route/library change** (the persisted `score_breakdown` jsonb narrows a field harmlessly).

**Determinism.** Scoring is server-side, end-of-match, and NOT part of the game-state hash — no `finalStateHash` / `PRE_WP080_HASH` re-pin (verified: engine replay/sentinel suites green). PAR artifact hashes change (expected, separate). No `G` / move / fixture touched.

_Active 2026-08-22 — landed at WP-585 execution (EC-620). Full removal of roundCost/roundsPar/weightedRoundCost; both version pins bumped; 128 seed artifacts + 128 scoring-configs regenerated @ scoringConfigVersion 3 / rawScoreSemanticsVersion 2; no game-state-hash re-pin. Engine 2852→2851/0 (round-monotonicity test replaced by a rounds-invariance test); arena-client + server green; `pnpm -r --no-bail test` green. Hard-deps WP-584/D-24393 + WP-422/D-24242 + WP-531/D-24342. D-24026 live-verify operator-pending (`User-Visible Surface = play.legendary-arena.com`; endgame worked calc has no round-cost line, score reflects the rulebook penalties)._

### D-24395 — Fix the Bystander-Rescued Undercount in Competitive Scoring (Active 2026-08-22 — WP-586 / EC-621)

**Problem.** The competitive score undercounted rescued Bystanders. A Bystander reaches a victory pile from **two** ext-id sources: villain-deck bystanders (`bystander-villain-deck-NN`, registered in `G.villainDeckCardTypes` as `bystander`) and supply-pile bystanders (`BYSTANDER_EXT_ID` = `pile-bystander`, attached to Villains/Masterminds and awarded to a victory pile on defeat/rescue, **never** registered in `villainDeckCardTypes`). The scoring-input derivations `deriveScoringInputs` (`scoring/parScoring.logic.ts`) and `deriveScoringInputsFromFinalState` (`simulation/par.aggregator.ts`) tested only `villainDeckCardTypes[id] === 'bystander'`, so they silently dropped every supply-pile Bystander from both `bystandersRescued` (a reward) and `bystanderLost` (a penalty). `computeFinalScores` (VP) and `countBystandersRescued` (HUD) already used the correct dual test, so the three surfaces disagreed — observed live: ~8 credited against a victory pile / HUD of 18–26, mis-grading a Legendary run as C.

**Decision.** Extract one exported predicate `isBystanderCard(gameState, cardExtId)` in `scoring/scoring.logic.ts` (`villainDeckCardTypes[id] === 'bystander' || id === BYSTANDER_EXT_ID`) as the **single source of truth** for "Bystander in a pile," and route all six count sites through it: `computeFinalScores`, `countBystandersRescued`, and both `bystandersRescued` + `bystanderLost` loops in each of `deriveScoringInputs` and `deriveScoringInputsFromFinalState`.

1. **Live and PAR-calibration paths share the predicate.** A narrow predicate on one side but not the other would systematically skew PAR vs the live score on bystander-heavy scenarios; sharing one helper makes them symmetric by construction.
2. **No game-state-hash re-pin.** Scoring is server-side, end-of-match, and derived from terminal `G`; the fix adds no `G` field, so `finalStateHash` / `PRE_WP080_HASH` are byte-unchanged (verified: the engine replay/sentinel suites stay green).
3. **No weight / formula / PAR-artifact change.** This corrects a counting bug in the derivation, not the scoring weights or the seed PAR baselines; no `par:seed:generate` regeneration is needed.
4. **No retroactive recompute.** Existing `legendary.competitive_scores` rows keep their pinned `score_breakdown` (the D-24394 / WP-585 no-retroactive-invalidation precedent); only new submissions score correctly.

**Scope guard.** The `villainDeck.reveal.ts` `cardType === 'bystander'` branch (reveal handling) and the `ai.competent.ts` `keyword === 'bystander'` check (AI hint) are a different concern (villain-deck reveal / AI heuristics) and correctly stay narrow — only victory-pile/escaped-pile **count** sites route through `isBystanderCard`.

**Surface.** `scoring/scoring.logic.ts` (new exported `isBystanderCard` + `computeFinalScores` refactor); `scoring/parScoring.logic.ts` (rescued + lost loops); `simulation/par.aggregator.ts` (rescued + lost loops + import); `ui/uiState.build.ts` (`countBystandersRescued` refactor; drops the now-unused `BYSTANDER_EXT_ID` value import); `scoring/parScoring.logic.test.ts` (+3 regression tests). **No `apps/server` route/library change** (the derivation is internal to the engine; the returned `bystandersRescued` / `bystanderLost` fields are unchanged in shape, now correctly valued).

_Active 2026-08-22 — landed at WP-586 execution (EC-621). One shared `isBystanderCard` predicate; all six count sites routed through it; live + PAR symmetric; no game-state-hash re-pin; no retroactive recompute. Engine 2852→2855/0 (+3 regression tests). Hard-deps WP-585/D-24394 + WP-422/D-24242 + the WP-017 supply-pile bystander model. D-24026 live-verify operator-pending (`User-Visible Surface = play.legendary-arena.com`; endgame "Bystanders rescued" + score match the HUD / victory pile)._

### D-24396 — Endgame PAR Derivation, Grade Scale, and Named Penalties (Active 2026-08-22 — WP-587 / EC-622)

**Problem.** The endgame screen showed the competitive score, its worked raw-score calculation, and a grade badge, but not how PAR was derived (the operator asked "where did −1150 come from?"), what score each grade needs, or which penalties the worked calc summed (it read "(7 × 300)", not "7 scheme twists").

**Decision.** Add the score-legibility surface as a cross-layer change — the engine exposes the data, the arena-client renders it.

1. **`ScoreBreakdown.parBaseline`.** `buildScoreBreakdown` field-copies the scenario `ParBaseline` (`bystandersPar` / `victoryPointsPar` / `escapesPar`) into the returned breakdown (no alias — the JSON-serializable, no-shared-reference invariant, D-2801 / D-4806). A derived, display-only projection; it never re-enters scoring. The server persists and returns the whole breakdown as `score_breakdown` jsonb verbatim (`scoreBreakdown: row.score_breakdown`), so there is **no server code change**, and rows persisted before WP-587 simply lack the field — the client type marks it optional and the PAR-derivation block is omitted for them.
2. **`SCORE_GRADE_BANDS` is the single source of truth.** `{ grade, maxFinalScore }` with inclusive-upper ceilings (`null` on the worst, unbounded band), grades in `SCORE_GRADES` order, ceilings ascending; `gradeForFinalScore` iterates it. Runtime drift-pinned (WP-563 rule) against `SCORE_GRADES` and the boundary table, so the classifier and the displayed scale can never disagree. Barrel-exported with `ScoreGradeBand`.
3. **The client owns all copy.** Every player-facing word (grade labels), grade-range string, penalty name, and PAR-derivation string is built in `apps/arena-client` (`gradeDisplay`, `scoreCalcDisplay`) — the no-copy-in-`packages/` boundary (D-24392 / D-24367). The engine ships only numbers and enums.
4. **The PAR-derivation never fabricates a weight.** PAR and the raw score share the config weights, so the PAR line reuses the per-unit weights derived from the match; a weight not derivable from the match (e.g. the escape penalty weight when the match had 0 escapes) is shown symbolically ("escape penalty"), and the PAR value itself is always rendered verbatim from the breakdown.
5. **No version bump, no hash re-pin.** Additive display data — no `scoringConfigVersion` bump (no formula/weight change) and no `finalStateHash` / `PRE_WP080_HASH` re-pin (scoring is server-side, end-of-match, and adds no `G` field; verified by the green replay/sentinel suites). Existing `competitive_scores` rows are not recomputed.

**Surface.** `scoring/parScoring.grade.ts` (`SCORE_GRADE_BANDS` + `gradeForFinalScore` refactor), `scoring/parScoring.types.ts` (`ScoreBreakdown.parBaseline`), `scoring/parScoring.logic.ts` (copy in `buildScoreBreakdown`), `index.ts` (barrel); arena-client `lib/api/competitionApi.ts` (optional `parBaseline`), `vfx/scoreCalcDisplay.ts` (named penalties + `buildParDerivation`), `vfx/gradeDisplay.ts` (`buildGradeScale`), `components/hud/EndgameSummary.vue` (render). **No `apps/server` route/library change** (jsonb pass-through; the returned breakdown widens by one optional field).

_Active 2026-08-22 — landed at WP-587 execution (EC-622). Engine exposes parBaseline + SCORE_GRADE_BANDS; arena-client renders PAR derivation, grade scale, and named penalties; no server change; no scoringConfigVersion bump; no game-state-hash re-pin. Engine 2855→2858/0 (+3 tests); arena-client 1372→1389/0 (vue-tsc clean). Layout approved via a show_widget mockup before build. Hard-deps WP-583/D-24392 + WP-584/D-24393 + WP-585/D-24394 + WP-586/D-24395. D-24026 live-verify operator-pending (`User-Visible Surface = play.legendary-arena.com`; endgame shows the PAR derivation, the grade scale with your row marked, and named penalties)._

### D-24397 — Endgame Report Card: Per-Player Split, PAR Basis, Colour-Coded Grade Scale (Active 2026-08-22 — WP-588 / EC-623)

**Problem.** Three operator requests for the endgame report card (the WP-587 surface): break the raw-score reward terms down per player; state what PAR is based on; make the grade scale wider and colour-coded.

**Decision.** Cross-layer display refinements — the engine adds the per-player data, the arena-client renders all three.

1. **Per-player split.** `ScoringInputs` gains an optional `perPlayer` (`PlayerScoringContribution` = `{playerId, victoryPoints, bystandersRescued}`), populated in `deriveScoringInputs` from terminal `G`: VP is each player's `totalVP` (from `computeFinalScores`, sorted by playerId); bystanders are re-counted from that player's own victory pile via the shared `isBystanderCard` predicate (WP-586). `buildScoreBreakdown` deep-copies it (no alias — the JSON-serializable, no-shared-reference invariant, D-2801 / D-4806). The competitive score REMAINS a shared-team score (D-4803); `perPlayer` is a display-only reconciliation that **sums to** the team `victoryPoints` + `bystandersRescued` and never changes the score. Optional: the synthetic inputs `computeParScore` builds have no players, and rows persisted before WP-588 carry none — the report card then shows only the team totals.
2. **PAR basis.** The endgame names what sets PAR — verified against the code, not assumed: PAR is keyed on the `ScenarioKey` (`scheme::mastermind::sorted-villain-groups`, `parScoring.keys.ts:buildScenarioKey`) and calibrated by `composeScenarioDifficulty` (`0.40·mastermind + 0.40·scheme + 0.20·avg(villains)`, `generate-seed-par.mjs`). So it is set by the scheme, mastermind, and villain groups, **explicitly not henchmen** (the operator asked "…and henchmen, right?"; the honest, code-checked answer is no). Client copy only (no copy in `packages/`).
3. **Grade scale.** Rendered as a horizontal, colour-coded strip (one cell per `SCORE_GRADE_BANDS` entry, tinted its grade colour, the earned cell emphasised) rather than the WP-587 vertical list. Colour is REINFORCEMENT: the current cell also carries a text marker ("your score") + `aria-current`, preserving the D-24392 not-colour-alone rule. The client owns the colours and words.

**Determinism.** `perPlayer` is derived from terminal `G` and adds no `G` field, so `finalStateHash` / `PRE_WP080_HASH` are byte-unchanged (verified by the green replay/sentinel suites). No `scoringConfigVersion` bump (additive display data). The server returns the breakdown jsonb verbatim, so there is **no server code change**.

**Surface.** `scoring/parScoring.types.ts` (`PlayerScoringContribution` + `ScoringInputs.perPlayer`), `scoring/parScoring.logic.ts` (populate in `deriveScoringInputs`, deep-copy in `buildScoreBreakdown`), `index.ts` (barrel); arena-client `lib/api/competitionApi.ts` (`CompetitivePlayerContribution` + optional `perPlayer`), `vfx/scoreCalcDisplay.ts` (`buildPerPlayerSplit`, Player-N labels), `components/hud/EndgameSummary.vue` (per-player block, PAR-basis line, horizontal colour strip). **No `apps/server` route/library change** (jsonb pass-through).

_Active 2026-08-22 — landed at WP-588 execution (EC-623). Optional per-player split that sums to the team totals (score stays team-level); PAR-basis copy code-verified (scheme + mastermind + villain groups, not henchmen); horizontal colour-coded grade strip with the earned cell text-marked. No server change; no scoringConfigVersion bump; no game-state-hash re-pin. Engine 2858→2860/0; arena-client 1389→1394/0. Hard-deps WP-587/D-24396 + WP-586/D-24395 + WP-020 (computeFinalScores). D-24026 live-verify operator-pending (`User-Visible Surface = play.legendary-arena.com`; a 2p report card shows per-player VP + bystanders, the colour-coded grade strip with your cell marked, and the PAR-basis line)._

### D-24398 — Optional-KO-Reward: Icon-Reward Fidelity (Parser Suppression + Marker Backfill) (Active 2026-08-23 — WP-589 / EC-624)

**Problem.** A family of "You may KO a card from your hand or discard pile. If you do, you get +N[resource]" Heroes — core Rogue **Energy Drain** the operator-reported case — is authored in card data with the KO prose and the reward icon (`+N[icon:recruit|attack]`) but WITHOUT the `[keyword:optional-ko-reward:<reward>:N]` marker its sibling Dangerous Rescue carries. With no marker, `heroAbility.setup.ts` extracts only the icon (Step 2b/3 → a plain `recruit`/`attack` effect) and drops the entire "you may KO … if you do" clause: the ability becomes an UNCONDITIONAL resource grant, the player is never offered the KO, and the reward lands for free. Observed in a real 2p Red Skull / Midtown match (`gained +1 recruit from Energy Drain`, no KO prompt). A data-only fix is unsafe: the parser has no icon-suppression for `optional-ko-reward`, so adding the marker to a line that also carries the reward icon emits BOTH the plain grant AND the KO-gated reward — a double-grant already latent in `co2e` Energy Drain 2e.

**Decision.** Two coupled changes, shipped together.

1. **Marker backfill (data).** Add the missing `[keyword:optional-ko-reward:<reward>:N]` markers to the 6 affected lines via `scripts/convert-cards/inputs/hero-ability-markers.json` (the existing curated map), then regenerate `data/cards/*.json`. Closed set: `core` rogue/energy-drain (recruit:1); `ssw1` apocalyptic-kitty-pryde/phase-out (attack:1), dr-strange/trust-me-im-a-doctor (recruit:1), namor-the-sub-mariner/feed-the-sharks (draw:1); `ssw2` black-swan/witness-the-end (draw:1), elsa-bloodstone/bloodstone-pendant (recruit:1). The applier's `VALID_TOKEN_PATTERN` already whitelists the token, so `apply-hero-ability-markers.mjs` is unchanged. `<reward>` ∈ the seeded set { rescue, draw, attack, recruit }; unseeded-reward KO lines (Shard, New-Recruit, cost-scaled) stay unmarked (honest-partial). `co2e` needs no data change (already marked).

2. **Parser icon-suppression (engine).** In `heroAbility.setup.ts`, after Step 4 dedup, when a line emitted an `optional-ko-reward` effect whose `rewardType` is a keyword the icon pass can also produce (`attack`/`recruit`), drop that plain keyword from `uniqueKeywords` and delete its magnitude — so only the KO-gated reward remains. This mirrors the D-24148 (`shuffle-discard-empty-reward`) and D-24016 (`attack-per-count`) icon-suppression precedents. It is a **no-op** for `draw`/`rescue` rewards (which never produce a plain icon keyword), so pre-existing marked cards — Dangerous Rescue — are byte-identical. Bound (inherited from the D-24148 precedent): a line legitimately carrying BOTH a standalone icon grant and an `optional-ko-reward` of the same resource would lose the standalone; no such line exists in the corpus.

The Covert / team / Spectrum class-synergy gates on these lines are faithful and untouched — this WP does not change condition parsing. The pending-choice UX, bot resolution, and the `resolveOptionalKoReward` move (WP-248/WP-249 / D-24019) are reused as-is.

**Determinism.** No new `G` field — `PendingOptionalKoReward` already exists. Hero-effect evaluation DOES change for the swept cards, so a reference-match `finalStateHash` / sentinel could move IF a swept card appears in a pinned fixture. Execution is scaffold-first: prototype the suppression block + the core Energy Drain marker and run the engine suite + replay/sentinel BEFORE the full sweep; a moved hash oracle is assessed (and only deliberately re-pinned) rather than blanket-accepted.

**Surface.** `packages/game-engine/src/setup/heroAbility.setup.ts` (suppression block) + `heroAbility.setup.test.ts` (suppression + park pins); `scripts/convert-cards/inputs/hero-ability-markers.json` (6 rows); regenerated `data/cards/{core,ssw1,ssw2}.json` (marker append only). No `apply-hero-ability-markers.mjs`, no `apps/server`, no `apps/*` client change.

_Active 2026-08-23 — landed at WP-589 execution (EC-624). Parser icon-suppression added (mirrors D-24148/D-24016); 6 markers backfilled (core Energy Drain + ssw1×3 + ssw2×2); data + card-derived feeds regenerated (bounded). Engine 2860→2863/0 (+3 suppression pins); effect-index/ledger:heroes/mechanics:metadata :check green; pnpm -r --no-bail test green; finalStateHash + replay/sentinel byte-unchanged (no new G field); co2e double-grant corrected by the parser fix (no co2e data change); Covert/team/Spectrum gate untouched. Hard-deps WP-248 / D-24019 + WP-249. D-24026 live-verify CONFIRMED 2026-08-23 (on `play.legendary-arena.com` at gitSha `6e99f0b`, a 2p Red Skull / Midtown match: Energy Drain offers + resolves the KO-a-card choice with the Covert synergy active, e.g. `KO'd Wound (pile-wound) from their discard pile for Energy Drain's ability` → `gained +1 recruit`)._

### D-24399 — Log the Silent KO in `resolveOptionalKoReward` (Active 2026-08-23 — WP-590 / EC-625)

**Problem.** `resolveOptionalKoReward` (WP-248 / D-24019) resolves the "you may KO a card from your hand or discard pile; if you do, <reward>" choice by KO'ing the player's chosen card (Step 5, `G.ko = koCard(...)`) and then dispatching the reward (Step 6). The reward logs itself (rescue / draw / attack / recruit), but the KO does not — so the game log records the payoff with no line naming the card that was spent to earn it. A player (or a diagnostics reviewer) reading the log sees a card leave their hand/discard with no explanation.

**Decision.** Emit exactly one game-log line for the KO cost. In Step 5, after the zone shortening + `koCard`, and BEFORE the Step-6 reward dispatch, call `pushLog(G, …, 'neutral')` naming (a) the KO'd card via `formatCardRef(G.cardDisplayData, targetCardId)`, (b) its human zone label (`hand` → "their hand", `discard` → "their discard pile"), and (c) the source ability via `formatCardRef(G.cardDisplayData, front.sourceCardId)`. Outcome `neutral` — it is a cost the player paid, mirroring the Master Strike KO and `heroEffectKo` phrasing, not the reward's `applied`. The decline path (`{ decline: true }`) emits no KO line. No change to the KO/reward mechanics, ordering, atomicity, seeded-reward set, or `PendingOptionalKoReward`.

**Determinism.** `hashGameState` (→ `finalStateHash`) excludes `messages`, so the game-state hash is byte-unchanged. `computeStateHash` (→ the replay hash / `PRE_WP080_HASH`) KEEPS `messages` hashed (the exclusion is diagnostics-only, WP-488), so a pinned reference replay that executes a `resolveOptionalKoReward` KO-with-selection would shift the replay hash. If so, it is re-pinned as a **log-only** change — identical moves and gameplay, only the observable `messages` grew — with the reason recorded. Execution is scaffold-first: the re-pin question is answered by running the replay/sentinel suites, never by assertion.

**Surface.** `packages/game-engine/src/moves/optionalKoReward.resolve.ts` (two imports + one Step-5 `pushLog`) + `optionalKoReward.resolve.test.ts` (KO-line + decline-no-line assertions); conditionally the pinned replay/sentinel hash constant. No client/server/registry change.

_Active 2026-08-23 — landed at WP-590 execution (EC-625). One Step-5 `pushLog` (imports `pushLog` + `formatCardRef`) names the KO'd card + zone + source ability, outcome `neutral`, before the Step-6 reward dispatch; decline logs none. Engine 2860→2863/0 (+3 pins); no mechanics/ordering change; no new `G` field; `finalStateHash` byte-unchanged (messages excluded from `hashGameState`); replay/sentinel byte-unchanged — the sole pinned replay records no `resolveOptionalKoReward` move, so no re-pin. Hard-dep WP-248 / D-24019. D-24026 live-verify CONFIRMED 2026-08-23 (on `play.legendary-arena.com` at gitSha `6e99f0b`, a 2p Red Skull / Midtown match: the KO of the spent card is named in the log before the reward line, e.g. `Player 0 KO'd Wound (pile-wound) from their discard pile for Energy Drain's ability`)._

### D-24400 — Interim Scheme-Aware PAR Recalibration (Active 2026-08-23 — WP-591 / EC-626)

**Problem.** The competitive PAR was uncalibrated and scheme-BLIND (`bystandersPar = clamp(2, 8, 8 − ⌈D/2⌉)`), but bystander rescues are scheme-DRIVEN — validated from 13 real-game diagnostics (Midtown Bank Robbery 24-37 vs Cosmic Cube 3-4). So the single PAR (−1150) made flood schemes pin at Legendary AND made light-scheme WINS grade F.

**Why interim (simulation deferred).** VISION §26 Phase-2 simulation calibration is the real answer, but an empirical spike (`generateScenarioPar` on the real Midtown/Red Skull board) showed the competent heuristic AI is too weak to be a valid competent-play reference — its 55th-percentile game is near break-even (~0 to −1400 raw) vs a competent human's −5170. Calibrating to it would set PAR ~0 (easier than today). Strengthening the AI is a separate parallel arc; this decision records the interim.

**Decision.**
1. **Scheme-aware baselines.** `baselineForScenario(schemeSlug, difficulty, playerCount)` (the generator) replaces the flat template with per-scheme profiles anchored to the observed competent-win medians (structural estimates for Killbots / Portals / Legacy Virus / Negative Zone). The scheme sets bystander + twist expectations; player count scales the reward totals; difficulty mildly modulates VP + escapes.
2. **Physical baselines (operator option A).** `ParBaseline` gains `schemeTwistsPar` + `bystandersLostPar`, and `computeParScore` subtracts those penalties, so PAR shares the full penalty footing with the raw score and the baseline stays physically meaningful (the WP-587 endgame PAR-derivation display stays honest — it now shows the twist term).
3. **Loss penalty (grade-by-margin).** `computeRawScore` adds a flat `LOSS_PENALTY` (6000 centesimal) when `ScoringInputs.matchLost` is true (derived from `evaluateEndgame(...).outcome === 'scheme-wins'`), so a bystander-heavy loss grades D/F and can never out-grade a competent win. Exposed as `ScoreBreakdown.weightedLossPenalty`. Operator chose grade-by-margin over an auto-F.
4. **Retuned grade bands.** `SCORE_GRADE_BANDS`: Legendary ≤ −2000, A ≤ −700, B ≤ 700, C ≤ 2000, D ≤ 4000, F — wider than WP-583's (a bystander is worth 200, so the old ±300 bands flipped a grade per ~1.5 bystanders). Validated against all 13 real anchor games (operator target: solid win B, exceptional A/Legendary).
5. **Versions + no retroactive invalidation.** `scoringConfigVersion 3→4` + `rawScoreSemanticsVersion 2→3` (a formula-shape change); existing `competitive_scores` rows keep their pinned versions. 128 seed artifacts + configs regenerated (`computeParScore === parValue` holds).
6. **Determinism.** Scoring is server-side, end-of-match, and adds no `G` field → `finalStateHash` / `PRE_WP080_HASH` byte-unchanged (verified by the green replay/sentinel suites). `deriveScoringInputs` sets `matchLost` internally, so there is no `apps/server` route change (jsonb pass-through). PAR artifact hashes recompute (expected).

**Surface.** `scoring/parScoring.types.ts`, `scoring/parScoring.logic.ts`, `scoring/parScoring.grade.ts`, `simulation/par.aggregator.ts`, `simulation/par.storage.ts`; `scripts/generate-seed-par.mjs` + `scripts/extract-par-anchors.mjs` (new); regenerated `data/par/seed/v1/**` + `data/scoring-configs/**`; arena-client `lib/api/competitionApi.ts`, `vfx/scoreCalcDisplay.ts`, `components/hud/EndgameSummary.vue`; `docs/12-SCORING-REFERENCE.md`. No `apps/server` route/library change.

_Active 2026-08-23 — landed at WP-591 execution (EC-626). Scheme-aware physical baselines from 13 real-game anchors; twist-aware PAR; loss penalty by margin; retuned bands; versions 4/3; 128 regenerated; no game-state-hash re-pin; no server route change; no retroactive invalidation. Engine 2860→2863/0; arena-client 1394→1396/0. EXPLICITLY INTERIM: simulation calibration (VISION §26 Phase-2) supersedes this once the competent AI is strong enough to be a valid reference. Hard-deps WP-585..588. D-24026 live-verify operator-pending (`play.legendary-arena.com`; flood + light scheme grades sensible)._

### D-24401 — Rogue "Steal Abilities": Discard-Top-and-Copy Hero Ability (Active 2026-08-23 — WP-592 / EC-627)

**Problem.** Rogue's `core/rogue/steal-abilities` ("Each player discards the top card of their deck. Play a copy of each of those cards.", cost 8, printed +4 attack, `hc:strength`) was UNIMPLEMENTED — surfaced from Jeff's live 2-player Red Skull / Midtown Bank Robbery game (turn 24, log `24.2.9`: the card applied only its printed +4 attack; the discard-and-copy ability was a silent no-op). Root cause (grep-confirmed): NO `[keyword:…]` marker in `hero-ability-markers.json` and NO handler in `heroEffects.execute.ts`, so the ability text was a keyword-less descriptor silently dropped (the D-24266 pattern). WP-535 and WP-582 both deferred it as "a related, harder copy mechanic."

**Decision.** A new `steal-abilities` HeroKeyword + a DETERMINISTIC, SYNCHRONOUS `heroEffectStealAbilities` handler.

1. **No new pending type / `G` field / move.** The handler parks NO `Pending*Choice` of its own → NO block-all-guard change, NO `game.ts` move registration, NO `game.test.ts` move-count change, NO `ai.legalMoves.ts` change, NO `uiState.*` change, NO arena-client change. Any interactive choice comes only from a COPIED card's existing keyword handler, which already owns its pending type / projection / prompt / guard.
2. **Discard phase.** Every player, in `Object.keys(G.playerZones).sort()` seat order, discards the top card of their deck to their OWN discard pile; an empty deck reshuffles the discard first (`reshuffleDiscardIntoDeck`, the D-24285 standard); a player with no cards anywhere discards nothing (logged).
3. **Copy phase.** The Steal Abilities player plays a copy of each discarded card in seat order = its printed economy (`G.cardStats` attack/recruit → `G.turnEconomy`; starters carry entries, Wounds carry none → a copied Wound adds 0/0) PLUS a re-fire of its on-play ability via the reentrant `executeHeroEffects`, threading the FULL move-context wrapper so a copied draw/reshuffle replays from `ctx.random` (mirrors `applyCopyPowers`).
4. **Ephemeral copies.** The copies enter no zone (the real discarded cards stay in their owners' discard piles), never call `applyCardPlay`, never mutate `cardTraits`, and grant Steal Abilities NO class/team — a DELIBERATE bounding: unlike D-24391's full-duplicate merge, "a copy of each card" is not a merge into the source card.
5. **Recursion guard.** A discarded card whose base ext_id (`#N` stripped) is `STEAL_ABILITIES_EXT_ID` OR `COPY_POWERS_EXT_ID` is economy-only, NOT re-fired (logged). BOTH are reentrant-copy keywords that can re-target the just-played, in-play Steal Abilities card: a re-fired Copy Powers auto-copies the sole eligible Rogue Hero (the in-play Steal Abilities card) and re-fires it, and nothing decreases monotonically (reshuffle-on-empty recycles the discards) → the `COPY_POWERS_EXT_ID` stack-overflow class (the ~30s "connection lost" crash). Two termination tests: (a) Steal Abilities on top of a deck; (b) Copy Powers on top with Steal Abilities the only in-play Hero.
6. **Cascade fork — Fork A (FIFO), operator-confirmed at review.** A copied ability re-fires fully; a parked choice lands in that keyword's existing pending queue (all `[]` FIFO queues). The ONLY single-slot pending type, `G.pendingHeroChoice` (`reveal-attack-choose`), is protected by that handler's existing reject-second guard (D-22001): a second copied `reveal-attack-choose` aborts cleanly rather than overwriting the slot. Fork B (economy-only for parking keywords) was the fallback for a keyword whose scaffold showed single-slot corruption; none was found.
7. **Determinism.** `ctx.random` is used ONLY for the empty-deck reshuffle. No new `G` field → the field-shape hash oracles cannot move for that reason. The card-data marker restages `G.heroAbilityHooks` for Rogue loadouts and the new log lines feed the replay hash (`computeStateHash` keeps `G.messages`), so scaffold-first confirmed the pin state: `finalStateHash` / `PRE_WP080_HASH` byte-identical (the pinned fixtures include no Rogue loadout) — NO re-pin; `sim:runtime-observed` unchanged (the committed observation set plays no Steal Abilities). ALL card-data-derived artifacts regenerated (`core.json`, card-mechanics, effect-index, hero-mechanic-ledger); every `:check` gate exits 0.

### D-24402 — Endgame Report Card v2: Named Players, Raw-Score Ledger, Luck of the Draw (Active 2026-08-23 — WP-593 / EC-628)

**Renumbered.** Originally reserved as D-24401; that number was taken by `rogue-steal-abilities` (WP-592 / EC-627 / D-24401), which landed on `main` while this arc was in build. This work is renumbered to WP-593 / EC-628 / D-24402.

**Problem.** The endgame report card labelled seats "Player 1 / Player 2" with no way to tell the bot from the human; the Raw Score showed only a monospace worked formula; and the card gave no read on how the shuffle treated the player. The operator also asked for opinionated hero/purchase coaching — deferred to a separate Pass-gated LLM feature (WP-B), not part of this decision.

**Decision.**
1. **Seat identity (derived, non-persisted).** A server helper `readSeatIdentities(matchId, seatCount, database)` returns a full 0..seatCount-1 roster `{ playerId, isBot, handle }` (`handle: string | null`), built from `readSeatAccounts` (WP-333) + `readMatchBotSeats` (WP-375) + `legendary.players.display_handle`. `submitCompetitiveScoreByMatchIdForRequest` attaches it to the `ok` result and the `POST /api/competition/scores` handler returns it beside the record (`{ record, wasExisting, seatIdentities? }`). It is NEVER a key of the locked 16-key `CompetitiveScoreRecord` and is NEVER persisted. Fail-safe: any roster/handle read error leaves the submission unchanged (client renders plain "Player N"). Not attached to `GET /api/me/scores` (the card uses the submit response).
2. **Raw-score ledger (client-only).** `buildWorkedScoreCalc` gains `rawLedger` (penalty lines + `penaltyTotal`, earned lines + `earnedTotal`, net `total` = verbatim `rawScore`) — a restyle of the same weighted values, never recomputed. The `match lost` penalty (WP-591 `weightedLossPenalty`) appears as its own penalty line.
3. **Luck of the draw (client-only, deterministic, OBJECTIVE).** `buildLuckRead(breakdown)` compares actual adversity (scheme twists + villain escapes + bystanders lost) against the WP-591 `parBaseline` expectation (`schemeTwistsPar` + `escapesPar` + `bystandersLostPar`) and bands the ratio: ≤ 0.75 favorable, ≥ 1.35 difficult, else average — framed encouragingly. Computed from the breakdown only (never deck order, which the engine never projects); `undefined` for records with no WP-591 adversity baseline. The OPINIONATED hero/purchase coaching is DEFERRED to WP-B (Pass-gated LLM).
4. **Player labels.** `Player {index+1}` + `(Bot)` for a bot ally, `(@handle)` for a human seat with a handle (one leading `@`, never doubled), else plain `Player N`.
5. **Determinism / persistence.** No engine change, no `G` field, no move, no scoring/formula change → `finalStateHash` / `PRE_WP080_HASH` byte-unchanged (no re-pin). The `CompetitiveScoreRecord` 16-key lock is untouched. The ledger and luck read are pure client display functions.

**Surface.** Server: `match/seatAccount.logic.ts`, `competition/competition.types.ts`, `competition/competition.logic.ts`, `competition/competition.routes.ts`. Client: `lib/api/competitionApi.ts`, `vfx/scoreCalcDisplay.ts`, `components/hud/EndgameSummary.vue`. Docs: `docs/ai/REFERENCE/api-endpoints.md` (submit row, D-11804), `docs/12-SCORING-REFERENCE.md`, ewiki `wiki/scoring.md`.

_Active 2026-08-23 — landed at WP-593 execution (EC-628). Seat identities derived + non-persisted (16-key record lock preserved); raw-score ledger + objective luck read client-only; graceful degradation on every optional path. No game-state-hash re-pin; no engine/`G`/move/scoring change. Opinionated hero/purchase coaching DEFERRED to WP-B (Pass-gated LLM). Hard-deps WP-333/375/338/578/583/584/587/588/591. ### D-24405 — PAR Turn-Distribution Profile (the empirical sweet-spot curve) (Active 2026-08-23 — WP-596 / EC-631)

**Context.** The PAR simulation (WP-049) plays hundreds of complete games per scenario but `generateScenarioPar` collapses them to a single `parValue` + a percentile summary, discarding the per-game `(turnCount, rawScore, outcome)` pairs. A 2026-08-23 prototype recovered those pairs from the real `simulateOneGame` loop and plotted the empirical turns-vs-score "sweet-spot" curve for `core/magneto + midtown-bank-robbery + brotherhood` (1p): 777 wins / 800, no interior peak (score improves monotonically to ~turn 34), minimum winning turn 9. The monotone shape at ~97% win rate is the calibration wiki's "a baseline for a different, easier game" caveat made measurable — a difficulty-fidelity signal that the under-built engine makes this scenario too easy.

**Decision.**
1. **Observability seam.** `par.aggregator.ts` gains an exported `generateScenarioParSamples(config, registry): PerGameSample[]` running the identical per-seed `simulateOneGame` loop; `generateScenarioPar` is refactored to build its `rawScores` from `samples.map(s => s.rawScore)`. `parValue` is **byte-identical** to the pre-refactor value — regression-pinned. The refactor adds observability; it never changes calibration (no seed, policy, scoring call, or percentile change).
2. **Derived profile.** `aggregateTurnDistributionProfile` reduces the samples to a per-turn `ParTurnDistributionProfile` (per `turnCount`: game count, median / p25 / p75 rawScore, win rate, median VP; plus `sampleSize`, `winCount`, `lossCount`, `stuckAtCapCount`, `minWinningTurn`, and a `monotoneImproving` flag).
3. **Persistence boundary.** The profile is a **derived, non-authoritative** artifact persisted in a SEPARATE `profile/<version>/` tree — never inside the immutable, hashed PAR artifact body (WP-050), never in the PAR index, never a competitive input, never read back into gameplay (persistence-boundary: derived record, not state; mirrors snapshots-are-counts-only). It carries an explicit `authoritative: false` marker.
4. **Fidelity signal, not strategy guide.** A `monotoneImproving` profile at near-100% win rate flags a scenario as currently too easy on the under-built engine; PAR calibration trust still gates on rules-faithful coverage (VISION §26). The profile is a diagnostic, not player-facing.
5. **Boundary / determinism.** Engine simulation + the D-5001 filesystem carve-out in `par.storage.ts` only. No new `G` field, no `boardgame.io` import in the simulation files, no `Math.random()`; `finalStateHash` / `PRE_WP080_HASH` byte-unchanged. Deterministic: identical `(baseSeed, simulationCount, setupConfig, scoringConfig)` → byte-identical samples + profile.
6. **Scope.** Engine functions + derived-artifact persistence + tests only. The render surface (`/coverage` or the scoring wiki) and the cross-scenario "too-easy" ranking sweep are a **separate follow-up WP**.

**Surface.** `packages/game-engine/src/simulation/par.aggregator.ts`; `packages/game-engine/src/simulation/par.profile.ts`; `packages/game-engine/src/simulation/par.storage.ts`; `packages/game-engine/src/index.ts` (+ their `.test.ts`).

_Active 2026-08-23 — landed at WP-596 execution (EC-631). Shipped exactly as locked: `generateScenarioParSamples` + `PerGameSample` reuse the WP-049 `simulateOneGame` loop; `generateScenarioPar` routes through it with `parValue` regression-pinned byte-identical (literal 0 / seedParDelta 1200 / all-zero distribution for the mock-registry test config). `aggregateTurnDistributionProfile` (`par.profile.ts`, pure) → per-turn median/p25/p75 rawScore + winRate + median VP + `minWinningTurn` + `monotoneImproving` (vacuous-true for <2 qualifying bins). `writeParProfileArtifact` / `readParProfileArtifact` persist to a SEPARATE `profile/<version>/` tree (derived:true / authoritative:false), OVERWRITING (regenerable) — never the immutable hashed PAR artifact/index.
