### D-24408 — Bystander Scoring Dominance: Watched; Scheme-PAR Mitigates; Diminishing-Returns-Past-PAR Reserved (Active 2026-08-24 — scoring policy, no WP)

**Context.** A standalone scoring-**policy** decision (no code, no WP/EC) recording an operator observation from the first live endgame report cards: bystander rescue is the single largest lever in the competitive score. Per the WP-585/WP-591 weights, a rescued bystander is worth **−200** raw score, a lost bystander **+400**, and a victory point only **−10** — so one bystander ≈ 20 VP. The concern: this could homogenize hero selection toward bystander-rescue-capable teams (e.g. Black Widow) and let players **gamify** the best scores, collapsing meta diversity.

**Analysis (why it is watched, not yet acted on).**
1. **PAR normalizes rescue to par.** `FinalScore = RawScore − PAR`, and the PAR baseline already expects a scheme's natural bystander count (Midtown expects ~22, Cosmic Cube ~3–4). Rescuing *to par* is neutral; only **beating par** moves the score. So the incentive is "rescue more than this scheme expects," not "rescue = win."
2. **Scheme-aware PAR (D-24400 / WP-591) varies the optimum by scheme.** On a bystander-flood scheme rescue matters; on a bystander-light scheme rescue heroes are near dead weight and VP/tempo win. Because the gauntlet rotates schemes, the score-optimal loadout **varies across the gauntlet** — no single card is forced gauntlet-wide. This is the current structural mitigation and it is already shipped.
3. **Most rescue is generic, not hero-specific.** The bulk of bystander rescue comes from **fighting the villains/henchmen holding captured bystanders** — any attack hero does that. Dedicated rescue abilities (Black Widow's Dangerous Rescue / Mission Accomplished) are conditional (class-synergy gated) and add only incremental rescues, so the pressure is "engage the bystander-holders," i.e. play the scenario well.

**Where the concern is valid.** A **single-scenario ranked board** will still converge on rescue-capable teams (any fixed puzzle has an optimal solution), so within one board diversity compresses. And the **20:1 bystander:VP ratio is steep** on a **high-variance, shuffle-driven** axis (how many bystanders the villains capture is largely luck) — so the score over-indexes one lucky axis, which surfaces in the WP-593 "difficult/favorable shuffle" luck read.

**Decision.**
1. **Do NOT reweight now.** Scheme-aware PAR (D-24400) is the load-bearing mitigation and was just recalibrated; reweighting on 1–2 games would over-correct. The weights (`bystanderReward 200`, `vpReward 10`, penalties 100/400/300/25/40) stand.
2. **Watch real ranked-board evidence.** Revisit only if the live single-scenario boards actually mono-culture on rescue teams — a data question, resolved by the real games now being generated (the same reason simulation calibration was deferred, D-24400).
3. **Reserved lever, in priority order, IF boards converge:** (a) **diminishing returns past PAR** — each rescued bystander beyond the scheme's expected count worth progressively less; this kills the "spam-rescue to gamify" strategy while keeping "meet par" neutral and every scheme's identity intact, and is PREFERRED because protecting bystanders is thematically core and should not be nerfed outright; (b) a **modest bystander:VP ratio narrow** (e.g. bystander 200→~150 or VP 10→~15) as the blunt alternative. Any such change is a new scoring WP with a version bump + artifact regeneration (the WP-585/591 pattern), never an inline tweak.
4. **Pay-to-win guardrail (VISION NG-1).** Whatever the score-optimal levers turn out to be, they MUST stay reachable from **Core / free** content — competitive integrity may never require a purchase. Black Widow is Core, so no issue today; this locks the rule for future set-gated heroes.

_Active 2026-08-24 — a watch-and-reserved-lever policy, not an implementation. Scheme-aware PAR (D-24400) is the current mitigation; diminishing-returns-past-PAR is the reserved lever if real ranked boards converge; NG-1 keeps score-optimal levers on Core content. A future scoring WP that acts on this cites D-24408; until then no code changes. Related: D-24400 (scheme-aware PAR), D-24394 (rulebook-faithful weights)._

> **SUPERSEDED by D-24409 (2026-08-24, WP-599).** D-24408 framed the bystander lever as a *dominance* concern (keep the −200 reward, watch, reserve diminishing-returns). The operator subsequently determined the −200 reward is itself a **non-rulebook invention** — the rulebook and the community Total Score give a rescued bystander no separate reward, only its 1 VP — so the fix is full rulebook fidelity (remove the reward, rescale penalties to true VP-units), not a dominance tweak. D-24409 records that reversal.

### D-24409 — Rulebook-Faithful Scoring: Remove the Invented Bystander Reward, Rescale Penalties to True VP-Units (Active 2026-08-24 — WP-599 / EC-634; supersedes D-24408)

**Context.** The endgame report card revealed that a rescued bystander was scored **twice**: the dedicated `bystanderReward` (−200) **and** its own printed 1 VP (−10, inside the summed `victoryPoints`), i.e. −210 per bystander. Investigating that double-count surfaced the deeper issue the operator named: the **−200 reward has no basis in the rules.** The Marvel Legendary v23 rulebook scores a win as *Victory Points minus penalties* (−4 per bystander carried away, −3 per scheme twist, −1 per escaped villain — the community "Legendary Leagues" Total Score `VP − 4·lost − 3·twists − 1·escapes` is the same shape). Rescued bystanders contribute **only their 1 VP**; there is **no** positive rescue reward. Legendary Arena's `bystanderReward` (and the VISION §21 structural invariants 1 & 3 that required it) was an invented layer on top of the rules.

**Decision.** Full rulebook fidelity, superseding D-24408's "keep 200, watch" posture (the operator's live decision, made with D-24408 in view):

1. **Remove the `bystanderReward` weight** (and `ScoreBreakdown.weightedBystanderReward`). A rescued bystander scores exactly once — as its printed 1 VP, already inside the `victoryPoints` term. This eliminates the double-count and the invented reward together.
2. **Rescale penalties to true VP-units** (1 VP = 10 on the centesimal scale): `villainEscaped 100→10`, `schemeTwistNegative 300→30`, `bystanderLost 400→40` — the rulebook 4:3:1, now on the same scale as VP so `RawScore = penalties − VP×10` mirrors `VP − 4·lost − 3·twists − 1·escapes`. The LA-only inert penalties (`mastermindTacticUntaken`, `scenarioSpecificPenalty`) take a minor in-scale value (10).
3. **Structural invariants:** 1 (`bystanderReward > villainEscaped`) and 3 (`bystanderLost > bystanderReward`) are **removed** (they referenced the deleted reward). Invariant 2 (`bystanderLost > villainEscaped`, 40 > 10) survives as the sole moral-hierarchy invariant — VISION §21's "rescue is the point" now lives entirely on the heavy loss penalty, exactly as the rulebook encodes it.
4. **Recalibration.** `LOSS_PENALTY 6000→800` and `SCORE_GRADE_BANDS` re-derived (Legendary ≤ −500, A ≤ −250, B ≤ 150, C ≤ 500, D ≤ 1100, F) for the compressed VP-dominated scale, validated against the same 13 real anchor games as D-24400 (a 34-bystander Midtown win → A, a competent win → B near PAR, a bystander-heavy loss → D, a low-VP loss → F). Interim / operator-tunable, like D-24400's bands.
5. **Versioning.** `scoringConfigVersion 4→5`, `rawScoreSemanticsVersion 3→4`. All 128 `data/scoring-configs` + 128 `data/par/seed/v1` artifacts + the index regenerated (`pnpm par:seed:generate`). Existing `competitive_scores` rows keep their pinned versions — **no retroactive invalidation** (VISION §22). The game-**winner** VP (rulebook table result) still counts bystanders at 1 VP each; only the competitive score changed.

**Deferred (not gating).** `data/par/profile/v1` diagnostic profiles (WP-597, not server-read, no CI gate) carry stale rawScore bins under the old formula; regeneration (a simulation sweep) is a follow-up. The report-card display *polish* (rescued/lost terminology, penalties/awards legend, RAW SCORE / BY PLAYER styling) is a separate follow-up PR; this WP does the minimal display-correctness edits the contract change forced.

_Active 2026-08-24 — supersedes D-24408. Related: D-24408 (the superseded dominance policy), D-24400 (scheme-aware PAR + interim bands), D-24394 (rulebook-faithful weights, roundCost removal), D-24342 (4:3:1 penalty anchor)._

### D-24410 — Endgame Report Card: Rulebook-Faithful Display Polish (Active 2026-08-24 — WP-600 / EC-635)

**Context.** The endgame report-card refinements the operator asked for, on top of the WP-599 model: (1) rescued/lost terminology, (2) a penalties/awards scoring-key legend, (3) RAW SCORE + BY PLAYER restyling. Display-only, stacked on WP-599.

**Decision.**
1. **Terminology.** The card never shows a bare "bystanders" — it says **bystanders rescued** (an award, via VP) or **bystanders lost** (the heaviest penalty). Fixes the per-player stat and the PAR-derivation "expected bystanders" given.
2. **Scoring key.** A penalties/awards legend (`buildScoringKey`, `vfx/scoreCalcDisplay.ts`) renders beside the grade scale: **Awards** — Victory Point −10 (each defeated villain/henchman/tactic + each rescued bystander at 1 VP); **Penalties** — villain escaped +10, scheme twist +30, bystander lost +40. The weights are a **documented client constant** (the `gradeDisplay` precedent, D-24392) — an explanatory legend must show events that didn't occur this match, so it can't be derived from the breakdown; it is cross-referenced to D-24409 and pinned by a test so it cannot drift from the engine's shipped configs.
3. **Styling.** The raw-score ledger sides are tinted to their sign (penalties warm / earned cool, matching the key); the per-player split renders as seat chips.

**Constraint.** Display-only — no engine, scoring, server, or `G` change; no hash re-pin; every match value still rendered verbatim from the server-returned breakdown. A rescued bystander is never a separate award (it scores inside VP, WP-599).

_Active 2026-08-24 — WP-600 / EC-635. Related: D-24409 (the rulebook-faithful model this displays), D-24402 (report card v2), D-24392 (client owns display copy/weights)._

### D-24411 — Endgame PAR Derivation Shows the Bystander-Lost Term (Active 2026-08-24 — WP-601 / EC-636)

**Context.** A real 2p Midtown / Red Skull live match (D-24026 verify) surfaced that the endgame PAR-derivation display did not reconcile: it printed `(1 × 10) + (6 × 30) − (74 × 10) = −470`, but that expansion is −550. The **−470 is correct** — `computeParScore` also adds `bystandersLostPar × 40` (WP-591 / D-24400) — but `buildParDerivation` never rendered that penalty term. WP-591 added the field to the PAR math and to the raw-score givens but not to the derivation display; WP-599 then removed the large bystander-reward term that had masked the shortfall.

**Decision.** Display-only fix: `buildParDerivation` renders the expected-bystander-lost penalty term (`+ (bystandersLostPar × 40)`) in the formula + substituted lines and adds an "Expected bystanders lost" given, mirroring how the twist term already works. The weight is derived from the breakdown (symbolic when the match had no bystander loss — never fabricated), gated on `bystandersLostPar > 0`.

**Constraint.** No engine/scoring/server/`G` change; the PAR value itself is unchanged (rendered verbatim). Only its shown derivation gains the missing term, so the on-card arithmetic now reconciles to the printed PAR.

_Active 2026-08-24 — WP-601 / EC-636. Related: D-24400 (bystandersLostPar in computeParScore), D-24409 (removed the bystander-reward term from the derivation), D-24396 (the PAR-derivation display)._

### D-24412 — Bystander-Reveal Notable-Event Overlay (`bystanderRevealed`) (Active 2026-08-24 — WP-602 / EC-637)

**Context.** The center-screen `NotableEventOverlay` on `play.legendary-arena.com` is driven by the engine's `UIState.notableEvents` stream. A villain-deck reveal raises the overlay only when the reveal pipeline pushes a notable event — a Scheme Twist (`schemeTwistResolved`), a Master Strike (`mastermindStrikeResolved`), or an Ambush (`ambushResolved`). The `cardType === 'bystander'` branch of `performVillainReveal` only wrote a `G.messages` log line and pushed **no** event; there was no bystander variant in the `NotableGameEvent` union at all. So revealing a Bystander was the only villain-deck reveal outcome with no overlay (operator-reported).

**Decision.** Add a **seventh** `NotableGameEvent` variant `bystanderRevealed` (mirroring the WP-381 `healResolved` sixth-variant precedent): `{ type, revealedCardId, captorCardId, narrative }` — minimal-payload (no `eventId`/`seq`/`timestamp` per D-20001). `performVillainReveal` emits it as the final step of the bystander capture branch, **additive** to the preserved "revealed and captured by" log line, via an unconditional `G.notableEvents.push` (mirroring the `ambushResolved` site); names resolve at the fire site through `G.cardDisplayData` so the composer (`composeBystanderRevealedNarrative`) stays pure. The event is **public** (not audience-redacted) and rides the existing wholesale `UIState.notableEvents` spread — no UIState projection or audience-filter change. The arena-client `NotableEventOverlay` renders a **"Bystander!"** chip + verbatim narrative (D-20002); `eventCardId` resolves the variant to `revealedCardId` so the overlay names the bystander.

**Constraint.** **Presentation parity only — not a new mechanic, counter, scoring, or reward** (explicitly distinct from D-24409's removed non-canonical bystander scoring reward; the capture already happens per WP-432, this only announces it). No engine gameplay change. `G.notableEvents` is hashed, but **no competitive-hash re-pin**: `PRE_WP080_HASH` replays an empty move list (no reveal fires) and the sole sentinel fixture reveals no bystander, so `finalStateHash` + `PRE_WP080_HASH` are byte-identical (verified: engine 2903/0). The exhaustive audio `sfxManifest` (WP-412) forced a seventh clip entry (`bystander-revealed.mp3`, operator-pending on R2 like every other clip) — a mechanical inline amendment, not new audio scope.

_Active 2026-08-24 — WP-602 / EC-637. Related: D-24182 (the `healResolved` sixth-variant precedent this mirrors), D-20008 / D-20001 (the notableEvents union + minimal-payload contract), D-24409 (the removed bystander scoring reward this is deliberately NOT), WP-432 (the canonical bystander reveal-capture path this announces)._

### D-24413 — Melter (Villain) Fight: Interactive Per-Card KO / Keep Choice (Active 2026-08-24 — WP-603 / EC-638; supersedes D-24332)

**Context.** WP-519 / D-24332 shipped core Melter's Fight — *"Each player reveals the top card of their deck. For each card, you choose to KO it or put it back."* — as a **deterministic auto-resolve**: the handler KOs only cullable cards (Wounds / basic S.H.I.E.L.D. starters) and keeps every real Hero, with **no player prompt**. D-24332 chose that fidelity level because the keep-option means a real Hero is never force-KO'd, so the WP-470 scry-ko agency bug could not arise. Jeff reported from a live 2p Midtown / Red Skull match (2026-08-24; game-log `23.2.13`, `[blocked] Fight effect: revealed each player's deck top; nothing worth KO'ing.`) that the ability looked dead — both deck tops were real Heroes, so the auto-resolve correctly kept them and did nothing visible. Jeff asked for the **faithful interactive** behavior: a per-card KO/keep prompt over every player's revealed deck top, kept cards returned to the top of their owner's deck.

**Decision.** Reverse D-24332 to a real **active-player pending choice**, modeled on the WP-470 / D-24282 interactive scry-ko and WP-242 ko-hero machinery. On Melter's `onFight`, reveal each player's deck top (sorted iteration, D-18902; empty deck reshuffles discard first, D-24285), snapshot each `{ ownerPlayerID, cardId }`, and park **one** `PendingMelterKoChoice` for the fighting (active) player carrying the snapshot list — KO nothing at park time. The resolve move `resolveMelterKoChoice({ cardId, keep })` acts on the front entry only; `cardId` must be in its `revealedTops` (round-trip rule); `keep === false` KOs the card from **its owner's** deck top to `G.ko`, `keep === true` is a no-op (the card was never removed — it stays face-up on top). Either action removes the entry; an emptied list shifts the queue. The choice is active-player-scoped (D-24284): the fighting player makes **all** decisions (own + every ally's), the shape Jeff requested. `pendingMelterKoChoice` is projected through `buildUIState` and passed through `filterUIStateForAudience` **field-by-field, redacted to the chooser** (D-24011); a new `PendingMelterKoChoicePrompt.vue` (two actions per revealed card) is wired into `PlayDesktop` / `PlayMobile` / `useTurnActions`.

**Constraint.** (1) **Primitive reuse** — the `ko-cullable-each-deck-top` primitive token, its marker rows, and `data/cards/core.json` are **unchanged**; only the handler body flips auto-resolve → interactive park. No union/array/marker/`core.json`/`mechanic-provenance` churn. The token name is retained (predates this upgrade) with a `// why:` note that D-24413 supersedes D-24332. (2) **Bot/sim byte-identity** — `isCullableDeckTopCard` is repurposed as the `getLegalMoves` default-pick (`keep = !isCullableDeckTopCard(cardId)`), so bot / simulation / replay outcomes reproduce the WP-519 auto-resolve **byte-identically**; only live human play gains the prompt. `resolveMelterKoChoice` MUST be in `SIMULATION_MOVE_NAMES` + the sim MOVE_MAPs or the per-turn loop hangs. (3) **No-UX-freeze** — the engine block-all guard (`hasPendingMelterKoChoice` at every scry-ko/ko-hero guard site), the UIState projection, and the client prompt ship together as one unit (the WP-470 precedent); a partial ship hard-freezes the match. (4) **Snapshot discipline** — the reveal never removes a card, so "keep" needs no return-to-deck mutation; the block-all guard freezes every deck top so the snapshot cannot drift. (5) **Determinism / persistence** — `pendingMelterKoChoices` is a runtime-only pending queue (never persisted; snapshots stay counts-only); randomness only via the seeded reshuffle. **Hashed-oracle posture:** the auto-resolve → park change alters the move-log for any fixture that FIGHTS Melter; a draft grep found no committed `finalStateHash` / `PRE_WP080_HASH` / sentinel fixture that fights or includes Masters-of-Evil / Melter, so no re-pin is expected — re-verify at execution and re-record via `record-game-fixture.mjs` (never hand-edit) if one does, noting the re-pin here.

**Execution note (2026-08-24).** Landed exactly as drafted, with one within-category refinement: the resolve payload is `{ ownerPlayerID, cardId, keep }`, not `{ cardId, keep }` — starter ext_ids (e.g. `starting-shield-agent`) are shared across every player's deck, so `cardId` alone cannot identify which deck top a decision targets; the round-trip rule matches on both. Whole repo green (game-engine 2916/0, arena-client 1444/0, all packages 0 fail); `finalStateHash` + `PRE_WP080_HASH` byte-identical (no committed hashed oracle fights Melter — no re-pin). Three files beyond the EC allowlist were touched as inline file-allowlist amendments, each a mechanical consequence of the interactive wiring: `TurnActionBar.vue` (the pending-flag prop + `useTurnActions` threading), `uiMoveName.types.ts` (the `resolveMelterKoChoice` client move-name), and `index.ts` (exporting `UIPendingMelterKoChoice` for the client).

_Active 2026-08-24 — WP-603 / EC-638. Supersedes D-24332 (the auto-resolve fidelity this reverses). Related: D-24282 (interactive scry-ko pending choice, the structural template), D-24006 / D-24007 (ko-hero interactive + block-all guard), D-24284 (active-player-scoped choices), D-24285 (reveal-reshuffle), D-24011 (pending choices redacted to the chooser), D-24102 (the pending-choice result shape)._

### D-24414 — Feedback & Public Roadmap: Build Custom on the Existing Stack (Active 2026-08-25 — WP-604 / EC-639; landed with the WP-604 execution)

**Context.** The ewiki design page [User Feedback and Public Roadmap](../../wiki/user-feedback-and-public-roadmap.md) surveyed how Legendary Arena should collect player feedback (bug reports, enhancement requests, reviews), track it, let players vote on enhancements, and publish a monthly changelog under quarterly roadmap themes. It left three decisions open, the load-bearing one being **build vs buy**: a custom board on the existing stack, a self-hosted Fider instance, or a SaaS board (Canny / Featurebase / Frill / Nolt) — as a permanent home or a validation experiment.

**Decision (operator, 2026-08-25).** **Build the feedback + public-roadmap system custom on the existing Postgres + Hanko + Dashboard stack.** Do NOT adopt a SaaS board or self-host Fider as the permanent home; SaaS is permitted only as a time-boxed validation experiment, never the system of record. The project already owns identity (Hanko), storage (Postgres `legendary.*`), and an operator admin surface (the dashboard), so a custom build avoids a per-seat SaaS bill, a second login for players, and off-platform data — the institutional-dependency trap the operating posture guards against.

**Corollaries (the design the build implements).**
1. **Own the data** — feedback and votes live in `legendary.feedback_item` / `legendary.feedback_vote` (ordinary domain tables; not `G`, not a snapshot, not a persistence carve-out).
2. **Identity-gated voting** — one vote per account per item, authenticated through the existing Hanko session; enforced by a `UNIQUE (feedback_item_id, account_ext_id)` constraint. No anonymous / IP voting.
3. **The DB owns `vote_count`** — it is a `COUNT` projection over the votes table, never a hand-set column.
4. **Status is authored only on the operator dashboard** — the `Under review → Planned → In progress → Shipped → Declined` status is an editorial judgment set on the dashboard (a single Hanko + Cloudflare Access gate, **no role tiers**); the public board only *displays* status; players never set it. "Shipped" derives from the WP/git spine.
5. **The public board is a read-only projection** — the authoritative record of what was built remains the internal Work Packet / EC / DECISIONS / git spine (the *System of record* rule from the wiki page).
6. **Vote weighting is out of scope and gated** — start unweighted; any future weighting (by engagement or paid tier) requires its own decision record, because it alters the roadmap's trust model and intersects the VISION fairness bright lines.

**Scope of WP-604 (the first packet).** WP-604 lands only the persistence + intake/voting **backbone**: the two tables and the `POST /api/feedback` (submit), `GET /api/feedback` (public enhancement list with projected `vote_count`), and `POST`/`DELETE /api/feedback/:id/vote` endpoints. It authors no UI and never mutates status. The **operator triage panel** (dashboard), the **public roadmap board** (marketing / arena-client), and the **changelog / monthly-recap** surfaces are follow-on WPs, each citing this decision. The two still-open questions from the wiki page — where the public roadmap renders (`www` section vs a `roadmap.` subdomain) and who the named operator is — are deferred to those follow-on WPs.

_Active 2026-08-25 — WP-604 / EC-639 (landed with the WP-604 execution: the two `legendary.*` tables + four `/api/feedback` endpoints). Related: the ewiki design page (`wiki/user-feedback-and-public-roadmap.md`), D-9905 (the closed auth set), D-11804 (the API-catalog update obligation), D-11504 (`Cache-Control` first), the persistence-boundary rule (feedback tables are ordinary domain storage, not a carve-out)._

### D-24415 — Luck of the Draw Stays a Read, Not a Score Adjustment (Active 2026-08-25 — standalone scoring-policy decision, no WP/EC/code)

**Context.** The endgame report card's **luck-of-the-draw** read (WP-593 / D-24402) prints an objective, deterministic verdict — *Favorable / Even / Difficult shuffle* — by comparing the adversity a match actually dealt (scheme twists, villain escapes, bystanders lost) against what the scenario's PAR baseline expects. It is **display-only**: `buildLuckRead` in `apps/arena-client/src/vfx/scoreCalcDisplay.ts` reads the returned `ScoreBreakdown` and never touches the score. Jeff proposed promoting it into an actual score term — e.g. `+2` when favorable, `0` when neutral, `−2` when adverse — to "reward skill over luck" and push the leaderboard toward skill.

**Decision (operator, 2026-08-25).** **Do NOT promote the luck read into a score adjustment — it stays an informational read.** The proposal's premise is half-right: per-match luck genuinely does leak into Final Score, but the only luck signal available is entangled with skill, so a flat penalty keyed on it would remove skill alongside luck — the opposite of the stated intent.

**Reasoning.**
1. **Per-match luck does leak in.** `finalScore = rawScore − parScore`, and `parScore` is a fixed per-scenario constant, so a match's adversity enters Final only as the delta from expectation: `finalScore = (actualAdversity − expectedAdversity) − (VP − VP_par)`. A kind, low-twist draw lowers Raw and the constant PAR never claws it back — the concern is real, not imagined.
2. **But the only luck signal is not pure luck.** The read is computed from actual-vs-expected adversity; it never sees deck order (`G` is not persisted, the engine never projects it). Those adversity terms are a blend of luck and skill: scheme-twist **count** tracks game length (win faster → fewer twists flip; only twist **order** is luck, per D-24342), and villain escapes are preventable by clearing the City on tempo. A flat penalty on the delta cannot separate "kind shuffle" from "played efficiently and ended early," so it neutralizes the skill component too — driving the score toward pure VP-efficiency and penalizing a tight, fast game as a "favorable shuffle."
3. **No unit for it.** WP-585 / D-24394 removed turns/rounds from scoring entirely (the rulebook has no round cost; twists are its length proxy), so a "±N turns" adjustment has no home in the formula.
4. **Comparability cost.** Any scoring-math change bumps `scoringConfigVersion`, regenerates every seed PAR artifact, and breaks cross-version comparability (VISION §22 immutability) — real cost for a change that works against its own goal.

**Constraint — where luck is actually addressed.** Reducing luck as a **competitive** variable is the job of two already-designed surfaces, not a report-card penalty: **Seed Challenges** hold the shuffle constant across the whole leaderboard (luck becomes a constant, not a variable — the complete removal, not a heuristic), and **simulation-calibrated per-match PAR** supplies a true counterfactual (what a competent team would face with *this exact draw*), which isolates luck properly. If a scored luck term is ever revisited, the least-bad form is a small, capped credit that **only** helps the player on a difficult shuffle and never penalizes a favorable one (avoids punishing efficiency, at the cost of slight scoring inflation) — but the standing decision is **no scored term**. No code, engine, scoring-config, or `G` change; the WP-593 read is unchanged.

_Active 2026-08-25 — standalone scoring-policy decision, no WP/EC/code (mirrors the D-24408 standalone-policy precedent). Related: D-24402 (the luck-of-the-draw read this keeps display-only), D-24394 / WP-585 (removed the round/turn scoring unit), D-24342 (twist count is tempo; only order is luck), D-24400 (scheme-aware PAR — the expected-adversity baseline the read compares against), VISION §22 (scoring-config immutability), the ewiki Scoring page §"Luck of the draw is a read, not a score adjustment"._

### D-24416 — Feedback Status Authoring: the Operator Dashboard Is the Sole Status Writer (Active 2026-08-25 — WP-605 / EC-640; landed with the WP-605 execution)

**Context.** D-24414 built the player-feedback + public-roadmap system custom on the existing stack and split its surfaces by authority (ewiki [User Feedback and Public Roadmap](../../wiki/user-feedback-and-public-roadmap.md) §Surfaces and authority): *players author demand, the operator authors status, the codebase authors "done."* WP-604 shipped the intake/voting backbone (`legendary.feedback_item` / `feedback_vote` + the public `/api/feedback` routes) and, per its EC-639, deliberately **wrote no status** — every item is created `under_review` and the whole `Under review → Planned → In progress → Shipped → Declined` workflow was deferred to the operator-triage follow-on. WP-605 is that follow-on; this decision locks how status authoring works.

**Decision (operator, 2026-08-25).** **The operator dashboard is the sole writer of `feedback_item.status` and `resolution_reason`.** Status is authored only through an **admin-gated** server endpoint (`PATCH /api/dash/feedback/:id/status`, behind `requireAdminSession` — the existing single Hanko + Cloudflare Access operator gate, **no role tiers**) driven by the dashboard triage panel. Players never set status; the public `GET /api/feedback` only *displays* it.

**Corollaries (the contract WP-605 implements).**
1. **One status writer.** `updateFeedbackItemStatus` (in the WP-604 `feedback/` persistence module) is the only code path that writes `status` / `resolution_reason` / advances `updated_at`. This introduces the first `UPDATE ... status`, **reversing** WP-604 / EC-639's no-status-write deferral — sanctioned here, not a violation.
2. **Closed status set.** A write must set `status` ∈ `FEEDBACK_STATUSES` (`under_review | planned | in_progress | shipped | declined`); an out-of-set value is rejected (`invalid_status`).
3. **Declined requires a reason.** `resolution_reason` is required + non-empty when `status = 'declined'` (`resolution_reason_required`) and normalized to `NULL` for every other status — a move off Declined clears any prior reason. (The "no, because…" that closes the loop honestly, design principle 5.)
4. **Operator-only reads see everything.** `GET /api/dash/feedback` returns **all** types (incl. `bug` / `review`, which may carry PII) and all statuses with a projected `voteCount`; it is admin-gated and never reachable by a player — distinct from the public enhancement-only, PII-stripped `GET /api/feedback`.
5. **"Shipped" is operator-set in the MVP.** The design says Shipped *reflects* a merged WP on the git spine; wiring that derivation automatically is out of scope — the operator sets it manually for now, and auto-derivation is a later decision.
6. **No role tiers / delegated moderation.** A single operator gate, exactly as today; a community-moderator tier would be a separate change to the dashboard auth model, raised then, not assumed now.
7. **`is_admin` stays encapsulated.** The admin check is `requireAdminSession` (the only site permitted to read `is_admin`); the triage routes never inline an `is_admin` read.

**Scope of WP-605.** WP-605 lands the two admin endpoints + the dashboard triage page. It does **not** touch the public/player surfaces, add vote weighting, auto-derive Shipped from git, resolve authors to handles, or add a changelog/roadmap-render surface — each a follow-on WP.

_Active 2026-08-25 — WP-605 / EC-640 (landed with the WP-605 execution: `GET /api/dash/feedback` + `PATCH /api/dash/feedback/:id/status` + the dashboard triage page; `updateFeedbackItemStatus` is the sole status writer). Related: D-24414 (the build-custom decision + the Surfaces-and-authority split this implements), the ewiki design page (`wiki/user-feedback-and-public-roadmap.md`), D-9905/D-15901 (the closed auth set + `admin-session-required`), D-11804 (the API-catalog update obligation), D-11504 (`Cache-Control` first), D-20503 (the `{ data }` dashboard envelope), the WP-131/WP-159 `requireAdminSession` operator gate._

### D-24417 — Draw-Pool Composition Projection: Own-Pool Owner-Only, Villain-Pool Public, Order Always Stripped (Active 2026-08-25 — WP-606 / EC-641; landed with the WP-606 execution)

**Context.** The client-visible `UIState` projected every player's zones as **counts only** (`deckCount` / `discardCount`), with one owner-only exception — `discardCards` (WP-243 / D-24010) — and the shared villain deck as `villainDeckCount`. The **deck** array was never projected in any form ("counts only; the next-card identity is NEVER projected"). The proposed [Deck Probability Panel](../../wiki/deck-probability-panel.md) needs one datum the client lacks: the **composition of each draw pool** — the multiset a player may still draw, and the multiset still in the villain deck — to compute draw odds client-side. This decision locks what is information-safe to project, and to whom.

**Decision.** Project two order-stripped composition fields, each with the audience its information-safety requires:
1. **A player's OWN draw-pool composition is owner-only.** `UIPlayerState.deckComposition?` is the **sorted (order-stripped) multiset** of `G.playerZones[id].deck`, projected to that player only and redacted for every opponent and spectator (the `discardCards` posture). It is information-safe *to the owner* — derivable from their own deckbuilding plus the public discard — but the remaining deck composition is not an opponent's to see.
2. **The villain-deck composition is public.** `UIDecksState.villainDeckComposition?` is the **sorted (order-stripped) multiset** of `G.villainDeck.deck`, value-identical for every audience (the `matchCardImageUrls` / D-24222 posture). It is public board knowledge — derivable from the public match setup (villain/henchman groups, scheme twists, master strikes, bystander count; the villain-deck cards carry synthetic generic ext_ids, no random identity assigned at shuffle) minus the public revealed discard.

**Corollaries.**
1. **Order is ALWAYS stripped.** Both fields are the sorted multiset (`[...zone].sort()`), never the raw zone. Projecting raw order would leak the next-draw **sequence** — the exact secret the WP-470 / D-24282 scry-KO redaction protects. The sort guarantees composition-not-sequence; a test proves order-independence (a permuted zone yields the identical projection).
2. **Projection-only — no `G` field, no hash surface.** Both are derived at projection time from existing `G` zones; `G` gains nothing, so `finalStateHash` and the replay `computeStateHash` / `PRE_WP080_HASH` are byte-identical. This is the `matchCardImageUrls` / menace precedent.
3. **Optional in the type.** Both are `?:`, so no arena-client UIState fixture backfill — the change stays game-engine only. Optional fields are pinned by a runtime keyset assertion on a **built** projection, never a `satisfies` or a hand-written-fixture keyset (WP-563 / D-24372).
4. **Advisory, never authoritative.** These fields exist so the client-side Deck Probability Panel can compute draw odds without the engine running probability math or `ctx.random`; the panel is a read-only aid that never feeds back into game state (a follow-on UI WP).
5. **The own-composition projection supersedes the old "no own-deck projection" assumption.** A player now sees their own order-stripped deck composition (their own revealed cards may appear there), which is why the WP-603 Melter opponent redaction test was refined at execution: the Melter next-draw secret (which card is on top) stays hidden — the sort strips order and `pendingMelterKoChoice` is redacted — while a player's own composition legitimately lists their own card. The other player's composition + the choice stay fully redacted.

**Scope of WP-606.** WP-606 lands the two projection fields + their filter routing + the drift / audience tests (5 game-engine files). It does **not** add the client panel, any probability math, a parallel display array, or any `G` change — each out of scope; the panel UI is a follow-on WP.

_Active 2026-08-25 — WP-606 / EC-641 (landed with the WP-606 execution: `deckComposition` owner-only + `villainDeckComposition` public, both order-stripped; engine suite 2919/2919, sentinel hashes unchanged). Related: D-24010 (the owner-only `discardCards` projection this mirrors), D-24222 (the `matchCardImageUrls` public information-safe pass-through this mirrors), D-12803 (the WP-128 audience-filter redaction matrix), WP-470 / D-24282 (the scry-KO next-draw redaction the order-strip protects), WP-563 / D-24372 (the optional-field built-projection pin), the ewiki [Deck Probability Panel](../../wiki/deck-probability-panel.md) design page._

### D-24418 — Deck Probability Panel Is a Client-Side Advisory Surface; Villain Cards Categorized by Ext_id Prefix (Active 2026-08-25 — WP-607 / EC-642; landed with the WP-607 execution)

**Context.** WP-606 / D-24417 projected the villain deck (public) and the viewer's own draw deck (owner-only) as order-stripped CardExtId multisets on `UIState`, the data foundation for the Deck Probability Panel. WP-607 lands the Phase-1 MVP (the plain card counter) that renders them. This decision locks how the panel computes and categorizes.

**Decision.** The Deck Probability Panel is a **client-side advisory** surface: it computes draw odds purely from the WP-606 `UIState` projection, **never** from `ctx.random`, and **never** feeds gameplay (extends D-24417). Villain-deck cards are categorized **client-side by ext_id prefix** (`master-strike-` → `mastermind-strike`; `scheme-twist-` → `scheme-twist`; `bystander-villain-deck-` → `bystander`; `henchman-` → `henchman`; else → `villain`), the synthetic grammar being deterministic in `villainDeck.setup.ts`, rather than via a new engine type-projection.

**Corollaries.**
1. **Villain-last fallback, no collision.** The prefix checks are ordered so `villain` is the fallback; villain ext_ids are `{setAbbr}-villain-…` and no set abbreviation equals a reserved prefix, so a villain can only reach the fallback.
2. **Killbots is a documented Phase-1 miscount.** The Killbots scheme rewrites some `bystander-villain-deck-*` cards to engine type `villain` via `G.convertedOrigins`, which is **not** projected — so the prefix reader miscounts those as Bystander. Accepted, documented, and pinned by test; correcting it needs an engine type-projection (a follow-on).
3. **Own-deck names are best-effort.** No complete client-side extId→display resolver exists, so own-deck names are harvested from the viewer's own display arrays (hand / in-play / discard / victory); un-resolvable ext_ids render as "Unknown". The own-deck **total** is exact (`deckComposition.length`).
4. **Engine types only.** The panel imports engine **types** only (no runtime import), consistent with its presentational role; arena-client MAY import the runtime-safe engine surface (WP-090), but this helper does not need to.
5. **Phase-1 scope.** The MVP is the plain counter + upcoming-risk odds; hand projection (Monte Carlo), pace/outlook, and deck health are follow-on phases (the ewiki panel page's phasing).

_Active 2026-08-25 — WP-607 / EC-642 (landed with the WP-607 execution: `DeckProbabilityPanel.vue` + the pure `deckProbability.ts`, arena-client only). Related: D-24417 / WP-606 (the projection this consumes), the ewiki [Deck Probability Panel](../../wiki/deck-probability-panel.md) design page, WP-090 (the arena-client runtime-safe engine surface)._

### D-24419 — Owner-Only Draw-Pool Card Stats Projection (`deckCardStats`), Sorted Keys (Active 2026-08-25 — WP-608 / EC-643; landed with the WP-608 execution)

**Context.** WP-606 projected the viewer's own draw-pool composition (`deckComposition`, owner-only) but not each card's recruit/attack — which the Phase-2 client hand-projection Monte Carlo needs. Those live only in the internal `G.cardStats` (never projected; the client ships no registry), and `UICardDisplay` is locked to 7 presentation fields (recruit/attack forbidden). WP-608 projects them.

**Decision.** Add an **owner-only, projection-only** `UIPlayerState.deckCardStats?: Record<string, UIDeckCardStat>` (`UIDeckCardStat = {recruit, attack, cost}`), derived from `G.cardStats` in `buildUIState`, redacted for non-owners like `deckComposition`. It is a **separate ext_id→stats map** — not enriching `deckComposition` (DRY, order-free), not on `UICardDisplay` (recruit/attack are gameplay values, distinct from the `cardDisplayData` presentation channel).

**Corollaries.**
1. **Sorted keys — no order leak.** A `Record`'s serialized key order is its insertion order, so the map is built from the **sorted** unique ext_ids of the deck∪discard union; raw-array order would leak partial next-draw sequence even to the owner (the `deckComposition` order-strip rationale, WP-470). A drift test pins key-order-independence.
2. **Deck∪discard union, deduped.** The draw pool is the owner's deck plus discard; a cross-zone duplicate yields a single key.
3. **Non-hero cards omitted.** Cards with no `G.cardStats` entry (e.g. Wounds) are omitted; the client defaults them to 0 recruit / 0 attack.
4. **No `G` aliasing.** The projection copies the three fields (`{recruit, attack, cost}`), not the `CardStatEntry`; the filter deep-copies per audience.
5. **Owner-only.** The stat values are public card data, but the map keys reveal the owner's pool composition (already redacted via `deckComposition` / `discardCards`); owner-only mirrors `deckComposition`.
6. **Projection-only.** Never a `G` field, no state-hash surface; `finalStateHash` + `PRE_WP080_HASH` byte-identical.

_Active 2026-08-25 — WP-608 / EC-643 (landed with the WP-608 execution). Related: D-24417 / WP-606 (the `deckComposition` projection this mirrors + extends), D-24418 (the client-side advisory Deck Probability Panel this feeds), WP-609 (the follow-on client hand-projection Monte Carlo consumer)._

### D-24420 — Deck Probability Panel: "Next hand" Projection (exact two-stage EV + stable-seeded Monte Carlo range) (Active 2026-08-26 — WP-609 / EC-644)

**Context.** WP-607 shipped the Deck Probability Panel's Phase-1 counter; WP-606/WP-608 project the owner-only draw pool (`deckComposition` + `discardCards`) and its per-card `deckCardStats`. Phase-2 turns those into a forward-looking read: what the viewer's next hand is likely to produce.

**Decision.** Add a **client-side advisory** "Next hand" section to `DeckProbabilityPanel.vue`, backed by a pure `apps/arena-client/src/components/play/handProjection.ts`. It shows the next hand's **expected recruit/attack** and a **p10/p90 range**. No engine logic crosses the boundary — the only new engine touch is two additive barrel re-exports (`HAND_SIZE` const, `UIDeckCardStat` type) on the Runtime-Safe Engine Surface (WP-090).

**Corollaries.**
1. **Exact two-stage EV, not a single combined pool.** The engine draws the deck top first and only reshuffles the discard into a fresh deck on exhaustion (`drawCards.logic`), so the mean is `fromDeck·meanDeck + fromDiscard·meanDiscard` with `fromDeck = min(HAND_SIZE, |deck|)`, `fromDiscard = min(HAND_SIZE − fromDeck, |discard|)`. A single-pool draw runs materially low on a short deck (deck=[10,10]/discard=5×0 projects **20**, not ~17.1) — a runtime test pins it.
2. **Only the range samples; the EV is closed-form.** The p10/p90 band is an **injectable-rng Monte Carlo** mirroring the two stages (sampling without replacement); the expected value is computed exactly, never as the sampled mean.
3. **Stable display seed — no jitter.** The component seeds `createSpeculativePrng` from a **deterministic** function of the current pool (`seedFromPool`), so the range does not re-roll between recomputes of the same state, yet shifts as the pool changes. Tests inject their own seed and assert presence + EV + range ORDERING, never exact percentiles.
4. **`HAND_SIZE` via the barrel — never a hardcoded 6.** The client imports the engine SSOT const (the engine forbids re-encoding the hand size).
5. **Self-hide, never throw.** The section renders only for the `handCards`-redaction-marker viewer when the stats map is present and the pool is non-empty; a missing `deckCardStats` key defaults that card to 0/0.
6. **Client-side advisory.** No `ctx.random`, no `boardgame.io`/engine-LOGIC runtime import, no game-state write — the projection is a read-only aid over already-projected fields.

_Active 2026-08-26 — WP-609 / EC-644. Related: D-24417 / WP-606 (`deckComposition` + `discardCards`), D-24419 / WP-608 (`deckCardStats`, the stats this consumes), D-24418 / WP-607 (the Phase-1 panel this extends), D-24026 (user-visible-surface live-verify)._

### D-24421 — Bottom-Left Play-Surface Overlay Stack (32px stride; the Deck Probability Panel takes the 72px slot) (Active 2026-08-26 — WP-610 / EC-645)

**Context.** Operator-reported: the collapsed "Deck odds" toggle was invisible in a live match — it rendered behind the "Download diagnostics" and "View loadout in Registry Viewer" buttons. WP-607 had pinned `DeckProbabilityPanel.vue` to `bottom: 8px; left: 8px; z-index: 9997` — the **same** corner slot as `DiagnosticExportButton` (`bottom: 8px`, `z-index: 9999`) but a **lower** z-index, so both utility buttons painted over it.

**Decision.** The bottom-left corner is a **vertical stack of fixed play-surface overlays on a shared 32px stride**: `DiagnosticExportButton` at `bottom: 8px`, `ViewLoadoutButton` at `bottom: 40px`, and now `DeckProbabilityPanel` at `bottom: 72px`. Moving the panel to the next free slot clears both buttons (collapsed and expanded — it grows upward into open space); no z-index change is needed once it no longer shares a slot.

**Corollaries.**
1. **Next slot = 104px.** Any future bottom-left fixed overlay takes the next 32px slot (104px), not an occupied one; do not re-pin an existing overlay's slot.
2. **Client CSS only.** One scoped-CSS property (`bottom: 8px` → `72px`); no engine / `G` / `ctx` / projection / hash surface, no logic, no z-index change.
3. **Layout not jsdom-observable.** `@vue/test-utils` (jsdom) does not lay out `position: fixed`, so no committed test asserts the offset; correctness was verified by a **live dev-server bounding-box measurement** (toggle box 72–101px; `panelOverlapsDiag: false` collapsed and expanded).

_Active 2026-08-26 — WP-610 / EC-645. Related: D-24418 / WP-607 (the panel this repositions), D-24026 (user-visible-surface live-verify)._

### D-24422 — Deck Probability Panel Hides at Game-Over (a live-play aid) (Active 2026-08-26 — WP-611 / EC-646)

**Context.** Follow-on to WP-610: with the panel finally visible, it also lingered on the **victory / game-over screen**, where expanding "Deck odds" showed only the villain-deck rows (the viewer's draw pool is empty; the Next-hand section already self-hid).

**Decision.** The Deck Probability Panel is a **live-play aid** and hides entirely once the match is over. The match-over signal is `UIState.gameOver` being present — the same test `EndgameActions.vue` uses to show its post-match controls. An `isMatchOver` computed guards the panel's `hasData`, so the whole panel adds no DOM at game-over; mid-match rendering is unchanged.

**Corollaries.**
1. **No new state or heuristic.** `gameOver` is already projected and barrel-exported (`UIGameOverState`); the guard is a client-only read.
2. **The endgame report card owns that surface.** There is no next hand or draw to advise once the match ends, so the panel adds only clutter there.
3. **jsdom-observable.** Unlike the WP-610 layout fix, this is testable in `@vue/test-utils`: a would-render snapshot + `gameOver` present → the panel root is absent (a committed test pins it).

_Active 2026-08-26 — WP-611 / EC-646. Related: D-24418 / WP-607 (the panel), D-24421 / WP-610 (the placement fix that surfaced the lingering), D-24026 (user-visible-surface live-verify)._

### D-24423 — Danger Meter names the scheme's counted card type (escaped-bystander) (Active 2026-08-26 — WP-612 / EC-647)

**Context.** Operator-reported: a Midtown Bank Robbery danger meter read **"Escaped 5/8"** beside the HUD's raw **"Escaped: 7"**. The `5/8` is the scheme's `escaped-pile-count` loss with `cardType: 'bystander'` — 5 **bystanders** carried into the escaped pile — while the `7` is villains + henchmen that fled. `resolveSchemeLossKind` collapsed every `escaped-pile-count` scheme to `SchemeLossKind: 'escaped-pile'`, discarding the `cardType`; the client mapped that to the noun **"Escaped"**, mislabeling the bystander case and colliding with the raw escaped-villain count.

**Decision.** The DangerMeter must name the quantity the scheme actually counts. Split the escaped-pile kind by counted card type — mirroring the existing `pile-depleted → hero-deck | wound-stack` split by pile: `cardType: 'bystander'` → a new `SchemeLossKind` **`escaped-bystander`** (client noun "Bystanders"); every other cardType (villain — Negative Zone, 12) stays `escaped-pile` ("Escaped"). The engine keeps **no display copy** (D-24367 §2); the client's `SCHEME_LOSS_NOUNS` owns the noun.

**Corollaries.**
1. **Projection-only.** `resolveSchemeLossKind` is a projection; the endgame loss uses `countEscapedPileByType` directly, so the split has no `G` / `ctx` / hash surface — both oracles stay byte-identical.
2. **Drift-pinned.** `escaped-bystander` is added to both the `SchemeLossKind` union and the `SCHEME_LOSS_KINDS` canonical array; the runtime `deepStrictEqual` pin and the client's exhaustive `Record<SchemeLossKind, string>` (vue-tsc) both enforce the pair.
3. **Degrades safely.** Any future non-bystander `escaped-pile-count` cardType reads "Escaped", which is correct for villains/henchmen fleeing.
4. **Distinct from the raw count.** The `EscapedPile` / HUD "Escaped: N" (raw villains fled) is unchanged; only the danger-meter track's label is corrected.

_Active 2026-08-26 — WP-612 / EC-647. Related: D-24366 / WP-557 (the menace/danger-meter contract), D-24371 §3 / WP-562 (the `SchemeLossKind` client noun mapping), D-24367 §2 (engine keeps no display copy), D-24026 (user-visible-surface live-verify)._

### D-24424 — Solo Mastery Badge Lane (playerCount-gated Tier-1 gameplay badges) (Active 2026-08-26 — WP-613 / EC-648)

**Context.** The WP-105 / D-1004 Tier-1 gameplay badges are player-count-agnostic, so a player who beats a scenario **solo** — alone against the whole mastermind, strictly harder — earns the same badges as a full table. The `wiki/awards-and-badges.md` design page names the gap: *"solo gets its own category, not nothing."*

**Decision.** Add a **Solo Mastery lane** to Tier-1 (extends D-1004) — two `playerCount`-gated badges, mirroring the shipped `sub-par-run` (per-run) + `multiverse-mastery` (breadth) pair:
- `gameplay.solo.lone-defender` (per-run, `competitive_score`): `playerCount === 1 && finalScore < 0`.
- `gameplay.solo.solitaire-master` (breadth, `competitive_history`): ≥ 5 distinct `scenario_key` with `final_score < 0 AND player_count = 1`.

`playerCount` (on the competitive record, D-24134) is threaded through `issueTier1BadgesForSubmission` → `evaluatePerRunBadges`; the breadth badge adds a `COUNT(DISTINCT scenario_key) … WHERE player_count = 1` query.

**Corollaries.**
1. **D-1004-compliant.** Quality-gated (`lone-defender`) + breadth-gated (`solitaire-master`, distinct scenarios) — never a volume count (§25 / D-0005). Cooperative-model-safe framing (solo = alone vs the mastermind, §23b). Per-player projection over the immutable `competitive_scores` row; append-only via the existing INSERT + `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` — no new table, no `/badges/*` route, no Tier 2/3, no state-hash surface.
2. **`null` player_count is NOT solo.** An unknown count never earns a solo badge (the per-run predicate returns false; the history query filters `player_count = 1`).
3. **Additive, not exclusive.** `lone-defender` co-fires with the general `sub-par-run` for a solo player — the solo lane is additional recognition, not a replacement.
4. **Cooperative / shared-table / retroactive badges remain DEFERRED.** The design page's centerpiece needs cross-player, table-level data the per-player record does not carry (the same gap the deferred `bystander-guardian` / `steady-crew` badges hit) — a follow-on that begins with a data-plumbing WP.

_Active 2026-08-26 — WP-613 / EC-648. Related: D-1004 (the Tier-1 badge system + tiered issuer model), D-0005 (§25 anti-volume), D-24134 (`playerCount` on the competitive record), D-24026 (user-visible-surface live-verify)._

### D-24425 — Shared Cooperative Badge (whole-table, grouped by `replay_hash`) (Active 2026-08-26 — WP-614 / EC-649)

**Context.** The `wiki/awards-and-badges.md` design's centerpiece is the **shared / table badge** — *"awarded to the whole table, not a person… nobody can farm it alone."* WP-613 left it deferred as needing cross-player data. It doesn't need a new column: competitive submission is by `matchId` (WP-338), so the server derives `replay_hash` from the **shared** replay artifact — every co-op player of one match has the **same** `replay_hash` (`UNIQUE (player_id, replay_hash)`), and grouping `competitive_scores` on it is exactly that match's player set.

**Decision.** Add the first shared cooperative badge (extends D-1004 / D-24424): `gameplay.shared.united-front` (`sourceKind 'competitive_history'`, `source_ref NULL`), awarded to **every** player of a match when the `replay_hash` group is **complete** (`rows.length === playerCount`), `playerCount ≥ 2`, and **every** player finished sub-PAR (`final_score < 0`). Issued by a new `issueSharedMatchBadges(replayHash, playerCount, configVersion, database)` called fire-and-forget from the competition submission hook.

**Corollaries.**
1. **Last-submitter-awards-all.** The group is evaluated on every submission; earlier submitters see an incomplete group and no-op. Only the submission that completes the group awards the whole table, via one multi-row INSERT + `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` — idempotent across the table's submitters.
2. **No migration.** Reuses the migration-013 `source_kind` value `'competitive_history'` (the badge is a group projection, not a single score) — no schema change, no new `source_kind`, no new table, no `/badges/*` route.
3. **Shared / ungameable.** `playerCount ≥ 2` and every player sub-PAR — no single strong run earns it; a solo / `null`-count match short-circuits before the group query.
4. **D-1004-compliant.** Quality-gated (never volume, §25 / D-0005), cooperative-model-safe framing (§23b), projection over immutable `competitive_scores` rows (D-5302) — no `G` / hash surface — append-only.
5. **Still deferred.** The design's "player A **enabled** player B's finish" flavor needs turn-level contribution attribution scoring does not capture (an engine-projection effort); tiered team badges (5/4/3/2-player) wait until this single shared badge validates the grouping model.

_Active 2026-08-26 — WP-614 / EC-649. Related: D-1004 (Tier-1 issuer model), D-24424 (the solo lane this sits beside), D-24134 (`playerCount`), WP-338 (submit-by-`matchId` → server-derived `replay_hash`), D-5302 (immutable competitive rows), D-24026 (user-visible-surface live-verify)._
